paras.zh: 穆拉尼曾于 2008 年至 2012 年担任 SNL 编剧。尽管他从来都不是演员，但自从离开后，他多次重返该剧，客串了很多次，并主持了七次。

paras.en: The comedian was joined by Phoebe Bridgers as musical guest, marking her second solo appearance (she’s also been on SNL as part of the musical group Boygenius).
paras.zh: 菲比·布里杰斯 (Phoebe Bridgers) 作为音乐嘉宾加入了这位喜剧演员，这是她第二次单独亮相（她还作为 Boygenius 音乐团体的成员出现在《周六夜现场》中）。

paras.en: So far on season 52, Jalen Brunson, Dakota Johnson, Shane Gillis, Inde Navarrette and Druski have each hosted.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，第 52 季的主持人包括 Jalen Brunson、Dakota Johnson、Shane Gillis、Inde Navarrette 和 Druski。

articles.title: Listen to the River! ‘Arrow for a Stone Heart’ Is a Poetic Experience Told Through an Indigenous Lens
articles.author: Georg Szalai

paras.en: A pig-like creature is walking around in the territory of the indigenous Guaraní on the outskirts of São Paulo, Brazil. “My name is Rete, I am a peccary,” it tells us. And it shares what started happening to nature back in the days when the colonizers began to settle. “One day, those who are many started arriving.” Over time, the stones they brought started swallowing up more and more space, restricting an ancient river, plants and many creatures.
paras.zh: 一种像猪一样的生物正在巴西圣保罗郊区瓜拉尼原住民的领地上行走。 “我的名字是雷特，我是一只西貒，”它告诉我们。它分享了殖民者开始定居的日子里自然开始发生的事情。 “有一天，许多人开始抵达。”随着时间的推移，他们带来的石头开始吞噬越来越多的空间，限制了一条古老的河流、植物和许多生物。

paras.en: Also in the indigenous territory, a woman named Jera Rete dreams. In her nightmares, the city invades her village. But there is also an old woman who keeps talking to her. And even the river has a voice – if you are only willing to listen.
paras.zh: 同样在原住民领地里，一位名叫杰拉·雷特 (Jera Rete) 的女人在做梦。在她的噩梦中，这座城市入侵了她的村庄。但还有一位老妇人一直在和她说话。即使河流也有声音——只要你愿意倾听。

paras.en: In her poetic debut feature, Arrow for a Stone Heart (Flecha para Um Coração de Pedra), writer, director and cinematographer Luiza Calagian, in collaboration with the local Guaraní indigenous community, transport us into the heart of the forest near the city. And the documentary-fiction hybrid’s narrative is very different for a reason. The way the indigenous people experience and narrate reality is different. From their perspective, myths, dreams, and relationships with non-humans connect different temporalities and perspectives.
paras.zh: 作家、导演兼电影摄影师路易莎·卡拉吉安 (Luiza Calagian) 与当地瓜拉尼土著社区合作，在她富有诗意的处女作《石心之箭》(Flecha para Um Coração de Pedra) 中，将我们带入城市附近的森林中心。纪录片与小说的混合体的叙事方式非常不同，这是有原因的。原住民体验和叙述现实的方式是不同的。从他们的角度来看，神话、梦境以及与非人类的关系连接着不同的时间性和视角。

paras.en: The cinematic, maybe even hallucinatory, journey that the movie takes us on elucidates the history of the community’s struggle. Cinema emerges as an opportunity for understanding and, possibly, change.
paras.zh: 电影带我们经历的电影般的、甚至可能是幻觉的旅程阐明了社区斗争的历史。电影成为理解甚至改变的机会。

paras.en: Arrow for a Stone Heart celebrates its world premiere on Tuesday, Nov. 17, in the Rebels with a Cause Competition of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia.
paras.zh: 《石心之箭》于 11 月 17 日星期二在爱沙尼亚第 30 届塔林黑夜电影节 (PÖFF) 的反叛者竞赛竞赛中庆祝其全球首映。

paras.en: Calagian co-wrote the film with Jera Rete. Calagian also handled cinematography and shared the editing duties with Caio De. The producers are Vinicius Toro and Sabrina Zimmermann, with Bruno Cucio serving as executive producer. Utopia Docs is handling distribution and world sales.
paras.zh: 卡拉吉安与杰拉·雷特共同编剧了这部电影。卡拉吉安还负责摄影，并与凯奥·德共同承担剪辑职责。制片人为维尼修斯·托罗和萨布丽娜·齐默尔曼，布鲁诺·库西奥担任执行制片人。 Utopia Docs 负责分销和全球销售。

paras.en: Ahead of the world premiere, Calagian told THR about how the idea for Arrow for a Stone Heart came about and its unique voice, look and feel.
paras.zh: 在全球首映之前，卡拉吉安向《好莱坞报道》讲述了《石心之箭》的想法是如何产生的，以及它独特的声音、外观和感觉。

paras.en: “I kind of grew up with this film. It’s been seven years now,” the creative explains. “The film began to transform as well, and at a certain point, I understood that it wouldn’t make sense for me to try to tell the story, which is the story of the Guaraní. It had to be told from their point of view and from their perspective rather than one that comes from the West.”
paras.zh: “我是伴随着这部电影长大的。现在已经七年了，”这位创意人士解释道。 “这部电影也开始发生转变，在某个时刻，我明白尝试讲述这个故事对我来说是没有意义的，这是瓜拉尼人的故事。它必须从他们的角度和他们的角度来讲述，而不是来自西方的故事。”

paras.en: So, how do you do that in a comprehensive way? “The mission became how do we bring the Guaraní cosmology, the Guaraní philosophy, the way that they see, organize, narrate and symbolize reality into the structure of a film, which is by its nature a Western thing,” Calagian tells THR. “But this also opened up the possibilities of transformation that this art has.”
paras.zh: 那么，如何全面地做到这一点呢？ “我们的任务是如何将瓜拉尼人的宇宙论、瓜拉尼人的哲学以及他们看待、组织、叙述和象征现实的方式融入到电影的结构中，而电影本质上是西方的东西，”卡拉吉安告诉《好莱坞报道》。 “但这也开启了这种艺术转型的可能性。”

paras.en: The first thing she started looking at was dreams. “The Guaraní are very, very, very connected to their dreams,” she explains. “They don’t understand dreams just as something that your mind creates or something that your imagination creates, but the dream for them is a form of connecting to other dimensions, other beings, other spirits, to people who are not here anymore, and to gods.”
paras.zh: 她开始关注的第一件事就是梦想。 “瓜拉尼人与他们的梦想息息相关，”她解释道。 “他们并不把梦理解为你的思想创造的东西或你的想象力创造的东西，但对他们来说，梦是一种与其他维度、其他存在、其他精神、与不再存在的人以及神联系的形式。”

paras.en: In the process, Jera became a close friend. “She embraced the project to the point that she became a co-writer,” Calagian shares with THR. “She also started organizing who was going to be in the film. The main characters other than her are her two daughters. One of the girls, her youngest, plays the river, and the older daughter, who also appears briefly at the end of the film, voiced Rete, the peccary. So everything kind of revolves around Jera. She is the leader of this village, and she became not only the co-writer but also the whole heart of the film.”
paras.zh: 在此过程中，杰拉成为了亲密的朋友。 “她非常喜欢这个项目，甚至成为了联合编剧，”卡拉吉安告诉《好莱坞报道》。 “她还开始安排谁将出现在电影中。除了她之外的主要角色是她的两个女儿。其中一个女孩，她最小的女儿，扮演河流，而大女儿也在电影结尾短暂出现，为野猪瑞特配音。所以一切都围绕着杰拉展开。她是这个村庄的领导者，她不仅成为了联合编剧，而且成为了电影的整个核心。”

paras.en: The filmmaker also fell in love with Rete, the peccary. And the peccary became the symbol of her production company, Mata Fechada Filmes. “For me, it is a symbol,” Calagian says. “It has a lot to do with the magic of cinema. The Guaraní say it has the capacity of moving and traveling between worlds and entering different dimensions, different perspectives and visiting the gods.”
paras.zh: 电影制片人还爱上了野猪雷特。西貒成了她的制作公司 Mata Fechada Filmes 的标志。 “对我来说，这是一个象征，”卡拉吉安说。 “这与电影的魔力有很大关系。瓜拉尼人说电影有能力在世界之间移动和旅行，进入不同的维度、不同的视角并拜访众神。”

paras.en: Humans destroying the natural balance and colonization are recurring themes of Arrow for a Stone Heart. The river, for example, is considered one of the wisest and most powerful spirits for the Guaraní. “Even before colonization, when everything was more in harmony, the Guaraní were very careful and very respectful of those river spirits because they can be dangerous – they are not to be messed with,” the filmmaker highlights. “That’s why I wanted to include this character, the river, to tell her side of the story. Despite all of this destruction, there is still life in the river, which is amazing. Somehow, nature finds a way to survive, even in such adverse conditions. She represents an anthropomorphic presence.”
paras.zh: 人类破坏自然平衡和殖民化是《石心之箭》中反复出现的主题。例如，河流被认为是瓜拉尼人最智慧、最强大的精神之一。 “即使在殖民化之前，当一切都更加和谐时，瓜拉尼人就非常小心，非常尊重这些河神，因为它们可能很危险——它们是不容惹恼的，”电影制片人强调道。 “这就是为什么我想把河流这个角色加入进来，讲述她的故事。尽管遭到了所有这些破坏，河里仍然有生命，这真是太神奇了。不知何故，即使在如此不利的条件下，大自然也找到了生存之道。她代表了一种拟人化的存在。”

paras.en: Even words and language were chosen with care to properly represent the indigenous people’s view of the world. “Those who are many” is one of the recurring phrases, for example. “That is the common way they call the people who invaded,” Calagian tells THR.
paras.zh: 甚至词语和语言都经过精心选择，以正确代表土著人民的世界观。例如，“人多”就是反复出现的短语之一。 “这是他们称呼入侵者的常见方式，”卡拉吉安告诉《好莱坞报道》。

paras.en: She has actually worked with the Guaraní for more than 10 years now, having in the past also focused on communications efforts to make their voice heard. “We were working on a campaign to make the government recognize the indigenous lands that they had inside the city, one of the biggest metropolises in the world,” the filmmaker notes. “There is a big historical dispute around the history of colonization, especially in São Paulo. There is a regional culture that celebrates the colonizers who were responsible for invading this territory, which has always been Guaraní territory.”
paras.zh: 事实上，她已经与瓜拉尼人合作了十多年，过去还致力于沟通工作，让他们的声音被听到。 “我们正在开展一项运动，让政府承认他们在世界上最大的大都市之一的城市内拥有的土著土地，”电影制片人指出。 “围绕殖民历史存在着很大的历史争议，尤其是在圣保罗。有一种地区文化颂扬那些入侵这片领土的殖民者，而这片领土一直是瓜拉尼人的领土。”

paras.en: That’s also where the film title, Arrow for a Stone Heart, comes from. It is not only a play on the phrase “heart of stone” for cruel or cold-hearted people but also a reference to the statues and other reminders and colonialism. “There are still a lot of historical monuments, a lot of street names, a lot of public political symbols that celebrate the colonizers, the people who killed and enslaved the indigenous people,” highlights Calagian. “We understood how important this dispute between narratives was, and that’s how this project was born.”
paras.zh: 这也是电影片名《石心之箭》的由来。它不仅是对残酷或冷酷的人的“铁石心肠”一词的玩笑，而且还提到了雕像和其他提醒以及殖民主义。卡拉吉安强调说：“仍然有很多历史古迹、很多街道名称、很多庆祝殖民者、杀害和奴役土著人民的公共政治符号。” “我们了解叙事之间的争论有多么重要，这就是这个项目的诞生。”

paras.en: Watch the trailer for Arrow for a Stone Heart here.
paras.zh: 在这里观看《石心之箭》的预告片。

articles.title: $180 million Van Gogh tests the art market and collector confidence

paras.en: The art auctions in New York next week could top $2 billion, as a treasure trove of masterpieces comes to the market for the first time in decades.
paras.zh: 下周在纽约举行的艺术品拍卖可能会突破 20 亿美元，数十年来首次出现一批杰作宝库。

paras.en: Total sales at Sotheby's, Christie's and Phillips are expected to be around $2.4 billion, which would equal last year's total, according to ArtTactic. Sotheby's alone is expected to pull in over $1.1 billion, with a single collection from The Blaquier-Arrieta Collection estimated at $450 million.
paras.zh: 据 ArtTactic 称，苏富比、佳士得和富艺斯的总销售额预计约为 24 亿美元，相当于去年的总销售额。仅苏富比拍卖行就预计收入超过 11 亿美元，其中 Blaquier-Arrieta 收藏的单件藏品估计价值 4.5 亿美元。

paras.en: The collection includes the two big headliners of the week: Vincent van Gogh's landscape "Châtaigniers en fleurs," (Chestnut Trees in Flower) estimated at $180 million and Paul Cézanne's "Arlequin," estimated at $120 million. Neither has been seen in public for a half a century.
paras.zh: 该藏品包括本周的两大头条作品：文森特·梵高的风景画《Châtaigniers en fleurs》（花中栗树）估价 1.8 亿美元，以及保罗·塞尚的《Arlequin》估价 1.2 亿美元。半个世纪以来，两人都没有在公开场合露面。

paras.en: Sotheby's CEO Charles Stewart said demand is strong in the art market, especially for the highest quality blue-chip works, as rising stocks markets and private wealth boost the confidence of collectors.
paras.zh: 苏富比首席执行官查尔斯·斯图尔特 (Charles Stewart) 表示，随着股市上涨和私人财富提振收藏家的信心，艺术品市场需求强劲，尤其是对最高品质的蓝筹作品。

paras.en: "There's been enormous wealth creation and a lot of confidence in markets," Stewart said. "It's a global phenomenon. We're seeing recovery and greater interest across Asia and something really exciting happening from the Middle East across to Singapore and Europe and the U.S."
paras.zh: “巨大的财富创造和市场信心增强，”斯图尔特说。 “这是一个全球现象。我们看到整个亚洲的复苏和更大的兴趣，从中东到新加坡、欧洲和美国，正在发生一些真正令人兴奋的事情。”

paras.en: Christie's star of the week is Wassily Kandinsky's "Betonte Ecken," estimated at $60 million to $80 million. Christie's CEO Bonnie Brennan describes the market is "confident but discerning, rewarding truly exceptional works." She said recent gyrations in the stock market and fears of an AI bubble aren't likely to deter serious collectors.
paras.zh: 本周佳士得的明星作品是瓦西里·康定斯基 (Wassily Kandinsky) 的《Betonte Ecken》，估价为 6,000 万至 8,000 万美元。佳士得首席执行官邦妮·布伦南 (Bonnie Brennan) 形容市场“充满信心，但眼光独到，奖励真正杰出的作品”。她表示，最近股市的波动和对人工智能泡沫的担忧不太可能阻止严肃的收藏家。

paras.en: "At the very highest end of our market, collectors tend to take a much longer-term view," Brennan said. "They understand that the opportunity to acquire a masterpiece may come only once in a generation, and that can be far more important than what the stock market has done in any particular week. In uncertain moments, the very best can actually become even more compelling."
paras.zh: “在我们市场的最高端，收藏家往往会采取更长远的眼光，”布伦南说。 “他们明白，获得杰作的机会可能一代人只有一次，这可能比股市在任何特定一周的表现都要重要得多。在不确定的时刻，最好的作品实际上会变得更加引人注目。”

paras.en: The art market has continued to rebound this year after declines in 2023 and 2024, with auction sales in the first half up 70% over last year, to $6.8 billion, according to Bank of America.
paras.zh: 根据美国银行的数据，艺术品市场在经历了 2023 年和 2024 年的下滑后，今年继续反弹，上半年拍卖销售额比去年增长 70%，达到 68 亿美元。

paras.en: Drew Watson, head of art services at Bank of America, said blue-chip art is outperforming, with Impressionist & Modern sales up 133% in the first half.
paras.zh: 美国银行艺术服务主管德鲁·沃森表示，蓝筹艺术表现出色，上半年印象派和现代艺术销售额增长了 133%。

paras.en: "Our outlook for the art market this November is cautiously optimistic," Watson said. "Improving liquidity, combined with an unusually strong concentration of fresh-to-market private collections, creates a favorable backdrop for the marquee sales."
paras.zh: “我们对今年 11 月艺术市场的前景持谨慎乐观的态度，”沃森说道。 “流动性的改善，加上新上市的私人收藏异常集中，为大型拍卖创造了有利的背景。”

articles.title: SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first

paras.en: After a booster explosion on Friday, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage, or spacecraft, portion of its massive Starship rocket from orbit on Saturday — a triumphant milestone for the company.
paras.zh: 周五助推器爆炸后，SpaceX 于周六成功从轨道上捕获了其大型 Starship 火箭的上级或航天器部分，这是该公司的一个胜利里程碑。

paras.en: SpaceX made the historic catch using its "chopsticks," mechanical arms attached to a launch tower, at its facility in Starbase, Texas.
paras.zh: SpaceX 在其位于德克萨斯州 Starbase 的工厂中，利用其“筷子”（连接在发射塔上的机械臂）实现了这一历史性的成功。

paras.en: Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship test yet, marked the first time Elon Musk's company attempted to catch both the rocket's booster and upper stage.
paras.zh: 15 号试飞是迄今为止最雄心勃勃的星舰测试，标志着埃隆·马斯克的公司首次尝试同时捕获火箭的助推器和上级。

paras.en: Musk posted a video on X inspecting the upper stage craft after completing the capture.
paras.zh: 马斯克在完成捕获后在 X 上发布了一段视频，检查了上层飞船。

paras.en: During the first phase of the test flight on Friday, SpaceX failed to catch and recover the booster, instead diverting it to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico where it exploded before hitting the water.
paras.zh: 在周五试飞的第一阶段中，SpaceX 未能捕获并回收助推器，而是将其转移到墨西哥湾的近海溅落处，助推器在落入水面之前爆炸。

paras.en: The rocket's upper stage then continued into orbit and flew around the Earth 14 times before successfully landing on SpaceX's launch tower, nicknamed Mechazilla.
paras.zh: 火箭的上级随后继续进入轨道并绕地球飞行 14 圈，然后成功降落在 SpaceX 绰号为 Mechazilla 的发射塔上。

paras.en: The Hawaii Department of Transportation issued a temporary pause on some West Coast flights Friday, due to debris risk from the flight. Separately, the FAA issued a rare, nationwide ground stop due to telecommunications system failures. (Both of those orders have since been lifted.)
paras.zh: 由于航班存在碎片风险，夏威夷交通部周五暂停部分西海岸航班。另外，由于电信系统故障，美国联邦航空局罕见地在全国范围内进行了地面停止。 （这两项命令现已被取消。）

paras.en: Making Starship a reliable and fully reusable rocket is critical to SpaceX's ambitions. In the near term, the company needs Starship to send more satellites into orbit to expand its Starlink satellite internet service, which is currently the company's profit center.
paras.zh: 让 Starship 成为可靠且完全可重复使用的火箭对于 SpaceX 的雄心壮志至关重要。短期内，该公司需要Starship将更多卫星送入轨道，以扩大其Starlink卫星互联网服务，目前该服务是该公司的利润中心。

paras.en: SpaceX is also expected to use Starship to bring astronauts and cargo from lunar orbit to the Moon's surface and back for NASA. Musk also has a grand vision to use Starship to "colonize Mars" and "make humanity multi-planetary."
paras.zh: SpaceX 预计还将利用 Starship 将宇航员和货物从月球轨道运送到月球表面，然后返回 NASA。马斯克还有一个宏伟的愿景，就是利用星际飞船“殖民火星”、“让人类走向多行星”。

paras.en: During Test Flight 15 on Friday, SpaceX released another 26 of its newest Starlink v3 satellites into orbit, growing its commercial satellite internet network.
paras.zh: 在周五的第 15 次试飞期间，SpaceX 将另外 26 颗最新的 Starlink v3 卫星送入轨道，扩大其商业卫星互联网网络。

paras.en: The company's constellation already included over 11,000 satellites in low Earth orbit. One Starship rocket can carry up to 60 Starlink v3 satellites, the company has said.
paras.zh: 该公司的星座已包括近地轨道上的 11,000 多颗卫星。该公司表示，一枚 Starship 火箭最多可携带 60 颗 Starlink v3 卫星。

articles.title: Could Budapest be the next digital nomad hotspot?

paras.en: When mechanical engineering graduate and entrepreneur Lexi Vindisch wanted to run her business from a remote location, she didn't pick a town in North America where she lived. Instead, Budapest was top of her list.
paras.zh: 当机械工程专业毕业生兼企业家 Lexi Vindisch 想在偏远地区经营自己的生意时，她没有选择自己居住的北美城镇。相反，布达佩斯是她的首选。

paras.en: With its mix of grand sights, cafés, cultural events and inexpensive public transportation, the Hungarian capital has become a popular place for digital nomads — people embracing the "work from anywhere" trend that took off during the Covid-19 pandemic.
paras.zh: 凭借其宏伟的景点、咖啡馆、文化活动和廉价的公共交通，匈牙利首都已成为数字游牧者的热门之地——人们拥抱在 Covid-19 大流行期间兴起的“随时随地工作”趋势。

paras.en: Based at co-working space Create26 in Budapest, Vindisch runs a domestic cleaning company based in Victoria, Canada, as well as overseeing Lead Machine, a marketing software firm for home service businesses.
paras.zh: Vindisch 的总部位于布达佩斯的 Create26 联合办公空间，经营着一家位于加拿大维多利亚的家庭清洁公司，并负责监管一家面向家庭服务企业的营销软件公司 Lead Machine。

paras.en: Hungary ranked fifth for digital nomads on a 2025 list of countries, behind Spain, the United Arab Emirates, Montenegro and the Bahamas. The index, compiled by visa information website VisaGuide, considered factors such as taxes, income and cost of living.
paras.zh: 在 2025 年数字游牧国家名单中，匈牙利排名第五，落后于西班牙、阿拉伯联合酋长国、黑山和巴哈马。该指数由签证信息网站VisaGuide编制，考虑了税收、收入和生活成本等因素。

paras.en: Vindisch, who has worked in many European and North American cities, but has Hungarian roots, said Budapest feels different. "I've been in locales that are super beautiful, well organized, great facilities, but they lacked a personality ... I've never been able to replicate the feeling that Budapest holds anywhere else," she said.
paras.zh: 温迪施曾在许多欧洲和北美城市工作过，但有匈牙利血统，他说布达佩斯给人的感觉不同。 “我去过的地方超级美丽、组织良好、设施一流，但它们缺乏个性……我从来无法复制布达佩斯在其他地方的感觉，”她说。

paras.en: EU citizens can work remotely from Hungary long-term if they meet certain requirements, while Hungary's White Card scheme, which provides one- or two-year residency permits for digital nomads from outside the EU, requires a net monthly income of at least 3,000 euros ($3,370).
paras.zh: 如果满足某些要求，欧盟公民可以在匈牙利长期远程工作，而匈牙利的白卡计划为欧盟以外的数字游牧民提供一年或两年的居留许可，要求每月净收入至少为 3,000 欧元（3,370 美元）。

paras.en: There are around 35 co-working spots in central Budapest, according to the Coworking Hungary Association, several of which are in the bustling District VI, near the fashionable bars and restaurants of the Jewish Quarter. Alongside these hubs, the city offers around 35 serviced offices, including locations from larger providers such as Regus and DBH Flex.
paras.zh: 据匈牙利联合办公协会称，布达佩斯市中心约有 35 个联合办公地点，其中几个位于繁华的第六区，靠近犹太区的时尚酒吧和餐馆。除了这些中心之外，该市还拥有约 35 个服务式办公室，其中包括 Regus 和 DBH Flex 等大型供应商的办公地点。

paras.en: "Budapest has its own vibe," said Áron Levendel, a founder of co-working space Kaptar, which is within view of the city's striking St Stephen's Basilica. "Whoever wants to connect, make friends or meet people, has an easy job. Whoever wants to have fun, learn or get experiences in English, will have the challenge of choosing from hundreds of options every evening," he said.
paras.zh: “布达佩斯有自己的氛围，”联合办公空间 Kaptar 的创始人 Áron Levendel 说，该空间位于该市引人注目的圣史蒂芬大教堂的视野之内。 “无论谁想与人交往、交朋友或结识新朋友，工作都是轻松的。无论谁想用英语享受乐趣、学习或获得经验，每天晚上都会面临从数百个选项中进行选择的挑战，”他说。

paras.en: Levendel and his co-founders are organizational developers who wanted a workplace that was both sociable and professional. In 2010, they came up with the idea for Kaptar (the word means "hive" in Hungarian).
paras.zh: Levendel 和他的联合创始人都是组织开发者，他们想要一个既社交又专业的工作场所。 2010 年，他们提出了 Kaptar（该词在匈牙利语中的意思是“蜂巢”）的想法。

paras.en: "Gmail was already there, but most of the work was not in the cloud or online yet; people had folders and papers. Digital nomads were not a thing," Levendel told CNBC by email. "Co-working" also wasn't a term in common use at the time, so he called the space a "közösségi iroda," or community office.
paras.zh: “Gmail 已经存在，但大部分工作还没有在云端或在线进行；人们有文件夹和文件。数字游牧民还不是一个东西，”莱文德尔通过电子邮件告诉 CNBC。 “联合办公”在当时也不是常用的术语，因此他将这个空间称为“közösségi iroda”，即社区办公室。

paras.en: Since the Covid-19 pandemic, Kaptar has grown more than 30% every year, according to Levendel, including a "wave" of digital nomads who joined after the pandemic, often arriving initially for a month but staying for up to a year. Overseas members either keep an existing job and work remotely, or they are freelancers who can travel, Levendel said.
paras.zh: Levendel 表示，自 Covid-19 大流行以来，Kaptar 每年增长超过 30%，其中包括大流行后加入的“数字游民浪潮”，他们通常最初抵达一个月，但停留长达一年。莱文德尔说，海外成员要么保留现有工作并远程工作，要么是可以出差的自由职业者。

paras.en: Mónika Gyurity opened co-working space Liftoff in 2019. After a career as a television executive, she wanted to expand her digital skills and bring different generations together to learn from each other.
paras.zh: Mónika Gyurity 于 2019 年开设了联合办公空间 Liftoff。在担任电视高管之后，她希望扩展自己的数字技能，并让不同代人聚集在一起互相学习。

paras.en: Located in a former elevator factory close to Budapest's central Nyugati station, Liftoff attracts a mix of professionals — including short-term visitors in need of a workspace, as well as remote employees working for international companies. One of Liftoff's team members is also a remote worker who regularly participates in Nomad Cruise voyages, or "workation" trips that combine a conference program with land excursions.
paras.zh: Liftoff 位于布达佩斯中央 Nyugati 车站附近的一家前电梯工厂内，吸引了各种专业人士，包括需要工作空间的短期访客，以及为国际公司工作的远程员工。 Liftoff 的团队成员之一也是一名远程工作者，他定期参加 Nomad Cruise 航行，或将会议计划与陆地游览相结合的“工作”旅行。

paras.en: Gyurity expects the digital nomad trend to continue, noting that AI now allows individuals to create and launch services or businesses without the resources of a large organization. "More people will be able to imagine their knowledge, skills and opportunities outside the traditional corporate world," she said.
paras.zh: Gyurity 预计数字游牧趋势将继续下去，并指出人工智能现在允许个人在没有大型组织资源的情况下创建和启动服务或业务。 “更多的人将能够想象他们在传统企业界之外的知识、技能和机会，”她说。

paras.en: At the same time, she recommends that those in the corporate world spend time in a co-working environment. "Most people are there because they are trying to solve something," she said. "Every day I meet younger people who are at a very different stage of their lives and careers, use different tools, and approach problems differently. We can learn from each other."
paras.zh: 与此同时，她建议企业界人士在联合办公环境中度过时光。 “大多数人来这里是因为他们想解决一些问题，”她说。 “我每天都会遇到年轻人，他们处于生活和职业的不同阶段，使用不同的工具，以不同的方式处理问题。我们可以互相学习。”

paras.en: A few streets north of the Hungarian Parliament building and steps from the River Danube sits Kubik, a co-working space where roughly 20% of members are digital nomads working in IT, software development, design or marketing. According to co-owner Éva Mocsár, many of these professionals split their time between Budapest and warmer climes, with some choosing to escape the Hungarian winter in Argentina, before returning in the spring.
paras.zh: Kubik 位于匈牙利议会大厦以北的几条街道上，距离多瑙河仅几步之遥，这是一个联合办公空间，大约 20% 的成员是从事 IT、软件开发、设计或营销工作的数字游牧者。据合伙人埃娃·莫克萨尔 (Éva Mocsár) 介绍，这些专业人士中的许多人都在布达佩斯和温暖的气候之间奔波，其中一些人选择前往阿根廷躲避匈牙利的冬天，然后在春天返回。

paras.en: As with other co-working hubs, one of Mocsár's primary challenges is recruiting new members, particularly as larger office spaces compete with Kubik on price. "Co-working is closely connected to the office market, and Budapest has a huge amount of office space, a lot of it empty," she said. According to consultancy Cushman and Wakefield, 12% of the city's office stock is vacant.
paras.zh: 与其他联合办公中心一样，Mocsár 面临的主要挑战之一是招募新成员，尤其是在更大的办公空间与 Kubik 进行价格竞争的情况下。 “联合办公与办公市场密切相关，布达佩斯拥有大量办公空间，但其中很多是空置的，”她说。根据咨询公司 Cushman and Wakefield 的数据，该市 12% 的写字楼库存处于空置状态。

paras.en: At Create26, events are a core strategy for member retention. The space regularly hosts the city's Claude AI Community meetups and maintains a close partnership with the non-profit Startup Hungary, frequently featuring workshops on building and scaling with AI or navigating investor funding. "It's a full package," said Create26's general manager Seloua Benkaid Kasbah. "So, you are here not only working alone at your desk, but you also find yourself at lunchtime talking with members from big companies ... and in the evening you find yourself at an event with founders and investors," she said.
paras.zh: 在 Create26，活动是保留会员的核心策略。该空间定期举办该市的克劳德人工智能社区聚会，并与非营利性初创匈牙利公司保持密切合作伙伴关系，经常举办有关人工智能构建和扩展或引导投资者融资的研讨会。 “这是一个完整的包，”Create26 的总经理 Seloua Benkaid Kasbah 说。 “所以，你不仅独自在办公桌前工作，而且你还会发现自己在午餐时间与大公司的成员交谈……晚上，你发现自己与创始人和投资者一起参加活动，”她说。

paras.en: Mocsár said that while remote work is "here to stay," she's not convinced a life of constantly moving around is sustainable. "What I see more is that people create a few fixed points for themselves around the world. Places they come back to from time to time, where there are familiar faces, and where they feel a little bit at home. And I think co-working spaces can play a really important role in that," she said.
paras.zh: 莫萨尔表示，虽然远程工作“将继续存在”，但她并不相信不断走动的生活是可持续的。 “我更多地看到的是，人们在世界各地为自己创造了一些固定点。他们时不时会回来的地方，那里有熟悉的面孔，他们感觉有点宾至如归的地方。我认为联合办公空间可以在这方面发挥非常重要的作用，”她说。

paras.en: While Budapest is undoubtedly popular with digital nomads, it remains an emerging market for flexible office space, accounting for just 1.7% to 1.8% of the city's total office stock, according to data from Cushman and Wakefield.
paras.zh: 戴德梁行和韦克菲尔德的数据显示，尽管布达佩斯无疑受到数字游牧者的欢迎，但它仍然是灵活办公空间的新兴市场，仅占该市办公楼存量总量的 1.7% 至 1.8%。

paras.en: It ranked Hungary 31st on a list of 40 countries in its Global Trends in Flexible Office 2026 report — behind Spain and Portugal but ahead of Italy and Canada — while the Coworking Hungary Association views flexible solutions as "one of the most significant opportunities in the upcoming years."
paras.zh: 在其《2026 年灵活办公全球趋势》报告中，匈牙利在 40 个国家/地区的名单中排名第 31 位（落后于西班牙和葡萄牙，但领先于意大利和加拿大），而匈牙利联合办公协会则将灵活解决方案视为“未来几年最重要的机会之一”。

paras.en: For those looking to explore Hungary as a digital nomad, Vindisch's advises approaching the experience as a relocation rather than a visit, emphasizing the importance of sorting admin like banking and residency paperwork early. But, "most importantly," she said: "With a culture that's really uniquely beautiful, like Hungary, I would say come ready to embrace it and assimilate into it."
paras.zh: 对于那些希望以数字游牧者的身份探索匈牙利的人，温迪施建议将这种体验视为一次搬迁而不是一次访问，并强调尽早对银行和居住文书等行政管理工作进行分类的重要性。但是，“最重要的是，”她说：“对于像匈牙利这样真正独特美丽的文化，我想说准备好拥抱它并融入它。”

articles.title: The neuroscience behind stuttering

paras.en: Rachel Feltman: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·费尔特曼：《科学美国人》的《科学快报》，我是雷切尔·费尔特曼。

paras.en: Stuttering is a neurologic disorder affecting the timing, initiation and flow of speech, and it’s been documented throughout recorded history. Some folks even interpret a portion of the Torah as saying that Moses had a stutter. It’s also a fairly common speech variation, with around 5 to 10 percent of people stuttering for some portion of their childhoods and about 25 percent of that population continuing through adulthood. Roughly three million Americans speak with some kind of stutter, which can take the form of the repetition or prolongation of sounds, as well as interruptions in speech.
paras.zh: 口吃是一种神经系统疾病，影响说话的时机、开始和流畅，在整个历史记录中都有记录。有些人甚至将《托拉》的一部分解释为摩西有口吃。这也是一种相当常见的言语变异，大约 5% 到 10% 的人在童年的某些时候会口吃，而其中大约 25% 的人会一直口吃到成年。大约三百万美国人说话时有某种口吃，表现为声音的重复或延长，以及言语的中断。

paras.en: But this phenomenon has received surprisingly little attention from the medical and scientific communities, and some experts say treatment options could use a major overhaul.
paras.zh: 但令人惊讶的是，这种现象很少受到医学界和科学界的关注，一些专家表示，治疗方案可能需要进行重大改革。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Just this year a group of physicians, speech-language pathologists, researchers and people who stutter came together to release the first-ever consensus guidelines on the condition. Gerald Maguire, a psychiatrist and researcher who stutters himself, helped make that happen. He’s the founder and president of Stuttering Treatment and Research Society, or STARS, as well as the chief of medical staff and the director of residency training in psychiatry at College Medical Center in Long Beach, California. He’s here today to tell us what modern science has to say about stuttering and what comes next.
paras.zh: 就在今年，一群医生、语言病理学家、研究人员和口吃患者齐聚一堂，发布了有史以来第一份关于口吃疾病的共识指南。杰拉尔德·马奎尔（Gerald Maguire）是一位患有口吃的精神病学家和研究员，他帮助实现了这一目标。他是口吃治疗和研究协会 (STARS) 的创始人和主席，也是加州长滩大学医疗中心的医务人员主任和精神病学住院医师培训主任。他今天来这里是为了告诉我们现代科学对口吃的看法以及接下来会发生什么。

paras.en: Feltman: Thanks so much for coming on to chat with us today. I would love to start by just hearing a little bit about the work you do and how you got interested in the topic of stuttering in the first place.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常感谢您今天接受我们的采访。我很想先听听您所做的一些工作以及您最初是如何对口吃这个话题感兴趣的。

paras.en: Maguire: Thank you, Rachel. I’d like to say that I first became interested in stuttering probably around age three, when I began to talk. I do remember stuttering as a little boy, age four or five, and was always kind of mystified, like, “What’s different in my brain? What’s going on here? How is it that I can sing”—I don’t sing on key, but I can sing the, the term fluently. Um, everything else seemed okay, but—“How is it that I get stuck on these words? How is it that I get anxious about things and thinking about what words I was gonna say?” So it began then, and I remember, every New Year’s Eve, saying, “Okay, my New Year’s resolution: I’m not gonna stutter next year.” You’re seven, eight years old, and by 12:02 A.M., I was stuttering again. So I said, “There’s something here,” and I, kind of, committed even back in, you know, I remember in intermediate school, definitely by early high school, that I wanted to go to medical school to try to see what’s going on, to see if I could help myself and maybe help others with this.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：谢谢你，雷切尔。我想说，我第一次对口吃产生兴趣大概是在三岁左右，当时我开始说话。我确实记得小时候四五岁的时候口吃，而且总是有点困惑，比如，“我的大脑有什么不同吗？这里发生了什么事？我怎么会唱歌”——我不会唱调，但我可以流利地唱这个词。嗯，其他一切似乎都还好，但是——“我怎么会被这些话困住？我怎么会对事情感到焦虑并思考我要说的话？”我记得，从那时起，每个除夕夜，我都会说：“好吧，我的新年决心：明年我不再口吃了。”你七八岁了，到了凌晨 12 点 02 分，我又开始口吃了。所以我说，“这里有一些东西，”我，有点，甚至回到了，你知道，我记得在初中，肯定是高中早期，我想去医学院尝试看看发生了什么，看看我是否可以帮助自己，也许可以帮助别人。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, and could you tell us a little bit about your own experience of stuttering and what that’s like for you because I understand that there’s a lot of variation.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。好吧，您能否告诉我们一些您自己的口吃经历以及您的口吃经历，因为我知道口吃的情况有很多差异。

paras.en: Maguire: Yeah. So stuttering, it’s, for me, you know, for most of us, the vast majority of us, begins in childhood, so I’m no different than that. There’s quite a variability. We know that stuttering’s likely not one cause. I do have a strong family history. My older brother, who’s since passed away, he s- stuttered. Uh, I have family members on my mother’s side who also stutter. So it’s got to be some familial or genetic component with me that plays a role.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：是的。所以口吃，对我来说，你知道，对我们大多数人来说，我们绝大多数人，都是从童年开始的，所以我和这没有什么不同。有很大的可变性。我们知道口吃可能不是原因之一。我确实有很深厚的家族史。我的哥哥已经去世了，他说话结结巴巴的。呃，我妈妈那边的家人也口吃。所以一定是我的一些家族或遗传因素在起作用。

paras.en: For me, it was early on. It was a great amount of avoidance, mental exhaustion, even physical exhaustion, thinking about what word I was gonna say. “How am I gonna avoid a certain situation where I might have to say my name?” So tremendous avoidance, social anxiety and then, um, blocking on the words themselves.
paras.zh: For me, it was early on.这是一种巨大的回避，精神上的疲惫，甚至身体上的疲惫，思考我要说什么。 “我该如何避免必须说出自己名字的情况？”如此巨大的回避、社交焦虑，然后，呃，对词语本身的封锁。

paras.en: So that was kind of a, a snowball effect. The avoidance made the stuttering worse, and the stuttering would make the avoidance worse, and the so- social anxiety. We know that people who stutter do have a high coexistence or comorbidity with social anxiety, even depression. Fortunately I didn’t struggle with that. My late older brother did.
paras.zh: 这有点像滚雪球效应。回避让口吃变得更糟，而口吃又会让回避以及社会焦虑变得更糟。我们知道，口吃的人确实与社交焦虑甚至抑郁症有很高的共存或合并症。幸运的是我并没有为此挣扎。我已故的哥哥做到了。

paras.en: And then my journey was that—and I remember speaking in front of class or especially going into my college years, even in my f-, early on in, uh, my medical internship as a physician—trying to avoid use of the phone. The phone is, for me, was an extreme barrier. Saying my name was always something. And that’s not unusual. I’m more common in that with others. But so compensating for that, like, as an intern, a first-year resident, just not answering the phone, just going to wherever part of that hospital was and just being awake all night to answer that question that could have, for most clinicians, could have been a quick phone call. For me, I’m—right, the nurse is always like, “Well, he’s always attentive. This guy’s always here.” So. But for me, it was a compensation, and maybe it helped me become the physician I am today.
paras.zh: 然后我的旅程就是这样的——我记得在课堂上讲话，尤其​​是进入大学时代，甚至在我作为医生的医学实习初期——试图避免使用手机。对我来说，电话是一个极大的障碍。说出我的名字总是一件很重要的事情。这并不罕见。我和其他人在这方面比较常见。但对此的补偿，就像，作为一名实习生，一名第一年的住院医师，只是不接电话，只是去医院的任何地方，整夜不眠地回答这个问题，对于大多数临床医生来说，这可能是一个快速的电话。对我来说，我是对的，护士总是说，“嗯，他总是很专心。这个人总是在这里。”所以。但对我来说，这是一种补偿，也许它帮助我成为了今天的医生。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. I’m curious whether you could tell us about how portrayals of stuttering in the media compare to what the experience is really like. I mean, I know a classic mainstream example would be The King’s Speech. But what do you think the big misconceptions are in the media?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。我很好奇你能否告诉我们媒体对口吃的描述与真实的经历相比如何。我的意思是，我知道一个经典的主流例子是《国王的演讲》。但您认为媒体中最大的误解是什么？

paras.en: Maguire: Well, unfortunately that stuttering is still—can be made fun of still. I, I’m so glad that The King’s Speech came out because at least it showed a humanistic side, that we should not make fun of stuttering. It really captured well, I think, the anticipatory anxiety that, that “Bertie” [King George VI], the king, had when approaching, especially, the microphone.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：嗯，不幸的是，口吃仍然是可以被取笑的。我，我很高兴《国王的演讲》出来了，因为至少它表现出了人文主义的一面，我们不应该取笑口吃。我认为，它确实很好地捕捉到了国王“伯蒂”（乔治六世国王）在接近麦克风时所产生的预期焦虑。

paras.en: [CLIP: Helena Bonham Carter as Queen Elizabeth in a clip from The King’s Speech: “My husband is, um, well he’s required to speak publicly.” Colin Firth as King George VI: “I have received, th- th- th-.”]
paras.zh: [剪辑：海伦娜·伯翰·卡特在《国王的演讲》的剪辑中饰演伊丽莎白女王：“我的丈夫，嗯，他需要公开讲话。”科林·费斯饰演国王乔治六世：“我收到了，th-th-th-。”]

paras.en: I thought that was a, a very good portrayal of that. Of course, he wasn’t cured by any means. Maybe he was treated to some extent, which is great, and formed that relationship with his therapist and Lionel, Lionel Logue. But it’s not even that long ago that we had A Fish Called Wanda, which was not great.
paras.zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的写照。当然，他无论如何也没有痊愈。也许他受到了某种程度的治疗，这很好，并与他的治疗师和莱昂内尔·莱昂内尔·洛格建立了这种关系。但就在不久前，我们还推出了《一条叫旺达的鱼》，效果并不好。

paras.en: Maguire: The Life of Brian, uh, you know, Michael Palin, he’s got a good center now in the U.K., but really making fun of stuttering and mocking stuttering. Uh, My Cousin Vinny was, had some really negative—um, a child growing up, you know, uh, laughing at Porky Pig and others.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：布莱恩的一生，呃，你知道，迈克尔·佩林，他现在在英国有一个很好的中锋，但他确实在取笑口吃并嘲笑口吃。呃，我的表弟文尼，有一些非常消极的东西——嗯，一个成长过程中的孩子，你知道，呃，嘲笑小猪和其他人。

paras.en: [CLIP: Porky Pig in an episode of Looney Tunes speaking with a stutter.]
paras.zh: [剪辑：《乐一通》中的猪猪口吃地说话。]

paras.en: So the media portrayals are still there and have been there for, to make fun of stuttering. But fortunately, I think we’re, The King’s Speech was a, a tremendous step for- forward for us, I believe. And, uh, I’m not sure that the, the types—that’s all they had then—was this behavioral form of therapy, seemed to maybe help him with that, which was—but he still—remember, I remembered speaking to the screenwriter of this, that it was inspiring that still the king was able to get on the radio and speak, which was great. Um, and so I think that is an inspiration to not have your voice silenced because you stutter. And so I think that was a great message from The King’s Speech.
paras.zh: 因此，媒体对口吃的描述仍然存在，并且一直存在，以取笑口吃。但幸运的是，我认为《国王的演讲》对我们来​​说是向前迈出的一大步，我相信。而且，呃，我不确定这些类型——这就是他们当时所拥有的——这种行为治疗形式，似乎可能对他有帮助，这——但他仍然记得，我记得和编剧说过这件事，国王仍然能够在收音机上讲话，这是令人鼓舞的，这很棒。嗯，所以我认为这是一个激励，让你的声音不会因为你的口吃而被压制。所以我认为这是《国王的演讲》传达的一个很好的信息。

paras.en: Feltman: So something that I found really surprising when I was reading about your organization was that the first consensus medical guidelines on stuttering that you guys helped come up with only came about this year. There’s a lot to unpack there, but maybe we can start with, you know, “Historically, how has stuttering been discussed and defined and treated?” And then we can get into a little bit how that’s changing.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当我读到有关你们组织的信息时，我发现真正令人惊讶的是，你们帮助提出的第一个关于口吃的共识医学指南今年才出台。有很多东西需要解开，但也许我们可以从“历史上，口吃是如何讨论、定义和治疗的？”开始。然后我们可以了解一下这是如何变化的。

paras.en: Maguire: To me, it’s interesting, is that stuttering has occurred throughout recorded human history. We know that Demosthenes, the Greek orator, ancient Greek orator [stuttered]. There’s even, uh, references to Moses being a person who stutters. So—but it’s amazing to me that when we founded STARS, Stuttering Treatment and Research Society, just less than two years ago, we were able to claim the domain stutteringresearch.org. Just think about that. That—where has this been? So there’s been just a lot of myths about stuttering. It’s been really ignored largely by the greater medical community.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：对我来说，有趣的是，口吃在人类历史上一直存在。我们知道德摩斯梯尼，希腊演说家，古希腊演说家[结巴]。甚至，呃，提到摩西是一个口吃的人。所以，令我惊讶的是，不到两年前，当我们成立 STARS（口吃治疗与研究协会）时，我们就能够拥有 stutteringresearch.org 域名。想想看。那——这是哪儿？因此，关于口吃的说法有很多误区。它确实被更大的医学界所忽视。

paras.en: And so it’s had a tremendous history. I, I can’t explain exactly why. I wasn’t the first psychiatrist or physician to look at stuttering, definitely not. In fact, it was even—and I think this is what kind of led to it—there’s so much, so much information that was brought forward that didn’t turn out to be true that we kind of lost it. There’s kind of this division of psychoanalytic theories, like some of the Freudian theories about it, and then some of the behavioral theories through, um, different forms of speech pathology and the phys—and that they didn’t really lead to great results for the majority of people who stuttered. So it, kind of, lost, and people kind of gave up. And so even today, when I meet with my fellow physicians, and I say, “Well, yeah, we know, we now know that stuttering is neurologically based.” And they’ll say, “Wow, why don’t we ever think about this? Why don’t we ever study it?” Stuttering is more common than, say, Tourette’s disorder, yet there’s many more treatments, there’s more understanding of that condition, which is great, that we have that understanding. But stuttering’s been kind of held in, I don’t know, I just—maybe because the thought that we persons who stutter can have a good day and bad day, there’s great variability. That’s true in Tourette’s disorder, too. It’s true in social anxiety. So I’m, we just got to bring it out of the darkness. I can’t explain why, except that it’s been largely ignored. And, uh, we aim to change that.
paras.zh: 因此它有着悠久的历史。我，我无法解释清楚为什么。我不是第一个研究口吃的精神科医生或医生，绝对不是。事实上，甚至——我认为这就是导致它的原因——有太多太多的信息被提出，但事实证明它们并不真实，以至于我们失去了它。精神分析理论有这样的划分，比如一些关于它的弗洛伊德理论，然后是一些通过，嗯，不同形式的言语病理学和物理学的行为理论——它们并没有真正为大多数口吃的人带来伟大的结果。所以，它有点迷失了，人们也有点放弃了。因此，即使在今天，当我与我的医生同事见面时，我也会说：“嗯，是的，我们知道，我们现在知道口吃是基于神经学的。”他们会说，“哇，我们为什么不考虑一下这个？为什么我们不研究它？”口吃比抽动秽语症更常见，但有更多的治疗方法，对这种情况有更多的了解，这很好，我们有了这样的了解。但口吃一直被抑制着，我不知道，我只是——也许是因为我们认为 口吃的人可能有好的一天，也有坏的一天，变化很大。抽动秽语症也是如此。在社交焦虑中确实如此。所以我，我们必须把它带出黑暗。我无法解释原因，只是它在很大程度上被忽视了。而且，呃，我们的目标是改变这一点。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. In the comparison to Tourette’s, I almost wonder if there’s some aspect of stuttering being a, something that i—sort of the, the onus is on the speaker and the person who stutters to decide, you know, to avoid a phone call or something of that nature. And, you know, Tourette’s, you know, is seen as more, quote, unquote, “disruptive,” um, and it’s, you know, such a bleak reason for one to be researched more than the other. But I can’t help but think that might be true.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。与抽动秽语症相比，我几乎想知道口吃是否有某种方面，某种程度，说话者和口吃者有责任决定，你知道，避免接到电话或类似性质的事情。而且，你知道，抽动秽语症被视为更多，引用，不引用，“破坏性”，嗯，这是一个令人沮丧的理由，让一个人比另一个人得到更多的研究。但我忍不住认为这可能是真的。

paras.en: Maguire: But part of it could also be, you know, my friend Greg, uh, Mattingly, who serves as our chief medical adviser, Rachel, he also says, “Stuttering is where ADHD [attention deficit hyperactivity disorder] was 20 years ago.” People would think ADHD: “Well, this person just needs to focus. They’re flighty. They daydream.” But when we understand the neurology of it, now treatments are there; there’s greater understanding; the stigma goes down. I think complex brain conditions or disorders are misunderstood, and because there could be good days, bad days, we don’t know the fluctuations and so forth, there’s a lot of misunderstanding.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：但部分原因也可能是，你知道，我的朋友格雷格，呃，马丁利，他是我们的首席医疗顾问，雷切尔也说，“口吃就是 20 年前 ADHD（注意力缺陷多动障碍）的情况。”人们会认为多动症：“这个人只需要集中注意力。他们很轻浮。他们做白日梦。”但当我们了解了它的神经学原理后，现在就有了治疗方法；有更多的理解；耻辱感下降了。我认为复杂的大脑状况或疾病被误解了，因为可能有好日子，也有坏日子，我们不知道波动等等，所以存在很多误解。

paras.en: And that the brain is really the most complex organ system, much more than the heart or the kidneys, especially something around speech, which is more uniquely human. So I think the level of knowledge has been lagging, even understanding attention, cognition. So hopefully stuttering is where ADHD was 20 years ago. Or I even view depression: In my career as a psychiatrist—I finished medical school 35 years ago—depression used to be thought, unfortunately, “Oh, the person just needs to pull themselves up by their bootstraps, get out of bed and get a job. That’s gonna make it okay.” And so that’s kind of that thought about stuttering. “Slow down, relax.” So as we understand the neurology of it, I’m hopeful the advocacy improves the understanding, kind of like where we’ve been with other brain-based conditions like depression and ADHD.
paras.zh: 大脑确实是最复杂的器官系统，比心脏或肾脏复杂得多，尤其是与言语相关的东西，这是人类所独有的。所以我觉得知识水平一直滞后，甚至理解注意力、认知。所以，希望口吃是 20 年前 ADHD 的情况。或者我什至看待抑郁症：在我作为一名精神科医生的职业生涯中——我 35 年前从医学院毕业——不幸的是，抑郁症曾经被认为是“哦，这个人只需要靠自己的力量振作起来，起床并找到一份工作。这样就可以了。”这就是关于口吃的想法。 “慢点，放松。”因此，当我们了解它的神经学原理时，我希望宣传能够提高理解，就像我们对其他基于大脑的疾病（如抑郁症和多动症）的了解一样。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, what do we know about what’s actually, uh, going on in the brain when someone experiences a stutter?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。好吧，当有人口吃时，我们对大脑中到底发生了什么了解多少？

paras.en: Maguire: Great question. I can’t say it’s true for everyone. We do believe there’s multiple subtypes, different causes. We do think there’s a disruption in the majority of us who stutter in a circuit of the brain that involves—like, we understand what word we wanna say just fine, Rachel. We have no difficulty with that. It’s in the timing and the initiation of the phrase. Now that’s, we believe this is through a region of the brain called the, uh, the basal ganglia, which is deep in the brain, kinda controls muscle initiation and motion. And the thalamus can play a role with that. The amygdala—so anxiety can disrupt it.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：好问题。我不能说这对每个人都是如此。我们确实相信存在多种亚型、不同的原因。我们确实认为，我们大多数口吃者的大脑回路都受到了干扰，这涉及到——比如，我们很好地理解我们想说的话，雷切尔。我们对此没有任何困难。关键在于短语的时机和开头。现在，我们相信这是通过大脑的一个区域，称为基底神经节，它位于大脑深处，有点控制肌肉的启动和运动。丘脑可以发挥作用。杏仁核——因此焦虑会破坏它。

paras.en: But if we have, like, an external timer, like if we’re singing or we’re speaking to a rhythm, we can bypass that circuit, have another circuit. That’s why we’re fluent when we sing, ’cause there’s external timer rhythm. So we know there’s something in that circuit.
paras.zh: 但是，如果我们有一个外部计时器，就像我们在唱歌或有节奏地说话一样，我们可以绕过该电路，使用另一个电路。这就是为什么我们唱歌时很流利，因为有外部定时器节奏。所以我们知道那个电路中有东西。

paras.en: We don’t know everything about that circuit. We know that for many people, we believe that dopamine, which is one of the neurotransmitters, regulates that circuit. We’re not saying that’s the only thing that’s involved. There’s likely other neurotransmitters, other neurochemicals, other ways to, kinda, work within the circuit. Not saying that’s the cause. Could be. We do know that [for] some children, this, this circuit pathway doesn’t fully form and can form later, the insulation on that wiring, so to speak, and maybe that explains why some children, by adolescent years, don’t stutter anymore. But we need to know more, and it’s—the symptom may look the same; it doesn’t mean that the treatments are gonna be the same and [that] the causes are the same. One could have hypertension due to a heart issue, a kidney issue, stress, anxiety. Maybe some medicines work for that.
paras.zh: 我们并不了解该电路的一切。我们知道，对于许多人来说，我们相信多巴胺（神经递质之一）可以调节该回路。我们并不是说这是唯一涉及的事情。可能还有其他神经递质、其他神经化学物质、其他方式在回路中发挥作用。没说是这个原因。可能是。我们确实知道，对于一些孩子来说，这个电路通路没有完全形成，可以在以后形成，可以说，线路上的绝缘体，也许这可以解释为什么有些孩子到了青春期就不再口吃了。但我们需要了解更多，而且症状可能看起来是一样的；这并不意味着治疗方法是相同的，原因也是相同的。一个人可能因心脏问题、肾脏问题、压力、焦虑而患有高血压。也许有些药物对此有作用。

paras.en: And so we do know that, for many people, medicines that regulate dopamine can treat stuttering. We need more data with that, uh, as well as with other medicines or even some sorts of, um, how do I say, neuromodulation. Deep-brain stimulations [have] been reported in a few people. That goes into that circuit [and] can be invasive. Transcranial magnetic stimulation—could it get deep enough?
paras.zh: 因此我们确实知道，对于许多人来说，调节多巴胺的药物可以治疗口吃。我们需要更多的数据，呃，以及其他药物，甚至某种，嗯，我怎么说，神经调节。据报道，少数人接受了深部脑刺激。这会进入该回路并且可能具有侵入性。经颅磁刺激——深度够深吗？

paras.en: But also, we know that talk therapy can change the brain. We know this. And so we know that certain individuals with certain forms of talk therapy can be beneficial, too. So I’m hopeful someday we’ll have studies, and that’s what STARS is behind, is to look at “What are the certain types of treatments that help for one particular type of stuttering or for that particular individual and empower that individual to, uh, receive that care?”
paras.zh: 而且，我们知道谈话疗法可以改变大脑。我们知道这一点。因此我们知道，某些接受某种形式的谈话治疗的人也可能是有益的。所以我希望有一天我们能进行研究，这就是 STARS 背后的目的，就是看看“有哪些特定类型的治疗方法可以帮助治疗一种特定类型的口吃或特定的个人，并使该人能够，呃，接受这种护理？”

paras.en: Feltman: Well, now that we finally have these guidelines, you know, I’d love to hear a little bit about what went into creating them and, and what you all agreed on.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：好吧，现在我们终于有了这些指导方针，你知道，我很想听听一些关于创建它们的过程以及你们都同意的内容。

paras.en: Maguire: So STARS, we, we got together, we got a group together of 35 of us, uh, physicians of multiple specialties, psychiatry, neurology, pediatrics, primary care, also leading speech-language pathologists, neuroscience researchers and persons who stutter themselves, to put together—it’s more of a call to action in that [the] majority of us, you know, what we came up with, a consensus: that the current understanding is poor. That we do believe that stuttering’s neurologic, it’s brain-based. That hopefully can help decrease some stigma, help energize the field to move for-, forward. We do believe that the current state of understanding of health care in general, not just in the medical field but across all, all health care professionals, is low. It’s a poor understanding of stuttering, like, the current states of treatments that are available are poor.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：所以，STARS，我们，我们聚集在一起，我们聚集了一个由 35 个人组成的小组，呃，来自多个专业的医生，精神病学、神经病学、儿科、初级保健，还有领先的言语病理学家、神经科学研究人员和口吃者，聚集在一起——这更多的是号召我们大多数人采取行动，你知道，我们达成了一个共识：目前的理解很差。我们确实相信口吃是神经性的，是基于大脑的。希望这可以帮助减少一些耻辱，帮助激励这个领域前进。我们确实相信，目前人们对医疗保健的总体了解程度很低，不仅是在医疗领域，而且在所有医疗保健专业人员中都是如此。人们对口吃的理解很差，比如目前可用的治疗方法很差。

paras.en: We do believe that intervening earlier in a child can be beneficial. We need more studies showing this. We need studies showing that we believe that, you know, some individuals, certain medications like the dopamine medicines can be beneficial. But we need more research looking [into] which individuals, when do we—and even looking at what types of talk therapy combined with types of different pharmacotherapy or medical therapies together. It’s probably gonna be a, what we see with ADHD and depression, that combining treatments are gonna be the best.
paras.zh: 我们确实相信，早期对孩子进行干预是有益的。我们需要更多的研究来证明这一点。我们需要研究表明我们相信，你知道，某些药物（如多巴胺药物）可能是有益的。但我们需要更多的研究来了解哪些人、何时进行，甚至研究哪些类型的谈话疗法与不同类型的药物疗法或医学疗法相结合。我们在多动症和抑郁症方面看到的情况可能是，结合治疗将是最好的。

paras.en: We got together because the field needed it. Um, we’re a nonprofit. We’re an all-volunteer board, and, and we say, “Hey, this is a call to action for the rest of the field, the greater scientific community and medical communities to notice us and help us answer these questions.”
paras.zh: 我们聚在一起是因为这个领域需要它。嗯，我们是非营利组织。我们是一个全志愿者委员会，我们说：“嘿，这是呼吁该领域的其他人、更大的科学界和医学界采取行动，以关注我们并帮助我们回答这些问题。”

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, if any of our listeners are interested in, in getting involved in research, if it, it’s relevant to them ...
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。好吧，如果我们的任何听众有兴趣参与研究，如果有的话，这与他们相关......

paras.en: Feltman: Where should they go to look for it?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：他们应该去哪里寻找它？

paras.en: Feltman: Well thank you so much for, uh, coming on to talk with us today.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，非常感谢您今天接受我们的采访。

paras.en: Maguire: Appreciate it very much. Thank you.
paras.zh: 马奎尔：非常欣赏。谢谢。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. We’ll be back on Monday for our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。我们将于周一回来参加每周科学新闻综述。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: Why the brain’s ability to picture images may influence decision making

paras.en: If you were to imagine the face of your favorite person, how well could you do it? Can you envision the shape of their nose? Or the texture of their hair? The exact hue of their eyes?
paras.zh: 如果你要想象你最喜欢的人的脸，你能做得怎么样？你能想象他们鼻子的形状吗？或者他们头发的质地？他们眼睛的确切颜色？

paras.en: Some of us will answer yes, in fine detail—but others won’t be able to do it all. It turns out that the way we conjure images in our mind is highly individual, says Joel Pearson, a professor of cognitive neuroscience at the University of New South Wales in Australia, who studies aphantasia, or the inability to visualize images.
paras.zh: 我们中的一些人会详细回答是的，但其他人则无法全部做到。澳大利亚新南威尔士大学认知神经科学教授乔尔·皮尔森（Joel Pearson）研究了失语症，即无法形象化图像的情况，他说，事实证明，我们在脑海中想象图像的方式是高度个人化的。

paras.en: “We have a range of individual differences when it comes to ability to visualize,” Pearson says. At one end of the spectrum, there’s aphantasia—a lack of any mental imagery. On the other is “hyperphantasia,” or the ability to envision hyper-realistic mental images. “Most people are somewhere in the middle,” he says.
paras.zh: “在可视化能力方面，我们存在一系列个体差异，”皮尔森说。一方面，存在失语症——缺乏任何心理意象。另一方面是“hyperphantasia”，即想象超现实心理图像的能力。 “大多数人都处于中间位置，”他说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The ability to hold an image in our “mind’s eye” is linked to the visual cortex—the part of the brain that is largely responsible for processing our sense of sight. In general, the size of a person’s primary visual cortex is inversely correlated with the strength of their mind’s eye, although it’s unclear why.
paras.zh: 在我们的“心灵之眼”中保存图像的能力与视觉皮层有关，视觉皮层是大脑中主要负责处理我们的视觉的部分。一般来说，一个人的初级视觉皮层的大小与他们的心灵之眼的强度成反比，尽管原因尚不清楚。

paras.en: In lab experiments, Pearson and his colleagues have found that “cortical excitability”—how responsive the brain’s cells are to stimuli—can influence their mental imagery, too. In a 2020 study published in eLife, they found that stimulating the visual cortex with electricity could increase or decrease a person’s visualization strength. This indicates that how responsive the visual cortex is to incoming information has a causal role in mental imagery, he says.
paras.zh: 在实验室实验中，皮尔逊和他的同事发现“皮质兴奋性”——大脑细胞对刺激的反应程度——也会影响他们的心理意象。在 eLife 2020 年发表的一项研究中，他们发现用电刺激视觉皮层可以增加或减少人的可视化强度。他说，这表明视觉皮层对传入信息的反应程度在心理意象中具有因果作用。

paras.en: Other factors may be at play, too. A head injury, for instance, can affect a person’s imagination, and largely anecdotal reports suggest psychedelic drugs can do so as well, Pearson says. Some researchers also hypothesize that our visualization abilities may change with age.
paras.zh: 其他因素也可能在起作用。皮尔森说，例如，头部受伤会影响一个人的想象力，而且大部分轶事报告表明迷幻药物也会产生这种影响。一些研究人员还假设我们的可视化能力可能会随着年龄的增长而变化。

paras.en: Other evidence suggests aphantasia may be at least partly genetic because it seems to run in families. But for the most part, the reasons why any individual might lack the ability to picture something in their mind is largely a mystery. “We can't explain why someone seems to be born with congenital aphantasia versus someone with very strong imagery,” Pearson says. It’s also unclear whether individuals with aphantasia simply have no mental imagery or if they’re just not consciously aware of it.
paras.zh: 其他证据表明失语症可能至少部分是遗传性的，因为它似乎有家族遗传性。但在大多数情况下，任何人可能缺乏在脑海中描绘某些事物的能力的原因很大程度上是一个谜。 “我们无法解释为什么有些人似乎天生患有先天性失语症，而有些人却具有很强的想象能力，”皮尔森说。目前还不清楚失语症患者是否根本没有心理意象，或者只是没有意识到这一点。

paras.en: Much less is known about the other end of the scale, hyperphantasia. Pearson says he has heard of individuals who can watch a movie and replay it in their mind as if they were watching it for real. But finding those people—and getting them into the lab to study—has been a challenge, he says.
paras.zh: 对于天平的另一端——过度幻想——知之甚少。皮尔森说，他听说有人可以观看一部电影并在脑海中重播，就好像他们正在观看真实的电影一样。但他说，找到这些人并让他们进入实验室进行研究一直是一个挑战。

paras.en: It’s also been a challenge to assess how strong a given person’s mind’s eye is, Pearson says. Aphantasia has been documented at least as far back as the 1880s, when English scientist Francis Galton asked 100 men to imagine an object such as their breakfast table and describe a couple of their mental image’s qualities, including how clear and distinct it was. Some of them, Galton reported, had no ability to do so.
paras.zh: 皮尔森说，评估一个人的心灵之眼有多强也是一个挑战。失语症的记录至少可以追溯到 1880 年代，当时英国科学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿 (Francis Galton) 让 100 名男性想象一个物体，比如他们的早餐桌，并描述他们心理图像的一些品质，包括它的清晰程度和独特性。高尔顿报告说，其中一些人没有能力这样做。

paras.en: Today scientists have developed more advanced methods. Pearson and his colleagues have tried out a few techniques, including a test that involves a phenomenon called “binocular rivalry,” in which two different stimuli, such as different color patterns, compete for dominance when they’re presented to each eye; in the test, imagining which of the two you will see just before both flash in front of you makes it more likely that you will actually see it. Other assays measure a person’s physiological responses to mental imagery, such as their pupil size when they think about something bright or their skin conductance when they envision something scary, such as a shark fin swirling nearby in the water.
paras.zh: 如今，科学家们已经开发出更先进的方法。皮尔逊和他的同事已经尝试了一些技术，包括一项涉及一种称为“双眼竞争”现象的测试，其中两种不同的刺激（例如不同的颜色图案）在呈现给每只眼睛时争夺主导地位；在测试中，想象一下您将在两者在您面前闪烁之前看到哪两个，这样您更有可能真正看到它。其他测定测量一个人对心理意象的生理反应，例如当他们想到明亮的东西时的瞳孔大小或当他们想象一些可怕的东西时的皮肤电导，例如附近水中旋转的鱼翅。

paras.en: “If you think in pictures, it will amplify any emotional response you have to things,” Pearson explains, “because it’s almost like it’s tricking the rest of your brain into thinking the thing is happening right in front of you, even though it’s not.”
paras.zh: “如果你用图片来思考，它会放大你对事物的情绪反应，”皮尔森解释道，“因为它几乎就像是在欺骗你大脑的其他部分，让你认为事情就发生在你面前，尽管事实并非如此。”

paras.en: Recently, researchers have started using computer algorithms and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to “decode” what people are thinking about. Researchers can train an algorithm on a person’s brain activity when they look at, say, a letter of the alphabet. Then, when that person visualizes that letter, the computer can recognize, or “decode,” that thought.
paras.zh: 最近，研究人员开始使用计算机算法和功能磁共振成像（fMRI）来“解码”人们的想法。研究人员可以训练一种算法，研究一个人在查看字母表中的字母时的大脑活动。然后，当该人看到该字母时，计算机就可以识别或“解码”该想法。

paras.en: How we picture things in our heads can have a profound effect on our lives—and not always in the ways you might think. Having aphantasia, for example, doesn’t necessarily limit creativity, Pearson says. As Scientific American previously reported, some of the world’s best animators, including Pixar co-founder Ed Catmull and former Disney animator Glen Keane, have said they don’t think in images. And some research suggests imagery may impact a person’s perception of risk, Pearson says—if you can visualize the feeling of bungee jumping, for instance, it may change your decision of whether to try it out.
paras.zh: 我们如何在头脑中想象事物会对我们的生活产生深远的影响——而且并不总是以你想象的方式。例如，皮尔森说，患有失语症并不一定会限制创造力。正如《科学美国人》之前报道的那样，世界上一些最优秀的动画师，包括皮克斯联合创始人埃德·卡特莫尔和前迪士尼动画师格伦·基恩，都表示他们不会用图像来思考。皮尔森说，一些研究表明图像可能会影响一个人对风险的感知——例如，如果你能想象蹦极的感觉，它可能会改变你是否尝试的决定。

paras.en: People with strong mental imagery, meanwhile, are more likely to experience anxiety or post-traumatic stress disorder after an upsetting event.
paras.zh: 与此同时，具有强烈心理意象的人在经历令人不安的事件后更有可能经历焦虑或创伤后应激障碍。

paras.en: To test your own mental imagery, try the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire, Pearson says—but keep in mind that these tests are not definitive.
paras.zh: 皮尔逊说，为了测试你自己的心理意象，可以尝试视觉意象的生动性问卷，但请记住，这些测试并不是确定的。

paras.en: “It’s an amazing example of how we all think in very different ways,” Pearson says. “It turns out, if you think in pictures or not, it will change the how you make decisions.”
paras.zh: 皮尔森说：“这是一个令人惊奇的例子，展示了我们如何以截然不同的方式思考。” “事实证明，无论你是否用图片思考，它都会改变你做决定的方式。”

articles.title: We beat screwworm once. Here’s how we’re trying to do it again

paras.en: A Texas rancher in the 1940s notices the small wound on his calf first thing in the morning. It’s nothing unusual—perhaps the calf snagged on barbed wire. But when the rancher returns at noon to check on the animal, the wound has grown and is raw and weeping. Closer inspection reveals hundreds of little, white larvae writhing and burrowing into the flesh: screwworm maggots. If left untreated, the calf will be dead within days.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 40 年代，德克萨斯州的一位牧场主早上第一件事就注意到小腿上的小伤口。这没什么不寻常的——也许小牛被铁丝网绊住了。但当牧场主中午回来查看这只动物时，伤口已经变大，而且还红肿流血。仔细观察会发现数百只白色的小幼虫在肉中扭动并钻入肉中：螺旋蛆。如果不及时治疗，小牛几天内就会死亡。

paras.en: This isn’t an isolated horror story: the flesh-eating parasite devastated livestock operations from Florida to Texas for much of the 20th century, when it killed thousands of animals every year and cost more than $1 billion annually in today’s dollars. Back then screwworm was simply a fact of life, a gruesome tax levied by nature on anyone who raised animals.
paras.zh: 这并不是一个孤立的恐怖故事：在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，这种食肉寄生虫摧毁了从佛罗里达州到德克萨斯州的畜牧业，每年杀死数千只动物，每年造成的损失以今天的美元计算超过 10 亿美元。那时，螺旋虫只是生活中的一个事实，是大自然向任何饲养动物的人征收的可怕税款。

paras.en: Then came one of the most remarkable triumphs in pest control. Through a brilliant combination of science and engineering, screwworm was eliminated in the U.S. in 1966. The victory seemingly closed a chapter in agricultural history. But then, on June 3, 2026, screwworm reared its ugly head once more: larvae were found in a three-week-old calf in Zavala County, Texas, followed within days by confirmed cases in three other counties, as well as in a dog in New Mexico that had traveled across state lines. The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed the first wildlife detection on October 21: an elk killed on a game ranch in Pecos County, Texas. There have been more than 60 confirmed cases in domestic animals since then and an additional case in another Texas elk. With hunting season now underway, more infections could emerge, particularly in wildlife, as hunters encounter affected animals.
paras.zh: 随后，害虫防治领域取得了最引人注目的胜利之一。 1966年，通过科学与工程的巧妙结合，美国消灭了螺旋蝇。这一胜利似乎为农业历史画上了新的一页。但随后，2026 年 6 月 3 日，螺旋虫再次露出了它丑陋的头：德克萨斯州萨瓦拉县一头三周大的小牛身上发现了幼虫，几天之内，其他三个县以及新墨西哥州一只跨越州界的狗身上也出现了确诊病例。美国农业部于10月21日确认了首例野生动物检测：一头麋鹿在德克萨斯州佩科斯县的一个狩猎牧场被杀。自那时起，已有超过 60 例家畜确诊病例，另外一例来自德克萨斯州麋鹿。随着狩猎季节的到来，当猎人遇到受影响的动物时，可能会出现更多感染，特别是在野生动物中。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The return of New World screwworm to U.S. soil for the first time in decades follows years of warnings from veterinarians and entomologists who have watched the parasite creep steadily northward through Central America and Mexico, propelled by a rise in temperatures, shifts in wildlife movements and gaps in surveillance. Its reappearance now poses an urgent threat to ranchers, wildlife and public health.
paras.zh: 几十年来，新世界螺旋蝇首次重返美国土壤，此前兽医和昆虫学家多年来一直发出警告，他们观察到这种寄生虫在气温上升、野生动物迁徙变化和监测漏洞的推动下，通过中美洲和墨西哥稳步向北蔓延。它的再次出现对牧场主、野生动物和公共健康构成了紧迫的威胁。

paras.en: It’s not 1966 anymore. The U.S. can’t simply rerun the old playbook. Instead officials are trying to pair proven methods with modern technology, such as artificial intelligence, drones and thermal cameras, to keep the once eliminated parasite from regaining a foothold.
paras.zh: 现在已经不是 1966 年了。美国不能简单地重演旧剧本。相反，官员们正试图将经过验证的方法与人工智能、无人机和热像仪等现代技术结合起来，以防止曾经被消灭的寄生虫重新站稳脚跟。

paras.en: The New World screwworm’s scientific name, Cochliomyia hominivorax, comes in part from a rough translation of “man-eater” in Latin. Unlike most other blowflies, which eat carrion, it feeds on the living tissue or flesh of warm-blooded animals—including people—to complete its life cycle.
paras.zh: 新大陆螺旋虫的学名“Cochliomyia hominivorax”，部分来自拉丁语“食人者”的粗略翻译。与大多数其他吃腐肉的绿头苍蝇不同，它以温血动物（包括人类）的活组织或肉为食，以完成其生命周期。

paras.en: The cycle begins when a female fly lays 200 to 300 eggs at a time in an open wound or orifice such as the eyes, nose or mouth. Within 24 hours, the eggs hatch into larvae and immediately start burrowing headfirst into the flesh using hooklike mouthparts. As they feed, they literally spiral or screw their way in, inspiring their common name. When sated, the larvae fall to the ground, lodge themselves into soil and emerge as adults to continue the vicious cycle.
paras.zh: 当雌蝇在眼睛、鼻子或嘴巴等开放性伤口或孔口一次产下 200 至 300 个卵时，这个周期就开始了。 24 小时内，卵孵化成幼虫，并立即开始用钩状口器头朝下钻入肉中。当它们进食时，它们实际上会螺旋或旋入其中，从而激发了它们的共同名字。吃饱后，幼虫会落到地上，将自己埋入土壤中，然后长成成虫，继续恶性循环。

paras.en: The results are devastating. Bacteria can infect the wounds where maggots are present, leading to sepsis. Without proper wound care and quarantine, infected animals die quickly, often within a week.
paras.zh: 结果是毁灭性的。细菌会感染有蛆虫的伤口，导致败血症。如果没有适当的伤口护理和检疫，受感染的动物很快就会死亡，通常在一周内。

paras.en: In the past, ranchers and veterinarians could only slow the spread of screwworm but never stop it. The reproductive rate of the fly was too high, and the geography it covered was too vast.
paras.zh: 过去，牧场主和兽医只能减缓螺旋虫的传播，却无法阻止它。苍蝇的繁殖率太高，而且它覆盖的地理范围太广。

paras.en: But in the 1930s USDA scientists Edward Knipling and Raymond Bushland came up with a protocol called the sterile insect technique (SIT). It’s founded on a basic biological process: female blowflies only mate once. If the male is sterile, she lays unfertilized eggs that never hatch, effectively removing them from the population. Release enough sterile males to outnumber wild males, and you can drive the population into collapse without a single drop of pesticide.
paras.zh: 但在 20 世纪 30 年代，美国农业部科学家 Edward Knipling 和 Raymond Bushland 提出了一项称为昆虫不育技术 (SIT) 的方案。它建立在一个基本的生物过程之上：雌性苍蝇只交配一次。如果雄性不育，她会产下从未孵化的未受精卵，从而有效地将它们从种群中清除。释放足够多的不育雄性，使其数量超过野生雄性，你就可以在不使用一滴农药的情况下使种群数量崩溃。

paras.en: After some trial and error, the technique succeeded in 1954, when it was used on the island of Curaçao. As screwworms tore through the local goat population, researchers packed sterile males into paper boxes and dropped them from aircraft. The boxes burst open on impact, scattering the flies across the landscape. They quickly swamped the wild population, and in about eight months, screwworm was eliminated from the island.
paras.zh: 经过一番试验和错误后，该技术于 1954 年获得成功，并在库拉索岛使用。当螺旋虫席卷当地山羊种群时，研究人员将不育的雄性山羊装入纸盒中，然后从飞机上扔下。盒子在撞击时爆开，苍蝇散落到各处。它们很快就淹没了野生种群，大约八个月后，螺旋虫就从岛上消灭了。

paras.en: Florida was cleared by 1959. Texas proved more challenging, given its vast ranching operations, but it, too, was eventually declared screwworm-free in 1966, and the effort pushed south through Mexico and into Central America.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州于 1959 年被清除。事实证明，得克萨斯州更具挑战性，因为其大规模的牧场经营，但它最终也于 1966 年被宣布消灭了螺旋蝇，这项工作向南推进，穿过墨西哥，进入中美洲。

paras.en: South America’s size, terrain and political complexity made it too difficult to tackle, so scientists established a suppression zone at Panama’s Darién Gap, the narrow neck of land where Central and South America meet. There sterile flies were continuously released to prevent northern migration. Screwworm was functionally eliminated everywhere north of that line by 2002. Not anymore.
paras.zh: 南美洲的面积、地形和政治复杂性使其难以应对，因此科学家在巴拿马的达连峡（中美洲和南美洲交界处的狭窄地带）建立了一个抑制区。那里不断释放不育的苍蝇，以阻止北方迁徙。到 2002 年，该线以北的所有地方螺旋虫都已被功能性消灭。现在不行了。

paras.en: For decades, the system worked. But by 2023, a perfect storm of factors had converged to create the conditions for the screwworm’s return.
paras.zh: 几十年来，这个系统一直有效。但到了 2023 年，一场完美的因素风暴汇聚在一起，为螺旋虫的回归创造了条件。

paras.en: Climate change has expanded the areas that have suitably warm, humid conditions for more of the year for screwworm to thrive, meaning less seasonal die-off and more generations of screwworms per year.
paras.zh: 气候变化扩大了一年中有更多时间适合螺旋虫生长的温暖、潮湿条件的地区，这意味着季节性死亡减少，每年螺旋虫的世代数量增加。

paras.en: Political instability in Panama, a surge in drug‑trafficking activity and heavy human migration through the Darién Gap made it increasingly hard to maintain the Panama Barrier. At the same time, U.S. federal budget pressures periodically forced cutbacks in surveillance. Early in 2025 the Trump administration’s U.S. DOGE Service sharply reduced funding for the USDA’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service and ended a USAID program that had monitored and contained New World screwworm in Central America. Border policies have also oscillated: in the past two years, Mexico-U.S. livestock import rules have relaxed and tightened repeatedly, creating windows in which infected animals could slip through. And even when border quarantines are in place, illegal livestock and wildlife crossings continue.
paras.zh: 巴拿马政局不稳定、贩毒活动激增以及通过达连峡的大量人口移民使得维持巴拿马屏障变得越来越困难。与此同时，美国联邦预算压力定期迫使监视活动削减。 2025 年初，特朗普政府的美国总督署大幅减少了对美国农业部动植物卫生检验局的资助，并结束了美国国际开发署在中美洲监测和遏制新世界螺旋虫的项目。边境政策也出现了波动：过去两年，墨西哥与美国之间的关系发生了变化。牲畜进口规定一再放松和收紧，为受感染的动物创造了机会。即使实施了边境检疫，非法牲畜和野生动物过境仍在继续。

paras.en: Adding to the strain, wild screwworm may be evolving to recognize and reject mass-reared sterile males. This behavior, known as assortative mating, would undermine the sterile insect technique the eradication program relies on.
paras.zh: 除了这种菌株之外，野生螺旋虫可能正在进化以识别和排斥大规模饲养的不育雄性。这种被称为选型交配的行为会破坏根除计划所依赖的昆虫不育技术。

paras.en: A warning of the current infestation came in a 2016 outbreak in the Key deer population of Florida—these were the first U.S. cases in decades. Though that outbreak was contained by strictly monitoring the deer and releasing sterile flies, it exposed critical vulnerabilities: the difficulty of detecting early cases, the danger to wildlife populations with no natural resistance and the risks associated with island and isolated ecosystems.
paras.zh: 2016 年佛罗里达州关键鹿群中爆发的一次疫情就发出了当前感染的警告——这是美国几十年来首次出现病例。尽管通过严格监测鹿和释放不育苍蝇遏制了疫情的爆发，但它暴露了严重的脆弱性：难以发现早期病例，对没有自然抵抗力的野生动物种群构成危险，以及与岛屿和孤立的生态系统相关的风险。

paras.en: Those same problems were still in play as the screwworm made its real return, moving steadily northward through Central America. In November 2024 screwworm was detected in a cow at an inspection checkpoint in the state of Chiapas in Mexico—the first detection that far north in the country in decades. By late 2025, isolated cases were being found in northern Mexico, within about 100 miles of the Texas border. In January 2026 the USDA shifted sterile fly dispersal efforts into Texas as a precaution. By February, a new sterile fly dispersal facility had opened at Moore Air Base in Texas, the first domestic installation the U.S. has ever built. None of it came fast enough.
paras.zh: 当螺旋虫真正回归并稳定地向北穿过中美洲时，这些同样的问题仍然存在。 2024 年 11 月，墨西哥恰帕斯州的一个检查站在一头牛身上发现了螺旋虫，这是几十年来在该国最北部地区首次发现螺旋虫。到 2025 年底，墨西哥北部距德克萨斯州边境约 100 英里的范围内发现了孤立病例。 2026 年 1 月，作为预防措施，美国农业部将不育蝇驱散工作转移到德克萨斯州。到了二月，一个新的无菌苍蝇扩散设施在德克萨斯州摩尔空军基地投入使用，这是美国建造的第一个国内设施。这些都来得不够快。

paras.en: For the first several months of the new infestation, screwworm cases were confirmed only in domestic animals, located in Texas and New Mexico, and early efforts to restrict trade and impose quarantine zones seemed to be working. But after hunting season began in September, the USDA confirmed the first U.S. wildlife detection in the Texas elk. With a dog in Arizona now among the reported cases and almost four dozen new domestic detections so far in November alone, veterinarians, ranchers and wildlife managers are bracing for more cases, particularly if the parasite gains a foothold in deer, elk or feral hogs that share ranges with livestock.
paras.zh: 在新感染的头几个月，螺旋虫病例仅在家畜中得到证实，位于德克萨斯州和新墨西哥州，限制贸易和实行检疫区的早期努力似乎正在发挥作用。但在九月份狩猎季节开始后，美国农业部证实了美国在德克萨斯州麋鹿中首次发现野生动物。目前，亚利桑那州报告的病例中有一只狗，仅在 11 月份就发现了近四打新的家养病例，兽医、牧场主和野生动物管理者正准备迎接更多病例，特别是如果这种寄生虫在与牲畜共享活动范围的鹿、麋鹿或野猪中占据一席之地。

paras.en: So what is being done to prevent screwworm from gaining ground this time around?
paras.zh: 那么，这次要采取什么措施来防止螺旋虫蔓延呢？

paras.en: The core response to the outbreak remains the approach that worked 60 years ago: sterile fly release. The new sterile fly facility at Moore Air Base has been releasing 100 million flies weekly since February 2026. A separate facility there is projected to begin operations in 2027, scaling up to producing 300 million flies per week. More flies are also being sent out across Mexico.
paras.zh: 应对疫情的核心措施仍然是 60 年前有效的方法：释放不育蝇。自 2026 年 2 月以来，摩尔空军基地的新无菌苍蝇设施每周释放 1 亿只苍蝇。那里的一个单独设施预计将于 2027 年开始运营，扩大到每周生产 3 亿只苍蝇。更多的苍蝇也被派往墨西哥各地。

paras.en: But the question on many researchers’ minds is whether these sterile flies are sufficient.
paras.zh: 但许多研究人员心中的问题是这些不育果蝇是否足够。

paras.en: On June 16, the USDA announced funding for 40 projects totaling around $105 million to help battle screwworm. Much of that investment is going toward next-generation control tools, but only a couple of these are usable now or will be in the very near future. The most advanced is NovoFly, a genetically engineered male-only strain. Conventional programs must rear and sterilize both sexes because they can’t easily be separated, even though only males are needed, so a male-only strain dramatically increases efficiency. The Environmental Protection Agency granted an emergency exemption for NovoFly use in the U.S. in June; Mexico has yet to approve it, pending public consultation. As of November, NovoFly was not yet being used operationally, and its deployment timeline remained uncertain.
paras.zh: 6 月 16 日，美国农业部宣布为 40 个项目提供总计约 1.05 亿美元的资助，以帮助对抗螺旋虫。大部分投资都用于下一代控制工具，但其中只有少数现在或在不久的将来可用。最先进的是NovoFly，一种基因工程改造的纯雄性品系。传统的计划必须对两种性别进行饲养和绝育，因为即使只需要雄性，它们也不容易分开，因此仅雄性菌株可以显着提高效率。 6 月份，美国环境保护局授予 NovoFly 在美国使用的紧急豁免；墨西哥尚未批准该法案，正在等待公众咨询。截至 11 月，NovoFly 尚未投入运营，其部署时间表仍不确定。

paras.en: Researchers are also testing a technology called eBeam sterilization. It uses high-energy electrons to sterilize flies instead of the current method, which involves the radioactive isotope cobalt 60. Early lab results are promising, and pilot evaluations are underway, though it would take years to adapt production facilities to use this technique. Yet another approach uses a synthetic scent, called swormlure-5, that mimics an open wound, luring adult flies into traps. Paired with insecticide, swormlure-5 has cut local fly populations by up to 90 percent, and it is now used in border traps for surveillance.
paras.zh: 研究人员还在测试一种称为电子束灭菌的技术。它使用高能电子来消灭苍蝇，而不是目前使用放射​​性同位素钴 60 的方法。早期的实验室结果很有希望，试点评估正在进行中，尽管需要数年时间才能使生产设施适应使用该技术。另一种方法是使用一种名为 swormlure-5 的合成气味，模仿开放性伤口，将成年苍蝇引诱到陷阱中。与杀虫剂配合使用，swormlure-5 已使当地苍蝇数量减少了 90%，现在用于边境诱捕器中进行监视。

paras.en: More speculative approaches, such as CRISPR-based gene editing to create sterile males, are likely many more years away from being implemented.
paras.zh: 更具推测性的方法，例如基于 CRISPR 的基因编辑来创造不育雄性，可能还需要很多年才能得到实施。

paras.en: The current response also draws on surveillance technologies that were unavailable during the last major eradication campaign. USDA teams are using drones equipped with thermal sensors and high-resolution cameras to survey livestock and wildlife across vast ranches, looking for abnormal heat signatures, visible wounds and unusual behavior that could signal infestation. The USDA carried out more than 2,000 drone surveillance flights and observations of nearly 40,000 animals in Texas between June 4 and October 22. In addition, AI tools are being developed to analyze the images, flag suspicious animals for closer inspection and help prioritize field investigations, while predictive models use weather, habitat and outbreak data to forecast where the pest may spread. Trail cameras, thousands of insect traps and enhanced monitoring of animal movements add further layers of surveillance.
paras.zh: 目前的应对措施还利用了上次重大根除运动期间无法使用的监测技术。美国农业部团队正在使用配备热传感器和高分辨率摄像头的无人机来调查大片牧场的牲畜和野生动物，寻找异常的热信号、可见的伤口和可能表明感染的异常行为。 6 月 4 日至 10 月 22 日期间，美国农业部在德克萨斯州进行了 2,000 多次无人机监视飞行，对近 40,000 只动物进行了观察。此外，正在开发人工智能工具来分析图像，标记可疑动物以进行更仔细的检查，并帮助确定现场调查的优先顺序，而预测模型则使用天气、栖息地和爆发数据来预测害虫可能传播的位置。追踪摄像机、数以千计的昆虫陷阱和对动物活动的强化监控进一步增加了监控层次。

paras.en: If this pest is not contained, the economic stakes are enormous. A sustained outbreak could mean livestock deaths, costly inspections and treatment, movement restrictions and more disruption to cross-border trade. Monitoring wild animals, which are harder to inspect and treat than livestock, is another challenge, and veterinary capacity is also a concern. Many U.S. veterinarians have never encountered screwworm, making rancher education and rapid diagnosis essential.
paras.zh: 如果这种害虫得不到遏制，经济损失将是巨大的。持续的疫情爆发可能意味着牲畜死亡、昂贵的检查和治疗、行动限制以及跨境贸易的更多干扰。监测野生动物是另一个挑战，因为野生动物比牲畜更难检查和治疗，兽医能力也是一个问题。许多美国兽医从未遇到过螺旋虫，因此牧场主教育和快速诊断至关重要。

paras.en: The coming months will show whether the current response is working. Progress would look like sustained declines in new infestations and wild-fly detections, followed by long stretches without cases. Historically, eradication programs have used six months without detection as a technical benchmark and 12 months as a basis for declaring an area officially free of screwworm, though it depends on the local circumstances. The question we have now is whether the response is suppressing the outbreak or merely chasing its spread. The tools exist; the challenge is deploying them at sufficient scale for long enough to make a lasting change.
paras.zh: 未来几个月将显示当前的应对措施是否有效。进展看起来像是新感染和野蝇检测持续下降，然后是长期没有病例。从历史上看，根除计划以六个月未检测到的情况为技术基准，并以 12 个月作为正式宣布某个地区无螺旋虫的基础，但这取决于当地情况。我们现在面临的问题是，应对措施是抑制疫情还是仅仅遏制其蔓延。工具已经存在；挑战在于以足够的规模部署它们并持续足够长的时间，以实现持久的改变。

articles.title: A high-fiber diet may clear away plastic in the gut
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Here’s a new reason to eat your beans and greens.
paras.zh: 这是吃豆类和蔬菜的新理由。

paras.en: A high-fiber diet may help sweep plastic particles from the gut, researchers report October 15 in Nature Communications. In mice that ingested plastic, eating loads of fiber daily kept the particles from piling up in the intestines. The finding hints at fiber’s power to protect the body from environmental garbage, says Eddy Y. Zeng, an environmental scientist at South China University of Technology in Guangzhou.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 15 日在《自然通讯》杂志上报道，高纤维饮食可能有助于清除肠道中的塑料颗粒。在摄入塑料的小鼠中，每天摄入大量纤维可以防止颗粒在肠道内堆积。广州华南理工大学环境科学家 Eddy Y. Zeng 表示，这一发现暗示了纤维具有保护人体免受环境垃圾侵害的能力。

paras.en: Researchers have long known that fiber can improve our health, in part by lowering cholesterol, keeping blood sugar levels in check and easing food through the gut. But now, Zeng says, his team’s results suggest an additional benefit.
paras.zh: 研究人员早就知道纤维可以改善我们的健康，部分原因是降低胆固醇、控制血糖水平和促进食物通过肠道。但现在，曾说，他的团队的结果表明了额外的好处。

paras.en: We live in a world littered with plastic, much of it too small to see. These micro and nanoplastics, shed by disposable water bottles, fast food containers and other worldly junk, can make their way into our bodies. It’s not completely clear what such shards do to our health, but we have some hints. Scientists have linked plastic particles in people’s arteries to increased risk of heart attack and stroke. And mice that ingest tiny bits of plastic can show signs of organ injury.
paras.zh: 我们生活在一个充满塑料的世界，其中大部分太小而看不见。这些由一次性水瓶、快餐盒和其他垃圾排出的微米和纳米塑料可以进入我们的身体。目前还不完全清楚这些碎片对我们的健康有何影响，但我们有一些提示。科学家们发现，人们动脉中的塑料颗粒会增加心脏病和中风的风险。摄入微小塑料碎片的老鼠会表现出器官损伤的迹象。

paras.en: Zeng’s team thought dietary fiber might provide some defense. Fiber forms a complex network of polymers that could trap ingested plastics like flies in a spider web, he says.
paras.zh: 曾的团队认为膳食纤维可能提供一些防御作用。他说，纤维形成了一个复杂的聚合物网络，可以像蜘蛛网上的苍蝇一样捕获摄入的塑料。

paras.en: The researchers put mice on low-, medium-, or high-fiber diets, then fed them plastic particles. Over the next 24 hours, the medium- and high-fiber groups of mice cleared more particles from their bodies than their low-fiber counterparts, the team discovered. That’s important, Zeng says, because these particles can do damage. After a week of daily plastic feedings, his team saw gut tissue damage — but only in the low-fiber group. Experiments in test tubes suggest that fiber physically wraps around and sticks to plastic particles.
paras.zh: 研究人员让老鼠吃低纤维、中纤维或高纤维饮食，然后喂它们塑料颗粒。研究小组发现，在接下来的 24 小时内，中纤维和高纤维组的小鼠比低纤维组的小鼠从体内清除了更多的颗粒。曾说，这很重要，因为这些颗粒会造成损害。经过一周的每日塑料喂养后，他的团队发现肠道组织受损——但仅限于低纤维组。试管实验表明，纤维以物理方式包裹并粘附在塑料颗粒上。

paras.en: It’s too soon to say if dietary fiber does the same in humans. Zeng’s study was performed in mice and not tethered to realistic fiber numbers. Though mice in the high-fiber group ate far more fiber than what what’s recommended for people, he thinks the findings are worth pursuing in follow-up studies.
paras.zh: 现在判断膳食纤维是否对人类有同样的作用还为时过早。曾的研究是在小鼠身上进行的，不受实际纤维数量的限制。尽管高纤维组的小鼠摄入的纤维远远多于推荐给人们的纤维，但他认为这些发现值得在后续研究中继续下去。

paras.en: And even if fiber doesn’t end up purging plastic from people’s guts, Zeng says, it probably wouldn’t hurt for us to add a little more to our diets.
paras.zh: 曾说，即使纤维最终不能清除人们肠道中的塑料，我们在饮食中多添加一点可能也不会有什么坏处。

articles.title: Drugs like Ozempic may help reverse chronic kidney disease
articles.author: Rachel Fairbank

paras.en: Ozempic’s key ingredient fixes faulty filters in the kidney.
paras.zh: Ozempic 的关键成分可以修复肾脏中出现故障的过滤器。

paras.en: The well-known weight loss drug repairs and restores blood vessels that power people’s waste disposal systems, researchers report October 1 in Nature Medicine. Those actions mean the ingredient, called semaglutide, can add another notch to its list of health benefits: treating chronic kidney disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 1 日在《自然医学》杂志上报道称，这种著名的减肥药可以修复和恢复为人们的废物处理系统提供动力的血管。这些作用意味着这种名为索马鲁肽的成分可以在其健康益处清单上再增加一个档次：治疗慢性肾病。

paras.en: In patients with the condition, semaglutide also increased blood flow and tamped down inflammation, the team found. The study reinforces the GLP-1 drug’s known anti-inflammatory effects, while also suggesting that it may play a direct role in protecting the kidney’s blood vessels, says Susan Quaggin, a nephrologist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine in Chicago who was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，对于患有这种疾病的患者，索马鲁肽还可以增加血流量并抑制炎症。芝加哥西北大学范伯格医学院的肾病学家 Susan Quaggin（未参与这项工作）表示，这项研究强化了 GLP-1 药物已知的抗炎作用，同时也表明它可能在保护肾脏血管方面发挥直接作用。

paras.en: Chronic kidney disease affects an estimated 674 million people worldwide, with some of the most common causes being diabetes and high blood pressure. As the disease progresses, the kidneys slowly lose their ability to filter out waste from blood and excrete it as urine. This causes other health complications, as well as a sharply increased risk of dying from a heart attack or stroke.
paras.zh: 据估计，慢性肾病影响着全球 6.74 亿人，其中一些最常见的原因是糖尿病和高血压。随着疾病的进展，肾脏慢慢失去过滤血液中废物并将其作为尿液排出体外的能力。这会导致其他健康并发症，以及死于心脏病或中风的风险急剧增加。
