articles.title: Milwaukee Tool Named Be Pro Be Proud Tool Partner
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Be Pro Be Proud has named Milwaukee Tool its exclusive National Tool Partner, bringing professional-grade tools and technology into interactive career exploration experiences designed to introduce students across the country to opportunities in the skilled trades.

Proud’s Mobile Workshops, virtual reality (VR) simulators and student recognition events. Students will gain exposure to the tools and technology used in skilled trades careers, including carpentry, electrical work, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), plumbing, water technology and diesel technology.

“A career feels real when a student can picture themselves doing the work,” said Andrew Parker, executive director of Be Pro Be Proud. “With Milwaukee Tool, we’re integrating industry-leading equipment into our Mobile Workshops, making career exploration more tangible and engaging while helping students envision a future in a high-demand technical profession.”

The investment will help enhance Be Pro Be Proud’s VR simulators, aligning the virtual tools students use with actual Milwaukee Tool products across six career modules. Milwaukee Tool equipment will also be integrated into Mobile Workshop experiences, including the National Mobile Workshop scheduled to launch in 2027.

The partnership will also extend to student recognition events, including Signing Days and Draft Days, where selected students will receive Milwaukee Tool products as they take the next steps toward careers in the skilled trades.

“The future of our industry depends on inspiring more young people to see what’s possible in the skilled trades,” said Scott Teson, senior vice president of Jobsite Solutions for Milwaukee Tool. “Milwaukee has built our business around understanding the people who work in these professions and developing solutions that help them succeed. Through Be Pro Be Proud, we’re helping students experience that innovation firsthand and discover rewarding career paths they may never have considered.”

The partnership builds on Milwaukee Tool’s broader commitment to strengthening America’s skilled trades workforce. The company expects to invest $200 million in U.S. skilled trades workforce development by 2030, supporting initiatives that introduce young people to the trades and help equip the next generation of skilled professionals.

Since launching in 2016, Be Pro Be Proud has reached more than 600,000 students nationally through its Mobile Workshops, which introduce students to technical careers across construction, manufacturing, transportation, and utilities.
For more information on Be Pro Be Proud, visit beprobeproud.org.

articles.title: Are You Following Proper Tire Mounting Procedures?
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: Proper tire mounting procedures can help prevent vibration, air loss, bead damage and damaged TPMS sensors. Technicians must understand their equipment, use approved lubrication and know where to apply pressure during mounting and demounting.
Rim clamp and pedestal tire changers require different mounting and demounting techniques. Technicians should follow the procedures specified for their equipment.

When breaking the bead away from the wheel, technicians should begin 90 or 180 degrees away from the valve stem or TPMS sensor. Applying pressure directly at the valve stem or sensor can cause damage and lead to an avoidable comeback.

Proper lubrication is also important. Technicians should apply an approved mounting lubricant to the tire bead to help it move smoothly along the wheel barrel. Insufficient lubrication is a common cause of bead damage during mounting and demounting.

The tire bead contains a metal band inside the tire’s inner lip. It creates the seal between the tire and wheel, allowing the assembly to hold air. Stretching, tearing or damaging this area can prevent the tire from sealing properly.
Tire Mounting Procedures for Bead Seating and Inspection
After the bead seats, technicians should fully deflate the tire before reinflating it to operating pressure. This allows the bead to settle evenly on the wheel and helps ensure proper tire centering.

Before mounting, technicians should clean the wheel surfaces and inspect the tire bead for existing damage. Driving while underinflated, rubbing curbs and hitting off-road obstacles can damage the bead before the vehicle reaches the shop.

Proper tire mounting requires technicians to follow equipment-specific procedures, protect TPMS sensors, apply sufficient approved lubricant and control inflation pressure. These steps help prevent tire damage and mounting-related problems.

articles.title: NHTSA Moves to Modernize Tire Testing Standards
articles.author: David Sickels

paras.en: The federal government is preparing to reconsider how tires are tested for safety, including laboratory procedures developed when passenger vehicles commonly rode on tall, bias-ply tires. Some of those testing methods remain part of federal regulations governing today’s low-profile radials, while emerging technologies such as airless tires present entirely different regulatory questions.

On October 26, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced plans to modernize federal tire safety standards, potentially launching the most significant overhaul of the regulations in more than two decades.
The agency is targeting tire strength, bead unseating resistance and endurance testing, along with tire sidewall markings, airless technology and load classifications for light-truck tires.

However, the agency isn’t proposing replacement requirements just yet. Instead, NHTSA plans to establish an advisory committee of up to 18 industry stakeholders and technical experts to develop recommendations for future rulemaking.
“As American tire technology and vehicle design continue to evolve, our regulatory framework must keep pace,” said NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison.

The agency says modernized standards could improve safety while reducing regulatory costs. Whether those changes ultimately expand tire availability, alter testing requirements or affect the information technicians rely on will depend on the regulations that emerge from the process.
Why Federal Tire Safety Standards Are Under Review
The push to modernize federal tire safety standards has been building for years.

The original federal tire safety regulations date to 1967, when bias-ply construction dominated the passenger tire market. Federal requirements subsequently evolved, most notably after Congress passed the Transportation Recall Enhancement, Accountability, and Documentation (TREAD) Act in 2000.

In 2003, NHTSA established Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 139, introducing more stringent high-speed and endurance testing, as well as low-inflation performance requirements for radial tires used on light vehicles.
As we reported at the time, the standard significantly expanded federal testing requirements, including coverage of P-metric and LT-metric radial tires. Its implementation concluded in 2007.

Still, some existing tests retained methods developed decades earlier. NHTSA revisited those procedures in a December 2019 regulatory review, asking whether they remained appropriate for modern tires.
One example is the tire strength test, also known as the plunger energy test.

The procedure presses a steel plunger into a mounted tire’s tread to evaluate its ability to withstand a specified energy level. But modern radial construction and lower-profile designs can complicate that measurement. NHTSA previously observed that the plunger sometimes reaches the wheel before the tire achieves the required test energy, particularly on low-profile tires.
That raises questions about how effectively the procedure measures the intended performance characteristic across today’s tire designs.

NHTSA also wants to reconsider bead unseating resistance testing, which measures the force required to dislodge a tire bead from the rim, and portions of the endurance test involving tread or sidewall chunking.
The agency has previously examined alternatives to existing strength and bead unseating tests but deferred changes pending additional research.
The October 27, 2026, Federal Register notice brings those longstanding issues back into formal consideration.
Tire Manufacturers Welcome the Proposed Changes
The U.S. Tire Manufacturers Association (USTMA) strongly endorsed NHTSA’s announcement.

“Outdated tire testing standards designed for the tires of the 1960s tell us nothing about whether today’s tires are safe,” said USTMA President and CEO Anne Forristall Luke in an October 26 statement.
The association argues that some existing requirements prevent American drivers from accessing newer tire technologies already available in other markets.
USTMA has previously urged regulators to reconsider testing methods that manufacturers contend provide limited safety benefits relative to their compliance burdens.

The distinction between maintaining meaningful performance requirements and eliminating outdated testing procedures will be central to the committee’s work. NHTSA must determine whether alternative methods can demonstrate appropriate safety performance while accommodating advances in tire construction.
The committee’s proposed agenda extends beyond traditional testing procedures.

One significant area involves non-pneumatic, or airless, tires. Unlike conventional designs, these tires do not depend on internal air pressure to support vehicle loads, creating challenges for regulations built around inflation pressure and pneumatic tire construction.
The issue is particularly relevant as manufacturers continue developing airless tires for potential use on passenger vehicles.
In a 2024 Tire Review interview, Michelin scientific and innovation communication director Cyrille Roget discussed the company’s Uptis airless tire prototype and its testing program.
Michelin had accumulated more than 2 million miles of testing at the time and was conducting pilot programs involving commercial delivery vehicles in Singapore and France.
Roget emphasized that Uptis remained a prototype at that point, with regulatory authorization necessary before wider on-road use.

NHTSA’s current initiative could help establish how technologies such as Uptis would be evaluated under future federal tire safety requirements. The agency has not yet outlined specific new testing procedures for non-pneumatic tires.
Another important issue involves Load Range F light-truck tires.
According to the Federal Register notice, the committee will consider a petition from the Tire and Rim Association to include Load Range F light-truck tires within FMVSS No. 139.
The proposed review could clarify how these higher-load-capacity tires fit within federal performance requirements as light-truck applications continue to evolve.
The agency has also identified inconsistencies involving inflation-pressure classifications.

In an August 2024 interpretation, NHTSA addressed questions from Goodyear about labeling Extra Load passenger tires with a maximum inflation pressure of 350 kPa, approximately 51 psi, and determining which strength-testing provisions applied.
NHTSA concluded that federal standards did not prohibit the proposed labeling and explained how the relevant test pressures would be determined.
The exchange illustrates the technical questions manufacturers encounter when applying established regulations to newer tire specifications.
What Tire Sidewall Changes Could Mean for Dealers
Modernizing tire markings could have particularly direct implications for tire service operations.
Sidewall information identifies construction characteristics, load capacity, inflation limits and other specifications technicians use when selecting, mounting, inflating and repairing tires.
The Tire Industry Association (TIA) has previously cautioned NHTSA against eliminating certain required markings.
As we reported in February 2020, TIA argued that removing ply-construction information from passenger and light-truck tire sidewalls could create safety concerns for technicians and motorists.

The association specifically emphasized the importance of identifying steel versus fabric sidewall plies when determining appropriate inflation procedures. It also supported retaining tubeless and tube-type markings to help prevent improper repairs.
TIA took a different position on the word radial, arguing that the existing tire size designation already communicates radial construction through the letter R.
Those comments concerned NHTSA’s earlier regulatory review and should not be interpreted as a new TIA response to the 2026 announcement.

NHTSA’s latest notice identifies tire markings as a topic for the advisory committee, although the agency plans a separate rulemaking to address specific requirements involving ply information, radial and tubeless markings, and certain inflation-pressure classifications.

For tire dealers, those distinctions are important. Changes that simplify manufacturer compliance must also account for the construction and identification information used during everyday tire service.
What Happens Next for Federal Tire Safety Standards

NHTSA plans to use a negotiated rulemaking process, bringing representatives of affected industries and technical organizations together to seek consensus before developing a formal regulatory proposal.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will appoint up to 18 committee members. The proposed composition includes four representatives from tire manufacturers or retailers, two from vehicle manufacturers, and additional members from manufacturing associations, safety organizations, research institutions and engineering or standards organizations.
NHTSA expects the committee to meet approximately four times annually and develop recommendations within its charter period, which can extend up to two years unless renewed.
Once the committee completes its work and the recommendations receive the necessary approvals, NHTSA intends to publish a notice of proposed rulemaking for public comment.
No new tire testing or labeling requirements have taken effect as a result of the October announcement. Existing federal standards remain in force.

NHTSA is accepting comments on the committee’s scope and proposed membership under Docket No. NHTSA-2026-1717 at Regulations.gov. The deadline for comments is November 27, 2026. Membership nominations must also be received by 5 p.m. Eastern on that date and may be submitted to [email protected].

articles.title: XL Parts, The Parts House Expands VIP Event Series
articles.author: Doug Kaufman

paras.en: XL Parts and The Parts House recently concluded its 2026 VIP Event Series with expanded programming across Houston, Dallas and Orlando.

“This year’s VIP Event Series represents a significant step forward in how we engage with our team, our vendor partners, and our customers,” said President and CEO Vikrant Aggarwal. “We have had the opportunity to create meaningful opportunities to align on strategic growth, strengthen industry relationships, and express our deep appreciation for the partners who drive our business forward.”

This year’s events introduced an upgraded two-day experience in both Houston and Orlando. The new structure provided dedicated time for internal strategy sessions, vendor showcases, formal awards ceremonies for employee-of-the-year honorees and supplier partners and customer-focused trade shows and appreciation dinners.

The series debuted Sept. 17-18 at The Woodlands Resort in Houston, TX, where XL Parts team members, vendor partners, and customers gathered for comprehensive product training, business development and vendor recognition.

It continued at The Shop Club in Dallas, TX, on September 24, where XL Parts says local shop owners and industry partners connected with suppliers over interactive exhibition booths, live entertainment, and multiple prizes.

The VIP event line-up concluded Oct. 1–2 at the Gaylord Palms Resort in Orlando, FL, where The Parts House (TPH) honored VIP customers and supplier partners through targeted product training, networking, and evening celebrations.

articles.title: Momentum USA Launches 77 Brake Part Numbers

articles.title: Replacing an Oil Filter Housing With an Integrated Oil Cooler
articles.author: Andrew Markel

paras.en: A leak at the oil filter housing isn’t limited to a gasket for its explanation. On many late-model import engines, the housing is part of a larger module that manages oil filtration and temperature, and may also contain sensors, thermostats and coolant passages.

Look at many late-model European engines and you’ll find an assembly bolted to the side of the block or mounted in the engine’s V. It may hold the oil filter and oil cooler, along with thermostats, valves or sensors. That arrangement helps fit more functions into a crowded engine compartment, but it can turn a straightforward oil leak into a more involved repair.

The design reflects two pressures on engine development: packaging and temperature control. Modern engines often use oil to operate variable valve timing systems and, in some engines, cylinder deactivation hardware. The oil must reach these components at the required pressure and volume, while staying within the engine’s operating temperature range.

Oil cooling has changed to meet those needs. Some older imports used an air-to-oil cooler mounted near the radiator, with oil routed through an adapter between the filter and its mounting base. Many later designs moved to a liquid-to-liquid cooler, often sandwiched between the engine and oil filter. Coolant warms the oil more quickly after a cold start and carries away heat once the oil is hot. Integrating the filter, cooler and related controls into a single module saves space and can simplify assembly.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A liquid-to-liquid cooler transfers heat between engine oil and coolant through plates or passages inside a compact heat exchanger. The fluids remain separate; heat moves through the metal between them. Because coolant can carry heat away efficiently in a relatively small space, the cooler can be packaged close to the engine without the airflow requirements of a front-mounted cooler.

Many designs use stacked plates to create a large heat-transfer area. That compact construction has a service tradeoff: narrow internal passages can retain debris. If a major engine failure sends metal fragments through the lubrication system, an oil change may not remove everything lodged in the cooler. Manufacturer guidance for some engine repairs calls for replacing the cooler and related components when bearing debris contaminates the oil circuit, because cleaning cannot reliably remove all of it.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Oil around the housing does not automatically mean that the housing itself has failed. The leak may come from the housing-to-engine seal, the cooler seals, the filter cap or another component above the assembly. Oil can travel down the engine and collect at the lowest point, making the source hard to identify.

Clean the area and inspect it closely. If necessary, use an approved leak-detection dye and re-check the engine after running it. Look for coolant residue as well as oil. A leak between the oil and coolant passages can cause contamination in either direction, depending on operating pressures and the failure. If the coolant is oily or the oil appears milky, diagnose the source before deciding what to replace.

Check the vehicle-specific service information before starting. The procedure may require draining coolant, removing intake or accessory components, or following a particular sequence to release the housing. Some assemblies include separate cooler seals; others are serviced as a unit. Check whether the manufacturer specifies replacement bolts, sealants, tightening sequences or a special coolant bleeding procedure.

Start with a cool engine. Drain the coolant if the service procedure calls for it, then disconnect electrical connectors and coolant hoses without stressing aged plastic fittings. Clean debris from around the assembly before opening the oil and coolant passages. Dirt that falls into an exposed passage can circulate through the engine.

Clean the engine’s sealing surface carefully. Avoid abrasive discs and aggressive scraping that can gouge or distort the surface. Keep debris out of the oil and coolant passages. If baked-on gasket material is difficult to remove, use a compatible gasket remover and a suitable non-damaging tool. Follow product directions and keep solvent out of the engine.

Install new seals in the correct locations and orientation. Lubricate them only if the service information calls for it. Tighten fasteners in the specified sequence and to the specified torque, using a torque wrench. Remember that uneven or excessive clamping force can distort a housing, damage a cooler or cause a new leak. Avoid adding sealant unless the procedure specifies it; excess sealant can squeeze into passages.
Address Contamination and Verify the Repair

If oil has entered the cooling system, replacing the failed cooler or housing may not be enough. Oil can remain in the radiator, heater core, hoses and expansion tank. Follow the vehicle manufacturer’s cleaning procedure and use only products approved for that cooling system. A 2025 service bulletin, for example, warns against using unvalidated detergents because they may damage seals or metal components. Replace contaminated parts when the prescribed procedure calls for it.

If coolant has entered the oil, change the oil and filter after the leak is repaired, and follow the manufacturer’s guidance on whether further oil changes or inspections are needed. If the engine has suffered a mechanical failure that released metal debris, do not assume flushing will make the cooler reusable. The passages can retain contamination that may return to the engine after startup.

Refill the fluids to the correct levels, and bleed the cooling system according to the application; some vehicles require a particular sequence or electronic procedure. Start the engine and check for leaks as it warms up. Confirm that the oil and coolant levels remain stable, then re-check the housing and surrounding area after a road test and cooldown.

articles.title: Static vs. Dynamic ADAS Calibrations
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: Choosing between static and dynamic ADAS calibration depends on the procedure specified by the vehicle manufacturer. Regardless of the method, the vehicle and its surroundings must meet the manufacturer’s requirements.
ADAS systems affected by a repair may need to be calibrated, relearned or re-zeroed. Terminology may vary, but the purpose is to establish an accurate reference point for the system.
A static calibration is performed while the vehicle remains stationary. Technicians position targets at exact distances and heights, and the targets must also be square to the vehicle’s centerline.
The vehicle must meet specified requirements for weight, ride height, tire pressure, fluid levels, lighting and background conditions.
Dynamic calibration takes place while driving. The technician places the system into calibration mode and drives the vehicle under specified conditions.
During the drive, the sensors verify that they can identify the roadway, recognize objects and align correctly with the vehicle’s centerline.
Extra weight, improper tire pressure, incorrect ride height or environmental interference can cause calibration to fail. These conditions can also establish an inaccurate reference.

Whether the procedure is static or dynamic, technicians must follow the manufacturer’s instructions exactly. ADAS calibration depends on precision, and even small inconsistencies can affect system performance.

articles.title: NTN Volunteer Event Supports Local Food Pantry
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: NTN Bearing Corp. of America held its Community Spirit & Engagement Event at the Elk Grove Township Food Pantry in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, on Tuesday, October 27. A team of twelve NTN employees volunteered to help combat food insecurity and support local families ahead of Thanksgiving.

Volunteers spent the morning assembling approximately 400 Thanksgiving food bags that will be distributed to families throughout the community. Designed as a “trick-or-treat” style shopping experience, team members worked together at various food stations, collecting and packing items including cooking oil, canned vegetables, canned pumpkin, mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese, gravy, brownie mix, and other household necessities.

In the afternoon, NTN employees assisted pantry staff with organizing and storing five pallets of donated food. According to the food pantry manager, the work completed by the NTN team in a few hours would have taken the pantry’s regular staff and volunteers up to a month to accomplish.

NTN’s Community Spirit & Engagement Program, launched in January 2023, includes contributing time and resources to charitable organizations, encouraging employees to take an active role in the local community, and building partnerships with other groups and organizations.

The Elk Grove Township Food Pantry provides food assistance and related support services to residents facing food insecurity, serving approximately 1,100 families each month through a client-choice model that allows households to access nutritious food and household essentials in a dignified and convenient manner. Through partnerships with community organizations, donors, and volunteers, the pantry helps ensure local families have access to the resources they need throughout the year and is expected to distribute the Thanksgiving food bags assembled during the event to nearly 900 families this holiday season.

articles.title: Clarios Expands hAGM Battery Technology
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: Clarios is expanding its hAGM technology platform across future original-equipment programs and the aftermarket. The expansion addresses growing demands on low-voltage energy systems in modern vehicles.

Vehicles across powertrain types are becoming increasingly connected, software-enabled and electrically intensive. More electronic control units, safety features, connectivity systems and energy-management functions increase the importance of the 12-volt battery. These systems also increase the battery’s role in vehicle reliability, performance and reducing battery-related warranty risks.
Modern vehicles also rely on the 12-volt battery to support electronic systems and important functions while parked.
Clarios Develops hAGM for Increasing Electrical Demands
Clarios developed hAGM as the next evolution of absorbent glass mat (AGM) battery technology to address these changing requirements.

Building on established AGM technology, hAGM supports improved dynamic charge acceptance and reliable operation under demanding conditions. These conditions include higher electrical loads, repeated cycling, extended parking periods and growing dependence on electronic systems.
These capabilities support faster energy recovery during short charging periods, improved cycling performance and vehicle efficiency under real-world operating conditions.
Automakers Select hAGM for Future Vehicle Programs

Multiple leading global automakers have selected Clarios’ hAGM technology for high-volume future vehicle programs. Production for previously announced programs will begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
An additional global automaker has also selected Clarios to supply hAGM technology for future vehicle programs. This agreement further expands the technology’s OEM pipeline.

“The role of the 12-volt battery is changing as vehicle architectures become increasingly sophisticated,” said Federico Morales-Zimmermann, vice president and general manager of global OEM customers and technology at Clarios. “The selection of hAGM for future vehicle programs demonstrates that automakers are preparing for higher electrical demands with technology designed to support improved dynamic charge acceptance, enhanced cycling performance and reliable operation under real-world conditions.”

The recently introduced OPTIMA REDTOP with hAGM+ technology builds on the Clarios hAGM technology foundation. Clarios developed the product for premium aftermarket applications. The battery supports demanding operating conditions, including higher electrical loads, frequent cycling, extensive accessory usage and modern electrical-system requirements.

“The technology trends shaping future vehicles will also shape the replacement market,” said Marc Andraca, president of U.S. and Canada Region at Clarios. “OPTIMA REDTOP with hAGM+ technology helps aftermarket partners and vehicle owners prepare for the more demanding battery requirements that increasingly sophisticated vehicles will bring.”
The expanding OEM program pipeline and new OPTIMA REDTOP demonstrate how Clarios is applying its low-voltage technology across both markets.

Clarios and OPTIMA highlighted the hAGM technology platform during AAPEX and SEMA in Las Vegas.

The companies provided customers and industry stakeholders information about changing low-voltage energy requirements. They also highlighted the connection between future vehicle technology and replacement-market demand.

articles.title: The 45-Day Rule: How Parts Stores Stop Financing Their Customers
articles.author: Bob Morgan

paras.en: Every parts store has an account like this. The shop buys a lot. The owner is a good guy. He pays — eventually. Meanwhile he’s 50 to 90 days out and asking for another special order “by Thursday.”

Here’s the hard truth I learned after about 15 years running stores on Long Island: volume you don’t collect isn’t volume. It’s a loan you never approved. Most stores aren’t short on sales. They’re short on cash because they’re quietly running a bank for their customers, with the special-order desk as the loan window.
The fix isn’t a collections agency or a nasty letter. It’s one rule, written down and used every single time.
If an account is 45 or more days past due and they want a special order, the special waits until the money is in the building.
That’s it. Shelf stock can still go out for cash. The relationship stays intact. But you stop ordering non-returnable, hard-to-restock parts for an account that hasn’t paid for the last batch.

Why special orders? A stocked part sold on account is a receivable. A special order for a slow-paying account is a receivable plus freight, a restocking fee and a part you may end up owning if the job falls through. That’s where slow accounts do the most damage, so that’s where the line goes.

Before the rule works, everyone at the counter has to agree on what “45 days” means. I count days past the due date, not days since the invoice. A Net 30 invoice dated June 12 is due July 12. On September 2, it’s 52 days past due — over the line.

If you’d rather age from the invoice date, fine. Pick one method, write it on the rule and never switch mid-argument. If your company already has a hold policy, use its number. The discipline matters more than the exact day.
The 45-day rule works because nobody gets surprised by it. The steps before it do the heavy lifting:
- Day 30 — a reminder, not a threat. “Invoice 1844 is at 30. Card or check on the next stop?”
- Day 35–40 — a human call. Not another statement they’re already ignoring. A person, by name, on the phone.
- Day 45 — credit hold for new specials. Shelf can still be cash. Specials wait.
- Day 60 — hard hold. No “just this once” unless a manager puts the amount and the date in writing.
Most accounts never reach day 45 once the day-30 and day-35 touches actually happen. The rule is the backstop, not the first move.
Give your counter people the exact words. Nobody should improvise a credit conversation with a regular at the register. At day 45:
“I can keep selling you what’s here if we’re cash. I can’t put another special in motion until 1844 is clear. I need you current so I can keep saying yes.”
“I like working with you. I can’t keep shipping on a 60-day balance. Let’s pick an amount for this week and a date for the rest. Until that starts, we’re cash.”
Those lines don’t threaten and don’t apologize. They state the rule and offer a path back. “I need you current so I can keep saying yes” puts you and the customer on the same side.

The most common way the rule breaks: “I’m not paying until you fix that core credit.” Freeze the one disputed line and research it. The rest of the balance is still due. Don’t let a $40 question hold up a $4,000 balance.
And if yelling breaks the rule, you’ve just taught every shop in town that yelling works. The rule has to hold for your biggest account, too.
A rule nobody checks turns into a suggestion. Once a week — I do it in a short Monday meeting — pull your aging and look at three things:
- Total dollars 45+ and 60+ days past due.
- A name and a next-call date next to every one of those accounts.
- Any special order that went out to a 45+ account, and who approved it.

A simple example (invented numbers): a store has $6,940 at 45+ days past due across two accounts. A fleet account on that list calls for a special. The counter person checks the list and uses the day-45 line. The special gets placed the afternoon the check clears. No fight, no exception, and the store isn’t fronting more parts to a customer who already owes $4,200.
- Export or write down your current aging.
- Highlight everything 45+ and 60+ days past due.
- Put a name and a next-call date on every one.
- Write the special-order rule on a sticky note at the counter where everyone can see it.
You can like the shop. You can need the volume. You still collect. The 45-day rule is how a parts store stops financing its customers and gets back to selling them parts.

articles.title: APA’s Gatsby Gala Brings Roaring ’20s Glamour to AAPEX
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: Automotive Parts Associates (APA) brought a touch of Roaring ’20s glamour to this year’s AWDA and AAPEX festivities with its annual industry cocktail party. This year’s party, The Gatsby Gala, was held November 3, 2026, at 1923 Prohibition Bar in Las Vegas.

Guests stepped back in time for an evening of drinks, networking, and old-school elegance. Adding to the occasion, APA staff dressed in 1920s-inspired attire, helping bring the spirit of the Jazz Age to life at the Prohibition-era venue.

“One of the best parts of AWDA and AAPEX is the opportunity to bring people together outside of the day-to-day business. The Gatsby Gala gave us a chance to celebrate the relationships that make this industry special while enjoying a memorable evening with our shareholders, members and supplier partners,” said Steve Tucker, president of Automotive Parts Associates.

The evening brought together APA shareholders, TruStar members, NEXUS representatives, and industry supplier partners for an opportunity to connect with fellow aftermarket professionals, strengthen existing relationships, and enjoy a night away from the busy trade show floor.

The Gatsby Gala carried on APA/TruStar’s tradition of hosting an annual gathering during one of the busiest weeks in the automotive aftermarket. Beyond the party, APA also held a dinner for its Board of Directors on Saturday night and met with more than 70 supplier partners during AWDA and on the AAPEX show floor.

articles.title: 'Links with the British royal family would eventually prove crucial': How DNA solved the 70-year mystery of what happened to the executed members of the last Russian imperial family
articles.author: Turi King

paras.en: In 1917, the Russian Revolution was in full swing. Tsar Nicholas II had abdicated, and he and his family were exiled to a remote Siberian town. There were plans to get the family to the U.K., but King George V (Nicholas' first cousin) and the British government withdrew their offer of asylum over concerns of the ramifications.

After the Russian Provisional Government was overthrown by the more extreme Bolsheviks in October 1917, Nicholas, his wife, their children and several members of the family's staff were moved to Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg, where, in July 1918, they were executed. Their bodies were hidden and remained lost to time for nearly a century — until modern technology, with some help from the British royal family, unraveled the fascinating story of their disappearance.

In this excerpt from "The Secrets of Our DNA: How Genetics Has Changed the World" (Pegasus Books, 2026), author Turi King, director of the Center for Evolution at the University of Bath, looks back at the incredible story of how DNA was used to solve a major mystery of modern history: What happened to the last members of the House of Romanov?

I was sitting in a lecture theatre at Cambridge University in 1994 when one of my lecturers, Erika Hagelberg, spoke about a new study she had just been involved in. It was the first major case to combine both mitochondrial DNA and DNA fingerprinting to identify human remains: those of the Russian imperial family.
But first I need to take you back to Russia in 1917 and the abdication of the tsar following the Russian Revolution.

The Russian royal family, the Romanovs, had been the reigning imperial dynasty since 1617, and three centuries later, Tsar Nicholas II was on the throne. Nicholas was the cousin of George V, king of the United Kingdom, their mothers being sisters, and had married George's cousin Princess Alix (Alexandra) of Hesse, who was apparently Queen Victoria's favourite grandchild. Nicholas and Alix had five children, four daughters (Olga, Tatiana, Maria and Anastasia) and a son, Alexei.

The tsar and his wife were not well liked by the Russian population and political unrest culminated in the revolution of 1917, when Nicholas was forced to abdicate. The family were kept under house arrest and in 1918 they were moved to Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg with the royal physician, Dr Botkin, and three of their staff. On the night of 16 July, the family, their doctor and staff were herded into the cellar together and executed. Their bodies were then taken to a secret location and placed in a hastily dug communal grave, doused in sulphuric acid in an attempt to disfigure them and hinder identification, and then covered over, the location of the grave being lost for more than 70 years.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Ironically, the new Russian government had wanted to get the Romanovs out of Russia due to the risk of their becoming a rallying point, but a plan to grant asylum to the Romanovs in the U.K. because of their links with the British royal family fell through, owing to a reluctance on the part of George V to grant it. Yet those links with the British royal family would eventually prove crucial in their identification.

Fast-forward to 1991, when several skeletons were found in a shallow grave some 20 miles from Yekaterinburg. Many of the bones were badly damaged but it was possible to determine, based on examination of the skeletal remains, that there were nine individuals — two short of the 11 killed that night. The faces of the skulls were badly damaged in all of the skeletons, all of them showing evidence of violence either in the form of bullet holes or bayonet wounds or both. Before the genetic study, Russian forensic scientists had used numerous techniques alongside historical data to tentatively identify the remains as some of the members of the Russian royal family, their doctor and servants.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: These included examining the bones, to determine approximate age and sex, and some of the teeth, the expensive dental work, incorporating gold, platinum and porcelain, indicating that certain remains must belong to members of an aristocratic family. The team worked out that the two missing individuals would have been two of the children, one of the daughters (while it was hard to determine which one it would be, given how close in age they were, it was thought that it was either Maria or Anastasia) and the son, Prince Alexei.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The Russian chief forensic medical examiner then contacted a team in the U.K., which included Erika, to see if genetic evidence could be used to confirm the identification. The U.K. team used the amelogenin genetic sex test, now part of standard forensic DNA testing, which confirmed the sex of the skeletons (four male and five female bodies), while an early form of DNA profiling showed that there was a family group here — two parents and three children — and four unrelated individuals. So far, so good.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Next, they needed to prove that this was the Russian royal family, and they did this using mitochondrial DNA analysis. As you'll remember, mitochondrial DNA is passed down by a mother to all her children, male and female, but only daughters can pass it on — so if female-line family members of Tsar Nicholas and Tsarina Alexandra could be found and would agree to give a DNA test, their mitochondrial DNA should match that of their royal ancestors. It just so happened that the late Prince Philip, husband of the late Queen Elizabeth, was related to the tsarina through the female line: she was his great-aunt, his maternal grandmother being the sister of the tsarina. He kindly gave a DNA sample.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The testing that they did was standard for the time in that they looked at two regions known as hypervariable regions 1 and 2 (HVR1 and HVR2). You'll remember that mitochondrial DNA has 37 rather crucial genes on it where any "typo" that occurs as the DNA is being copied could have serious consequences if the mutation is deleterious. By contrast, in those parts of the mitochondrial genome that don't code for anything, such as these two hypervariable regions, mutations can occur more freely without necessarily causing issues, meaning that these regions contain much more genetic variation. These are the sections of mitochondrial DNA that scientists began analysing for identification purposes. While it's not as precise as DNA profiling because many thousands of people will all have the same mitochondrial DNA type, it can be very helpful in a case such as this.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: When the team sequenced these two regions, Prince Philip's mitochondrial DNA was found to match that of the putative remains of the tsarina and her daughters. Next they found two living female-line relatives of the tsar, descended from his maternal grandmother: a great-great-niece, Princess Xenia Cheremeteff Sfiris, and a first cousin twice removed, James Carnegie, 3rd Duke of Fife. The mitochondrial DNA from these two matched each other perfectly, and they, in turn, matched that of the tsar, except at one base where there was both a match and a mismatch.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: This is because the tsar had what's known as a heteroplasmy at this position: some of the mitochondrial DNA sequences showed a T and others showed a C, his maternal relatives showing a T. Heteroplasmy is known to take place primarily through mutations occurring when the DNA is copied to make new cells in a person's lifetime, but it can be inherited from a maternal ancestor with heteroplasmy. Extremely rarely, it can come from paternal mitochondrial DNA making it into the cell. So the fact that heteroplasmy existed in the DNA sample didn't negate the match, and the probability that these were the Romanovs was still between 70 to 1 through to 840,000 to 1 in favour. But, it did sow some seeds of doubt. Incidentally, we now know that heteroplasmy is fairly common, with potentially over half of the human population having at least one heteroplasmy, albeit at a low percentage in terms of their mitochondrial DNA carrying it.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

- When a battery dies, you replace it — how jumpstarting cells with fresh mitochondria could revolutionize medicine
- Author Lise Barnéoud on the bizarre and provoking world of microchimerism — when cells from one person live in another, genetically distinct individual

So, to be doubly sure, in 1996 the remains of the tsar's brother, Georgij, who had died in 1899, were exhumed and he was found to have exactly the same mitochondrial heteroplasmy. Given the very low chance of two people having this particular heteroplasmy if they weren't related, this pointed to the mitochondrial DNA data the researchers obtained being 130,000,000 times more likely if these were the Romanovs than if they were an unrelated family.

The case was solved in terms of identifying the tsar, tsarina and three of their daughters, but the mystery still remained as to what had happened to the two other children. In the scientific paper reporting the results, the authors conjectured that possibly the two children had been buried separately, or that they could have survived the massacre. Incidentally, there was a woman living in the U.S. who claimed to be Anastasia, saying she had managed to escape being executed, and so the fact that two of the children were missing from the Romanov family group only fuelled the idea that maybe she truly was the missing princess.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Then, in 2007, a group of amateur archaeologists, digging a mere 70 metres away from the previously discovered mass grave, came across more human remains. Skeletal evidence showed that they were the remains of two bodies, a young woman aged 15-19 and a probable male aged 12-15. DNA analysis was brought to bear and again showed that the two individuals were siblings and related to the Romanovs already identified. As an extra DNA test, Y-chromosome testing was carried out, the Y chromosome being passed from father to son, to confirm that the Y chromosome of the newly found male skeleton was indeed male and that it matched the Y chromosome of the tsar. This also then matched male-line relatives — a second cousin once removed of the tsar (third cousin of Alexei) through Tsar Nicholas I. The missing Romanov children had been found.

From an award-winning expert on DNA, discover the myth-busting book that opens a dazzling window into the world of modern genetics.
Fascinating, compassionate, and entirely captivating, The Secrets of Our DNA is the essential book that explains how genetics has changed and transformed the world around us.

Turi King is renowned for presenting complex findings on DNA and genetic science in an accessible and compelling way and she has won awards for her public engagement in science. Turi is the director of the Milner Centre for Evolution at the University of Bath. She is an honorary fellow of the British Science Association, a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London, a member of the Chartered Society of Forensic Sciences, and a member of the International Society of Forensic Geneticists. She is well known for her academic work leading the identification of Richard III; advising on the case of Mary Jane Kelly (the last victim of Jack the Ripper); leading the project on sequencing Hitler’s genome; as well as her media work co-presenting BBC’s DNA Family Secrets.

articles.title: Which animal farts the most?
articles.author: Clarissa Brincat

paras.en: Flatology, the study of flatulence, sounds more like a joke than a serious scientific discipline. But studying farts actually helps biologists understand an animal's diet and digestion.
We know that a host of creatures — from whales, to snakes, to sloths — pass gas. But do we know which animal is the top tooter? Experts told Live Science the answer is blowing in the wind.

"Getting quantitative measurements for farts per animal is pretty difficult," Nick Caruso, a data scientist and co-author of '"Does It Fart?: The Definitive Field Guide to Animal Flatulence'' (Quercus Publishing, 2017), told Live Science in an email.

What we can do is hypothesize using the data we do have. Expelled gas is made partially of methane, so comparing methane emissions produced by different species may provide a clue. However, this method does have limitations, experts pointed out.

Researchers measure the methane animals produce by placing them inside respiration chambers, then inserting a capsule into the stomach that releases a tracer gas while strapping them with a harness that samples their breath. Alternatively, they capture their breath at stations where they feed or are milked.

Research points to livestock, especially cows, as major methane emitters. A recent report puts their total methane emissions at 117 teragrams per year. (One teragram is equal to 1 billion kilograms, or 2.2 billion pounds.) A buildup of cow-generated methane gas even caused a dairy shed in Germany to explode. However, contrary to what many people believe, the "overwhelming majority" of methane emissions from livestock is released through burping, not flatulence, Ermias Kebreab, a professor of animal science at the University of California, Davis, told Live Science in an email.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The reason comes down to where in the gut the gas is made. Herbivores can't break down plant material on their own; they rely on microbes in their guts to ferment it, and that fermentation releases gases such as methane and carbon dioxide, Dr. Marcus Clauss, head of research and co-director of the Clinic for Zoo Animals, Exotic Pets and Wildlife at the University of Zurich, told Live Science in an email. Some of this gas is absorbed into the bloodstream and exhaled. The rest tends to leave by the nearest exit — animals that ferment their food toward the front of the digestive tract mostly burp it out, while those that ferment it toward the back mostly pass it as wind, Clauss explained.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Feed your curiosity with an exclusive mystery every week, solved with science and delivered direct to your inbox before it's seen anywhere else.

Cows and other ruminants (such as buffalo, sheep, goats and camels) ferment their food in a chamber called the rumen, located near the front of the digestive system, so most of the methane they produce is through belching, Matthew Hayek, an associate professor of environmental studies at New York University, told Live Science in an email.

So if it's not cows, which animal is the top farter based on their methane emissions? The best candidates are hindgut fermenters — herbivores that digest plant matter in the large intestine (the hindgut). Meat eaters, by contrast, typically produce far less methane than herbivores do, Clauss said.

One possible contender are termites, which break down wood and grass in their hindguts. Their global population is estimated to be around 27 quadrillion (that's 15 zeros) individuals, and they collectively emit 10 teragrams of methane per year.

But, per individual, the title might go to horses. According to a 2019 report from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, horses have the highest methane emissions among hindgut fermenters — around 40 pounds (18 kg) of methane per horse each year.

However, Clauss is skeptical. "The ranking of horse as highest is only because it has been measured," he told Live Science in an email. "But there are so many hindgut fermenters not measured, like rhino ... Who knows?"
If we consider methane emissions per unit of bodyweight, the nutria (Myocastor coypus) — an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent — would have higher methane emissions than the horse, Clauss said.

Clauss also questioned the accuracy of using methane emissions data as an indicator of flatulence. "There is some methane in flatulence, but most likely the majority of methane produced by an animal is exhaled, i.e. it goes via blood to the lungs," he said.

So until scientists figure out how to measure animal farts, any ranking remains speculative. For now, scientists have developed ways to track intestinal gas in people, including swallowable electronic capsules that measure gases inside the gut and clip-on underwear sensors that detect hydrogen in farts.
Does animal flatulence contribute to climate change?

Methane is a particularly potent greenhouse gas when released into the atmosphere, and the quantities that large herds of cows and other ruminants emit through burping are enough to contribute to climate change. Indeed, scientists are experimenting with ways to reduce methane emissions from cattle — for example, by adding seaweed to their diet.
But animal flatulence is not a major contributor to global methane increases, Hayek said.

Even methane emissions from termite flatulence, while large, do not have an impact, Stefan Arndt, a professor of physiological and ecosystem ecology at the University of Melbourne in Australia, told Live Science in an email. "A large proportion of that methane is then consumed by methanotrophic bacteria in the soil," he said. These bacteria use methane as an energy source, thereby reducing the net methane emissions from termites substantially.

"Their emissions are part of the natural cycle of methane that has always been there for millennia," Arndt added. "The increasing methane concentrations in the atmosphere that are leading to climate change are caused by humans."

Clarissa Brincat is a freelance writer specializing in health and medical research. After completing an MSc in chemistry, she realized she would rather write about science than do it. She learned how to edit scientific papers in a stint as a chemistry copyeditor, before moving on to a medical writer role at a healthcare company. Writing for doctors and experts has its rewards, but Clarissa wanted to communicate with a wider audience, which naturally led her to freelance health and science writing. Her work has also appeared in Medscape, HealthCentral and Medical News Today.

articles.title: 'Flames soon engulfed us': Artemis II astronaut Jeremy Hansen describes his mission's riskiest moment
articles.author: John Larsen

paras.en: After nine days in space, the four crewmembers of NASA's Artemis II mission looked out their capsule window on April 10, 2026, and saw the bright-blue Earth below them. The crew had traveled more than 250,000 miles (400,000 kilometers) from our planet — farther from Earth than any humans had ever gone — and now, home was just a few hundred miles straight down.

Only one milestone remained: splashdown, a fast and fiery plunge into the Pacific Ocean that would mark the end of humanity's first crewed mission to the moon in more than 50 years.Mission specialist Jeremy Hansen, the lone Canadian Space Agency astronaut on the crew, had every reason to be confident that the team's Orion crew capsule would hold up just fine. But this was Hansen's first time in space, and his first time dropping through the sky like a fireball at 24,600 mph (39,600 kmh).

It wasn't that he was afraid for himself, Hansen explains in "Earthrise: Inside Artemis II, the Groundbreaking Human Mission into Deep Space" (Hanover Square Press, 2026), which he co-wrote with John Larsen). Rather, he knew that his wife Catherine and three children would be among the millions of Earthlings watching the most dangerous moment of his mission from below.
In this excerpt from the book, Hansen describes the thrilling intensity of splashdown and the euphoria of knowing that he and his crewmates were going to make it back safely — and make history.

Immediately after jettisoning the European Service Module, and exactly half an hour before we were due to splashdown, Mission Control initiated the crew module raise burn. This nineteen-second burn was the first and only burn using the small thrusters built into our Orion capsule. It slightly shallowed our entry trajectory to put us right in the sweet spot while also providing some added distance from the service module, as we'd be hitting the atmosphere in near succession. It, too, went flawlessly. I tightened my straps; it was time for the fireworks.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A re-entry into the Earth's atmosphere is absolutely on the short list of the most incredible experiences of my life. We slammed into it at 7:53 p.m., thundering down at over 10 kilometres [6.2 miles] per second. Per second.

The thrusters fired almost constantly to stabilize the capsule: loud thuds, as if Thor himself were hammering on our spacecraft, as the G-forces quickly began to build, aggressively scrubbing off the velocity we had added to our rocket nine days earlier. Within seconds, we saw plasma forming outside our windows, and the heat at the base of our capsule grew so intense that flames soon engulfed us. It started red and transformed into a bright, bluish-green, pulsating light. It was breathtaking, the bright colors igniting our senses.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It was insane to think about what we were doing. We all knew how this worked; we all knew the science. But deep inside, I also recognized that astronauts must have a screw loose to do this. Nobody in their right mind would strap themselves inside a metal canister that itself was sitting inside a giant fireball. But there was no other way down, and I had accepted the realities of this journey long in advance.

Although I was at peace, I felt guilty for the stress I was putting on my family. I had talked to them openly about the mission's risks, and this was the highest-risk moment. I tried to send my love telepathically, telling them it was going great.

As we continued our freefall, it looked like a thousand camera flashes were exploding inside Integrity. I lowered the sun visor on my helmet. There were only centimeters of heatshield and aluminum separating me from the more than 2500°C heat outside. Almost instantly, the heat inside our cramped home also began to rise, an increase that engineers refer to as "thermally benign." All I know is that I couldn't feel it, blissfully wrapped in my thermally controlled garments.

As we continued to fall, the G-forces built up to nearly four times the pressure we feel on Earth. I wasn't too worried, having endured more than five minutes of the same G-force, or more, in the NASA centrifuge trainer. I had half-expected the freefall back to Earth to seem short, but it was a long six minutes before the flames finally ceased and we re-established communications with Mission Control.
It had already been a wild ride, but I also knew another crazy part — parachute deployment and the actual splashdown — lay ahead. My adrenalin kept pumping.
"Integrity, Houston. Comms check, post-blackout," we heard from Mission Control. It was music to our ears. It was exactly 8:00 p.m.
"Houston, Integrity," Reid [Wiseman, mission commander], replied. "We have you loud and clear."

This is when people the world over clapped, hugged, and, in some cases, cried. For the folks at NASA, it was clear that all had gone well during the descent — a small fleet of NASA and Air Force planes had captured it on high-resolution cameras. But, for me, it wasn't over yet. I wouldn't truly feel safe until our three main parachutes successfully deployed. If they didn't, we'd be a chunk of metal slamming into the ocean at incredibly high speed, and the chances of surviving that would be somewhere between minimal and non-existent.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: I've watched many of my close friends return from space, and I find the minutes after surviving the re-entry heat until the parachutes deploy to be the hardest part to watch. When I see a capsule plunge through the clouds with no chutes, I always worry they might not appear at all. That's completely terrifying.

I thought of Catherine and the kids, sending them a "don't worry, gang" message in my mind. Catherine later told me that she had a very bad feeling about the heatshield, so when we emerged from blackout, she began crying and didn't even focus on the parachutes.

Three minutes later, at an altitude of 7,100 metres, timed explosions released small chutes that pulled off the cover for two larger chutes, called drogues because they are intended to slow our acceleration to a speed that would allow our main parachutes to open without ripping. They did their job perfectly, but it was wild inside the capsule, jerking us back and forth like a ride at the fair.

One minute later, at only 1,500 metres above the ocean, the drogue chutes cut loose, and, for a few moments, we felt like we were falling backward. Then, in succession, the three main parachutes began deploying, blossoming slowly so they wouldn't tear apart. The rate of our fall slowed as the red-and-white nylon canopies, each 35 metres in diameter, filled with air. The thrusters kept firing, aiming the capsule's base directly toward the point of impact.
- 'We're not a competitor to fusion. We are fusion': Inside the race to harness unlimited solar power in space
- 'Everything we know about space travel is going to change within a decade': The fusion breakthrough that could unlock a path to the stars
- 'We only expect to encounter that once every 130 years': A huge new crater on the moon could mean a giant leap for lunar science
"Integrity, we see three good-looking parachutes," we heard from our CAPCOM. Within seconds, our splashdown speed had reduced to 27 kilometres per hour.
That's it, I said to myself. I'm pretty sure we can survive whatever else could be thrown at us now.
Christina [Koch, mission specialist] seemed to agree. We grabbed one another's hands in a moment of celebration.

The dramatic, high-stakes account of Artemis II, the first human journey into deep space in fifty years, told from the perspective of astronaut Jeremy Hansen ... A riveting and intimate account of the iconic achievement of Artemis II, Earthrise—written by author John Larsen and based on extensive interviews he conducted with Hansen—is a testament to what can be achieved with unity, teamwork, and a bold belief in humanity’s ability to reach for the stars.

John Larsen is a former executive-level military public affairs officer who served with the Royal Canadian Air Force during combat operations in Europe. Based in Calgary, AB, he is a business advisor, entrepreneur, writer, and university instructor. He holds graduate degrees in Communications and in Creative Non-Fiction Writing. Earthrise is his second book.

articles.title: Global Fossil Fuel Emissions Are Expected to Drop This Year, Partly Because of the Conflicts in Iran and Ukraine

paras.en: In 2020, humans hunkered down amid the Covid-19 pandemic, contributing to an unprecedented 7 percent decrease in global fossil fuel emissions, according to the Global Carbon Project, an international collaboration that releases annual reports on emissions trends. For the first time since then, emissions are expected to fall again, although to a lesser degree.
paras.zh: 根据发布年度排放趋势报告的国际合作组织全球碳项目的数据，2020年，人类在新冠疫情中蛰伏下来，导致全球化石燃料排放量史无前例地下降了7%。自那以后，预计排放量将首次再次下降，尽管降幅较小。

paras.en: Global Carbon Project researchers predict that in 2026, countries will have emitted 42.1 billion U.S. tons of planet-warming carbon dioxide, a 0.4 percent decrease compared with the previous year. That’s partly because of growing solar and wind power, but also a surge in oil prices and supply chain issues sparked by the United States-Israel war with Iran.
paras.zh: 全球碳项目研究人员预测，2026年，各国将排放421亿美国吨导致全球变暖的二氧化碳，比上一年减少0.4%。这部分是因为太阳能和风能发电的增长，但也与美国-以色列对伊朗的战争引发的油价飙升和供应链问题有关。

paras.en: The team described these findings in a preprint report, which has not been peer-reviewed, released on November 10 in the journal Earth System Data Science. Some of the scientists also published an analysis in the journal Nature Climate Change.
paras.zh: 该团队在11月10日发表于《地球系统数据科学》期刊上的一份预印本报告中介绍了这些发现，该报告尚未经过同行评审。一些科学家还在《自然气候变化》杂志上发表了一篇分析文章。

paras.en: “A decline in fossil [carbon dioxide] emissions is encouraging, but a reduction driven partly by geopolitical shocks is not a sustainable climate solution,” says report and study co-author Pierre Friedlingstein, a climate scientist at the University of Exeter in England, in a statement. “The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies. While renewables and electric vehicles are increasingly offsetting growth in energy demand, further acceleration is needed if global emissions are to peak and enter a sustained decline.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: According to Friedlingstein and colleagues’ calculations, emissions from oil and gas are projected to decline this year by 1.9 and 0.3 percent, respectively. However, that’s partially offset by a 0.6 percent rise in emissions from coal. (Burning coal generates more pollution than oil or gas.)
paras.zh: 根据弗里德林施泰因及其同事的计算，今年石油和天然气的排放量预计将分别下降1.9%和0.3%。然而，煤炭排放量增加了0.6%，部分抵消了这一降幅。（燃烧煤炭产生的污染比石油或天然气更多。）

paras.en: Did you know? Atmospheric methane surged
paras.zh: 您知道吗？大气甲烷含量飙升

paras.en: In 2020, levels of methane—the second-largest contributor to climate change—surprisingly spiked. Earlier this year, researchers reported that the unexpected surge was caused by dynamics in the atmosphere and natural sources of the gas, including wetlands.
paras.zh: 2020年，甲烷（气候变化的第二大影响因素）的含量出乎意料地飙升。今年早些时候，研究人员报告称，这种意外飙升是由大气动力学和包括湿地在内的天然气源造成的。

paras.en: China emits around one-third of the world’s fossil emissions, making it the country that produces the most carbon dioxide. This year, its emissions declined overall, despite a small bump in coal pollution. That’s likely because China is leading the clean energy transition—it’s responsible for half of global emissions avoided due to renewable energy and electric vehicles.
paras.zh: 中国排放的化石燃料二氧化碳约占全球总量的三分之一，是二氧化碳排放量最多的国家。今年，尽管煤炭污染略有增加，但其排放量总体上有所下降。这很可能是因为中国正在引领清洁能源转型——由于可再生能源和电动汽车的使用，全球减排量的一半要归功于中国。

paras.en: In the United States, which follows China as a polluter, researchers predict a 1.3 percent decrease in emissions in 2026. That’s mainly thanks to a decrease in coal emissions following a spike last year due to high natural gas prices and cold weather.
paras.zh: 在美国，该国是仅次于中国的污染大国，研究人员预测2026年的排放量将减少1.3%。这主要归功于去年因天然气价格高企和寒冷天气而导致煤炭排放量激增后有所下降。

paras.en: Emissions from the rest of the world are projected to decline by 0.7 percent, driven largely by lower oil use.
paras.zh: 在很大程度上由于石油使用量减少，预计世界其他地区的排放量将下降0.7%。

paras.en: “I would call it unexpected,” says study and report co-author Glen Peters, a climate scientist at the Center for International Climate Research in Norway, to Brad Plumer at the New York Times. “It’s pretty rare to see a drop in oil demand this big.”
paras.zh: “我会称之为出乎意料。”挪威国际气候研究中心的气候科学家、研究和报告的合著者格伦·彼得斯（Glen Peters）在接受《纽约时报》记者布拉德·普卢默（Brad Plumer）采访时表示。“石油需求出现如此大幅度的下降非常罕见。”

paras.en: The researchers call this an “energy shock,” a short-term response triggered by the war in Iran. The combat zone caused officials to close the Strait of Hormuz, located partially in Iranian waters and a major global chokepoint for oil transportation. That conflict, along with the Russia-Ukraine war, has caused prices for oil and gas to soar worldwide, forcing many countries to turn to domestic fossil or renewable energy sources, reports the Times.

The team emphasizes that this global decline in fossil emissions will not last without structural efforts to tackle emissions, such as deploying more electric vehicles along with solar and wind projects. In the Nature Climate Change paper, the authors estimate that these renewable energy strategies should offset 64 to 79 percent of increasing emissions from now through 2028. Still, that means the transition to clean energy isn’t yet robust enough to offset the anticipated rise in emissions from growing energy demands.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “There’s plenty of good news in terms of the rapid expansion of renewables,” says report co-author Mike O’Sullivan, a climate scientist at the University of Exeter, to Simmone Shah at Time. “But on a global scale, it’s completely inadequate.”

articles.title: This Mysterious Combination Lock Sank in a 1583 Shipwreck. When Engineers Cracked the Code, It Clicked Open for the First Time in More Than 400 Years

paras.en: In 1999, Peter Hughes stumbled upon the brass combination lock on Margam Beach in Wales. It featured four rotating dials, each bearing six letters. The dials turned smoothly, but only one of 1,296 possible combinations would open the device.
paras.zh: 1999年，彼得·休斯在威尔士的马格姆海滩偶然发现了这把黄铜密码锁。它有四个旋转拨盘，每个拨盘上有六个字母。密码盘转动顺畅，但1296种可能的组合中只有一种能打开该装置。

paras.en: The lock was an artifact from the Ann Francis, a merchant ship that sank in 1583. Hundreds of the vessel’s treasures—including compasses, coins and cannonballs—have since surfaced on the beach. But Hughes was particularly intrigued by the lock. He fiddled with the dials for two decades, trying to solve the puzzle.
paras.zh: 这把锁是“安·弗朗西斯”号商船上的文物，该船于1583年沉没。此后，这艘船上的数百件宝藏——包括指南针、硬币和炮弹——陆续在海滩上被发现。但休斯对这把锁特别感兴趣。他摆弄了二十年的密码盘，试图解开这个谜题。

paras.en: Now, researchers have used CT scans to reveal the four-letter code: ANCE. When they tested it out, the lock clicked open for the first time in more than four centuries. “For me, it’s like opening the Ark of the Covenant,” Hughes tells BBC Wales’ Meleri Williams. “I’m delighted—truly thrilled.”
paras.zh: 现在，研究人员通过CT扫描揭示了由四个字母组成的密码：ANCE。当他们进行测试时，这把锁在四百多年来首次咔哒一声打开了。“对我来说，这就像打开约柜一样。”休斯对BBC威尔士的梅莱里·威廉姆斯（Meleri Williams）说。“我很高兴，真的非常兴奋。”

paras.en: The Ann Francis was traveling from Spain to England when a storm swept in on December 28, 1583. The winds blew it off course, and it ultimately wrecked off Margam Beach in southern Wales. According to a parish register, 14 sailors died in December 1583, and these men may have been the Ann Francis’ crew. The record blamed the incident on “the detestable working of an execrable witch.”
paras.zh: 1583年12月28日，安·弗朗西斯号正从西班牙驶往英格兰，这时一场风暴袭来。大风将它吹离航线，最终在威尔士南部的马格姆海滩（Margam Beach）触礁沉没。根据一份教区登记册，1583年12月有14名水手死亡，这些人可能是“安·弗朗西斯”号的船员。该记录将这起事件归咎于“一个可恶女巫的卑劣行径”。

paras.en: As word spread, looters descended upon the beach, prompting legal disputes over the rights to the ship’s treasures. A few months after the wreck, Francis Shaxton, the owner of the Ann Francis, claimed the vessel and recovered some of the items.
paras.zh: 随着消息的传播，掠夺者蜂拥至海滩，引发了关于船上宝藏所有权的法律纠纷。沉船事故发生几个月后，“安·弗朗西斯”号的所有人弗朗西斯·沙克斯顿（Francis Shaxton）对该船提出所有权主张，并取回了一些物品。

paras.en: For centuries, many more artifacts remained buried beneath the sand. Hughes, a metal detectorist, made his discoveries between 1996 and 2017, aided by dredging and storms that shifted the beach’s sand. He found the combination lock near coin weights and Spanish silver coins—perhaps items that the lock once protected.
paras.zh: 几个世纪以来，还有更多文物一直埋藏在沙下。休斯是一名金属探测爱好者，他在1996年至2017年间发现了这些文物，疏浚和风暴吹移海滩的沙子为他的发现提供了帮助。他在秤锤和西班牙银币附近发现了这把密码锁，这些物品或许曾是这把锁所保护的物品。

paras.en: “It’s in fantastic condition. It still has its working parts. All of the letters are really clear,” Siân Iles, a senior curator at Museum Wales, says in a video. “I think it’s human nature when you have a code to crack—that’s what you want to do.”
paras.zh: “它的状况非常好。它的工作部件仍然完好。所有字母都非常清晰。”威尔士博物馆高级策展人Siân Iles在一段视频中说道。“我认为，当人们面对一个需要破解的密码时，就会想要破解它，这是人之常情。”

paras.en: Museum Wales recently acquired Hughes’ trove of artifacts, including the lock. Curators decided to ask researchers at Cardiff University for help identifying the combination. They explained that they had an Elizabethan lock on their hands, but nobody knew how to open it. Would they be able to use micro-CT scanners to peer inside?
paras.zh: 威尔士博物馆最近收购了休斯的藏品，其中包括这把锁。馆长们决定请卡迪夫大学的研究人员帮忙破解密码。他们解释说，他们手里有一把伊丽莎白时代的锁，但没有人知道如何打开它。他们能否使用微型CT扫描仪来窥探内部？

paras.en: David Williams, a biomechanical engineer at Cardiff University, was intrigued. Normally, he studies how humans move, sometimes using micro-CT scanners to see inside 3D objects on a very small scale. He didn’t know whether the scans would reveal anything useful about the artifact. But he had a few history buffs on his team, and they agreed to try.
paras.zh: 卡迪夫大学的生物力学工程师大卫·威廉姆斯（David Williams）对此很感兴趣。通常，他研究人类的运动方式，有时会使用微型CT扫描仪以极小的比例观察3D物体的内部。他不知道扫描是否会揭示有关该文物的任何有用的信息。不过，他的团队里有几位历史爱好者，他们同意一试。

paras.en: “Micro-CT scanning allowed us to look inside the lock without damaging it,” Williams says in a statement. “We normally use this technology to study bones and other biological structures, so investigating a 400-year-old padlock was certainly a first for us!”
paras.zh: Williams在一份声明中表示：“微型CT扫描让我们能够在不损坏锁具的情况下观察其内部结构。” “我们通常使用这项技术来研究骨骼和其他生物结构，因此研究一把有400年历史的挂锁对我们来说绝对是第一次！”

paras.en: When the lock arrived, the researchers conducted an initial scan to determine whether this approach was worth pursuing. When they saw that they could make out letters in the images, they realized the answer might be close at hand.
paras.zh: 锁具送达后，研究人员进行了初步扫描，以确定这种方法是否值得继续研究。当他们看到可以在图像中辨认出字母时，他们意识到答案可能近在眼前。

paras.en: The team used the scans to determine how the notches on the lock’s dials lined up with the teeth on the key inside them. Unfortunately, the second scan was a bust. The third, however, was much more revealing, suggesting that the long-lost code was ANCE.
paras.zh: 研究团队利用扫描结果来确定锁盘上的凹槽如何与内部钥匙上的齿槽对齐。不幸的是，第二次扫描失败了。然而，第三次扫描揭示的信息要多得多，表明失传已久的密码是ANCE。

paras.en: “After a couple of days’ work, we were able to be fairly confident that what we had was the correct code,” Alastair Willis, a senior curator at the museum, says in the video. “And then when we took the lock back to the museum, we very carefully tried moving the rings in the right combination.” Right away, he noticed that the four dials felt looser. After conservators cleaned out some of the grit that had accumulated, the lock finally clicked open.
paras.zh: “经过几天的工作，我们有相当的把握认为我们找到了正确的密码。”博物馆高级策展人阿拉斯泰尔·威利斯（Alastair Willis）在视频中说道。“然后，当我们把锁带回博物馆时，我们非常小心地尝试以正确的组合转动密码环。” 他立刻注意到，四个密码盘感觉松动了。在文物修复师清理掉一些积聚的砂砾后，锁终于咔哒一声打开了。

paras.en: The combination lock is now on display at “Tides of Treasure,” a free exhibition at the National Waterfront Museum in Swansea. The show features other artifacts from the Ann Francis, including a boatswain’s whistle and gold coins dating to Ferdinand and Isabella’s reign.
paras.zh: 这把密码锁现正于斯旺西国家滨海博物馆的免费展览“Tides of Treasure”（宝藏潮汐）中展出。展览还展出了“安·弗朗西斯”号上的其他文物，包括一把水手长哨子和几枚可追溯至斐迪南和伊莎贝拉统治时期的金币。

paras.en: According to a 16th-century inventory of items recovered from the wreck, at least three chests had been aboard the ship. Their locks had been broken, and no objects were found inside. The researchers wonder whether the combination lock protected one of these chests.
paras.zh: 根据一份16世纪的船难文物清单，这艘船上至少有三个箱子。它们的锁已被撬开，里面没有发现任何物品。研究人员想知道密码锁是否保护了其中一个箱子。

paras.en: - According to Museum Wales, a similar combination lock is currently housed at the British Museum.
paras.zh: - 据威尔士博物馆称，大英博物馆目前收藏了一把类似的密码锁。

paras.en: - Found in York, England, this early 17th-century lock features one fixed ring and four rotating dials. The word that opens it is MARCI.
paras.zh: - 这把17世纪初的锁发现于英格兰约克，有一个固定的圆环和四个旋转的拨盘。打开它的密码是“MARCI”。

paras.en: “Elizabethan combination locks are known in Britain, but this one is in exceptionally good condition and is associated with a dated wreck, making it a unique find and the code a tantalizing mystery to solve,” Willis says in the statement. “Of course, now we’ve solved it, we are left wondering if the code meant something to its owner.”
paras.zh: “伊丽莎白时代的密码锁在英国并不鲜见，但这一把的保存状况格外良好，且与一艘年代久远的沉船有关，因此堪称独一无二的发现，而密码则是一个令人心痒难耐的谜团，亟待破解。”威利斯在声明中说道。“当然，现在我们已经破解了密码，但我们不禁想知道，这个密码对它的主人来说是否有什么意义。”

paras.en: In addition to the four letters on the rotating dials, the lock features stationary letters on its outer edges. But how these letters align with ANCE is unclear. Whatever the code’s meaning, Hughes thinks the intricately crafted artifact once protected something dear to the owner’s heart.
paras.zh: 除了旋转表盘上的四个字母外，密码锁的外缘还有一些固定的字母。但这些字母如何与ANCE对应尚不清楚。无论密码的含义是什么，休斯都认为这件工艺精湛的文物曾保护过主人心中珍视的东西。

paras.en: “Tides of Treasure” is on view at the National Waterfront Museum in Swansea, Wales, through June 26, 2027.
paras.zh: “Tides of Treasure”展览将于2027年6月26日在威尔士斯旺西的国家滨海博物馆展出。

articles.title: Florida Is Facing Its Worst Dengue Outbreak in Decades, With at Least 524 Locally Acquired Cases. Here's What to Know

paras.en: This year, the Florida Department of Health has recorded a staggering 524 locally acquired cases of dengue, a mosquito-borne viral disease, as of October 31. That’s the highest number recorded there since the disease returned to the state in 2009, according to Forbes’ John Drake. For context, only 62 locally acquired cases were documented in 2025.
paras.zh: 截至10月31日，佛罗里达州卫生部今年已记录了惊人的524例本地感染登革热病例，登革热是一种由蚊子传播的病毒性疾病。据《福布斯》的约翰·德雷克（John Drake）称，这是该疾病于2009年在该州再次出现以来记录的最高数字。为了说明情况，2023年仅记录了62例本地感染病例。

paras.en: Most infected people either do not show symptoms or experience only mild illness. But in early September, a Tampa-area woman named Gay Rabb Small died of dengue on her 80th birthday, after developing a tremor and going to the emergency room, per the New York Times’ Anemona Hartocollis.
paras.zh: 大多数感染者要么没有出现症状，要么仅出现轻度不适。但据《纽约时报》的Anemona Hartocollis报道，9月初，坦帕地区一位名叫Gay Rabb Small的女士在80岁生日那天因登革热去世。在此之前，她出现了震颤症状并被送往急诊室。

paras.en: Later that month, three counties in Florida declared local emergencies over the illness, and in October, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued a national emergency response to dengue.
paras.zh: 当月晚些时候，佛罗里达州有三个县因该疾病宣布进入地方紧急状态；10月，美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）发布了针对登革热的国家级紧急响应。

paras.en: “It is very unusual to have transmission in the United States,” Eva Harris, an infectious diseases expert at the University of California, Berkeley, tells the Times. “This is so very much of an eye-opener.”
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的传染病专家伊娃·哈里斯（Eva Harris）在接受《纽约时报》采访时表示：“在美国发生传播非常罕见。” “这真是大开眼界。”

paras.en: Dengue is a viral disease spread by mosquitoes, mainly the species Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, which are both present in Florida, among other places. The disease is more common in tropical and subtropical regions, where these biting insects thrive, than in temperate climates.
paras.zh: 登革热是一种由蚊子传播的病毒性疾病，主要传播媒介是埃及伊蚊和白纹伊蚊，这两种蚊子在佛罗里达州等地区均有分布。与温带气候地区相比，这种疾病在这些叮咬性昆虫大量繁殖的热带和亚热带地区更为常见。

paras.en: Around three in four infected people are asymptomatic or have mild flu-like symptoms, such as fever, headache, nausea and rash. Muscle and joint pain is another common symptom, which is why the disease is sometimes called “breakbone fever.” Symptoms usually appear within two weeks of being bitten by an infected mosquito and clear up after a week or two.
paras.zh: 大约四分之三的感染者无症状或有轻度流感样症状，如发热、头痛、恶心和皮疹。肌肉和关节疼痛是另一种常见症状，这就是为什么这种疾病有时被称为“骨折热”。症状通常在被感染的蚊子叮咬后两周内出现，并在一两周后消失。

paras.en: However, one in four dengue cases becomes severe. Those symptoms include extreme abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing and blood in vomit or stool, and anyone experiencing them should seek medical care. These signs often appear after the fever goes away, and people who have previously been infected are at a greater risk of severe dengue.
