paras.en: Sanders: That’s Samantha Brosler, a bioengineer at the University of California, San Francisco. Some brain-computer interfaces can pick up movements. We haven’t talked much about them, but these implants have their own very successful research history. They’ve allowed people to control a robotic arm, for instance.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是萨曼莎·布罗斯勒，加州大学旧金山分校的生物工程师。一些脑机接口可以接收动作。我们没有过多谈论它们，但这些植入物有自己非常成功的研究历史。例如，他们允许人们控制机械臂。

paras.en: Brosler: Most of these devices so far have been designed to restore one function at a time, whereas in reality, frequently people who are paralyzed are missing both the ability to speak and perform body movements. And so in this study, we asked whether a single brain implant could be used to decode both speech and movement at the same time.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：到目前为止，大多数这些设备的设计目的都是一次恢复一种功能，而实际上，瘫痪的人经常丧失说话和进行身体运动的能力。因此，在这项研究中，我们询问是否可以使用单个大脑植入物同时解码语音和运动。

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out, it could. She and her colleagues were able to decode gestures for communication — things like thumbs up, or a head nodding yes — and words. This combo approach is a more natural way of getting a point across.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明，可以。她和她的同事能够解读交流手势（例如竖起大拇指或点头表示同意）和言语。这种组合方法是一种更自然的表达观点的方式。

paras.en: Brosler: We naturally use gestures alongside our speech. So for example, some gestures can substitute for speech entirely, like nodding yes, shaking your head no, waving, shrugging, giving a thumbs up. But they can also add or change the meaning of what we’re saying. So for example, if you say maybe combined with nod head yes, that has a very different, you know, meaning than if you say maybe and shrug or shake your head no.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们在讲话时自然会使用手势。例如，某些手势可以完全替代言语，例如点头“是”、摇头“不”、挥手、耸肩、竖起大拇指。但他们也可以添加或改变我们所说的话的含义。例如，如果你说“也许”加上点头“是”，这与你说“也许”然后耸耸肩或摇头“不”的含义非常不同。

paras.en: Sanders: My kids know that a slow maybe with a skeptical eyebrow raise is much closer to a no than my fast upbeat maybe with a little head nod. There is so much subtext in our body language.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我的孩子们知道，缓慢地扬起怀疑的眉毛可能比我快速乐观地点头可能更接近于“不”。我们的肢体语言中有很多潜台词。

paras.en: Brosler: So I think of, you know, gestures and body movements as an additional communication channel that can work together with speech to add expressivity to what we’re trying to say.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：所以我认为，手势和身体动作是一种额外的沟通渠道，可以与语音一起工作，为我们想说的话增添表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: In the study, the output was a digital avatar who looked like the person. Success looked like the avatar moving and getting the word right.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在这项研究中，输出的是一个看起来像这个人的数字化身。成功看起来就像化身移动并正确表达了意思。

paras.en: Brosler: And the idea is that we enable the participants to use speech and gestures alone or together. So in theory, someone could say hello while waving.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们的想法是让参与者能够单独或一起使用语音和手势。所以理论上，有人可以一边挥手一边打招呼。

paras.en: Sanders: The researchers started simple, with just a few phrases — hello, bye, good idea, how’s it going, let’s go — and just a few gestures, like a shrug or a point, a fist pump, thumbs up.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：研究人员从简单的开始，只有几句话——你好、再见、好主意、怎么样、走吧——还有几个手势，比如耸肩或点一下、握拳、竖起大拇指。

paras.en: Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: Sanders: The sheer number of different approaches to restoring communication is a sign that this neurotechnology is coming fast. Here’s Willsey.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：恢复沟通的不同方法的数量之多表明这种神经技术正在快速发展。这是威尔西。

paras.en: Willsey: I think it’s good. There’s a lot of players that are entering into the field that have a variety of different ideas where they can run the clinical trials and see how these different devices stack up.
paras.zh: 威尔西：我认为这很好。许多进入该领域的参与者都有各种不同的想法，他们可以进行临床试验，看看这些不同的设备如何叠加。

paras.en: Sanders: There are lots of reasons to be optimistic about the future here, and it’s a future that isn’t even that far off. Here’s David Brandman, one of the researchers at UC Davis who works with Casey. He’s also the neurosurgeon who implanted Casey’s device.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有很多理由对这里的未来感到乐观，而且这个未来并不遥远。这是大卫·布兰德曼（David Brandman），他是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西一起工作。他也是植入凯西设备的神经外科医生。

paras.en: Brandman: I think I’m about five years away from being able to meet a patient with ALS and having the following conversation, and saying, you know, Ms. Smith, I’m sorry you’ve been diagnosed with ALS. I don’t have a cure for you, but I do have a device that I can implant that can help you communicate despite facing a future of paralysis. It’s a device that would be implanted. It’s fully wirelessly. It’s cosmetically invisible, and you’d be able to use it to communicate your needs and have a meaningful conversation with friends and family. So I think that kind of conversation is about five to 10 years away.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我想大约还有五年的时间我就能见到 ALS 患者并进行以下对话，然后说，史密斯女士，我很抱歉您被诊断出患有 ALS。我没有治愈你的方法，但我确实有一种可以植入的设备，可以帮助你在未来面临瘫痪的情况下进行交流。这是一个可以植入的设备。它是完全无线的。它在外观上是隐形的，您可以用它来传达您的需求并与朋友和家人进行有意义的对话。所以我认为这种对话大约需要五到十年的时间。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s a beautiful vision. When you’ve been a reporter as long as I have, you’re skeptical when scientists say something big is just five to 10 years away. But in this case, I see it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是一个美好的愿景。如果你像我一样当了这么久的记者，当科学家说五到十年后就会有大事发生时，你会持怀疑态度。但在这种情况下，我看到了。

paras.en: It’s easy to get drawn into the technical details here. Different types of implants, the decoding processes, AI-powered voice clones and what they can do and can’t do — what they should do and shouldn’t do. But if you step back and really look, you’ll see that this research is all propelled by a very simple and powerful fact: The human voice is too important to lose.
paras.zh: 这里很容易被技术细节所吸引。不同类型的植入物、解码过程、人工智能驱动的语音克隆以及它们能做什么和不能做什么——它们应该做什么和不应该做什么。但如果你退后一步仔细观察，你会发现这项研究都是由一个非常简单而有力的事实推动的：人的声音太重要了，不能失去。

paras.en: Casey: What does my voice mean to me? It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：我的声音对我来说意味着什么？这意味着很多。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: So now we are here, in this moment, as Jules would say, right here, right now. And right now, the human voice is shifting and changing, expanding in ways that were completely unthinkable even just a few years ago. The future of the human voice and its many replicas is anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以现在我们在这里，此时此刻，正如朱尔斯所说，就在这里，此时此刻。现在，人类的声音正在转变和变化，以几年前完全不可想象的方式扩展。人声及其众多复制品的未来谁也说不准。

paras.en: Sanders: In one of Jules’ comedy sets, the one he did in November of 2024, he wheels out onto the stage as the song “Walking on Sunshine” plays.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在朱尔斯于 2024 年 11 月拍摄的一部喜剧中，他在歌曲《行走在阳光下》中推上舞台。

paras.en: As the crowd settles and finishes their clapping and woo-ing, Jules pauses. You can’t see this, but he wiggles his eyebrows — a lot. The crowd goes crazy every time. He hasn’t said a single word yet. After another pause, he deadpans with his voice clone: “That is all the time I have. My Make-A-Wish covered only a few minutes. Goodnight, everybody.”
paras.zh: 当人群安静下来并结束鼓掌和求爱时，朱尔斯停了下来。你看不到这一点，但他经常摇动眉毛。每次人群都会疯狂。他还没有说一个字。又停顿了一下，他面无表情地用他的声音克隆说：“这就是我所有的时间了。我的愿望只持续了几分钟。大家晚安。”

paras.en: And with that, Jules takes control and he’s off on a tear, ripping through stories of a weatherman who seems too happy about standing out in hurricanes, the exquisite guilt trips lovingly crafted by his Cuban parents, and the indignities of having body parts shaved with his sister right there in the room. Jules has the audience laughing so hard. It’s magnificent.
paras.zh: 就这样，朱尔斯掌控了一切，他泪流满面，讲述了一个天气预报员似乎太高兴在飓风中脱颖而出的故事，他的古巴父母精心设计的精致内疚之旅，以及和他的妹妹一起在房间里剃掉身体部位的侮辱。朱尔斯让观众笑得很厉害。太棒了。

paras.en: MA: And being backstage and then seeing him come out, like roll out in his wheelchair and everybody go nuts because they’re like, what is going on here? Like, this doesn’t make sense. And every time I was like, this is like life. This is love. This is passion. This is like, what else is there? Like, I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here and what I can help him do.
paras.zh: MA：在后台，然后看到他出来，就像坐在轮椅上一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会想，这里发生了什么事？就像，这没有意义。每次我都想，这就像生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。这就像，还有什么？就像，我不知道还有什么比这个人在这里所做的事情以及我可以帮助他做的事情更强大的了。

paras.en: Sanders: I get what MA meant when she said that comedy is something that heals. When his set actually does come to a close, he tells the audience.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我明白马的意思，她说喜剧是一种治愈的东西。当他的演出真正结束时，他告诉观众。

paras.en: [Audio] Now you have to watch me slowly get off this stage. Goodnight, everybody.
paras.zh: [音频]现在你必须看着我慢慢走下这个舞台。大家晚安。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s hilarious. It’s happy. It’s sad. It’s perfect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这很搞笑。很高兴。很伤心。太完美了。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund, with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Europe’s Hera mission is ready to double down on asteroid science
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft is about to start a twofold mission to a twofold asteroid.
paras.zh: 欧洲航天局的赫拉航天器即将开始对一颗双重小行星的双重任务。

paras.en: On November 4, after more than two years trekking through space, the spacecraft finally came within 30 kilometers of space rocks named Didymos and Dimorphos. The encounter marks the first time scientists will explore a pair of asteroids navigating the solar system together. To date, spacecraft have stopped to investigate just seven other asteroids, every one of them a lonely speck in outer space.
paras.zh: 11月4日，经过两年多的太空跋涉，飞船终于到达了名为Didymos和Dimorphos的太空岩石30公里以内。这次相遇标志着科学家首次探索一对一起在太阳系中航行的小行星。迄今为止，航天器已经停下来调查另外七颗小行星，它们中的每一颗都是外太空中孤独的一粒。

paras.en: Hera will spend the coming weeks approaching Didymos and Dimorphos and will release two small companion spacecraft in January for an even closer look.
paras.zh: 赫拉将在接下来的几周内接近迪迪莫斯和迪莫弗斯，并将在一月份释放两艘小型伴生飞船进行更近距离的观察。

paras.en: Didymos, a mass of rocks about twice as wide as the Empire State Building is tall, and its small moonlet Dimorphos have had a rough time lately. In 2022, NASA slammed its Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft into Dimorphos, sending a plume of debris into space and shortening its orbit around Didymos by more than half an hour.
paras.zh: Didymos 是一块宽约是帝国大厦高两倍的岩石，它的小卫星 Dimorphos 最近经历了一段艰难的时期。 2022 年，美国宇航局将其双小行星重定向测试 (DART) 航天器撞向 Dimorphos，将大量碎片送入太空，并将其绕 Didymos 的轨道缩短了半个多小时。

paras.en: The cosmic realignment wasn’t a mere lark. Such an impact is one of the few ways scientists can practice planetary defense, the field dedicated to searching for dangerous asteroids and developing ways to deal with them lest humans go the way of the dinosaurs. DART and Hera are a carefully coordinated pair, with Hera’s top priority being to investigate the aftermath of DART’s crash and inform future planetary defense efforts.
paras.zh: 宇宙的重新调整不仅仅是一场闹剧。这种撞击是科学家进行行星防御的少数方法之一，该领域致力于寻找危险的小行星并开发处理它们的方法，以免人类重蹈恐龙的覆辙。 DART 和 Hera 是一对精心协调的搭档，Hera 的首要任务是调查 DART 坠机事件的后果，并为未来的行星防御工作提供信息。

paras.en: That process will also yield a treasure trove of observations asteroid scientists are determined to exploit.
paras.zh: 这一过程还将产生小行星科学家决心利用的观测宝库。

paras.en: “Planetary defense and science are sort of two sides of the same coin,” says planetary scientist Jessica Sunshine of the University of Maryland, who was on the DART team but is not involved in the Hera mission. On the science side, she says, “we’re trying to figure out not so much how did we break the thing, but how was it put together in the first place.”
paras.zh: “行星防御和科学是同一枚硬币的两面，”马里兰大学的行星科学家杰西卡·桑夏恩 (Jessica Sunshine) 说道，她是 DART 团队的成员，但并未参与赫拉任务。她说，在科学方面，“我们并不是想弄清楚我们是如何破坏这个东西的，而是想弄清楚它最初是如何组装在一起的。”

paras.en: DART purposefully targeted a binary system instead of a solo asteroid to make measuring the change in orbit it accomplished easier: Any difference would be much more obvious against the 12-hour baseline orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos than against the months- or yearslong orbit of an asteroid circling the sun. (Despite the difficulty, scientists were able to calculate that DART shortened the more-than-two-year orbit of the Didymos system around the sun by a fraction of a second.)
paras.zh: DART 有目的地瞄准双星系统而不是单独的小行星，以便更容易测量它所完成的轨道变化：与 Dimorphos 围绕 Didymos 的 12 小时基线轨道相比，任何差异都会比小行星绕太阳运行数月或数年的轨道更明显。 （尽管困难重重，科学家还是能够计算出 DART 将 Didymos 系统围绕太阳运行两年多的轨道缩短了不到一秒。）

paras.en: Hera’s observations will provide a crucial glimpse at binary asteroids generally, which astronomers believe account for some 15 percent of all asteroids. Scientists expect that most binary asteroids in the inner solar system, including the Didymos system, probably formed their moonlets from debris that sloughed off the larger object then clumped together in orbit.
paras.zh: 赫拉的观测将为双小行星提供一个重要的视角，天文学家认为双小行星约占所有小行星的 15%。科学家预计，内太阳系中的大多数双星小行星，包括狄迪莫斯系统，可能是由较大天体脱落的碎片形成的，然后在轨道上聚集在一起。

paras.en: Didymos spins so quickly that its gravity may not be strong enough to hold all its rock together. As the asteroid spins, it may send boulders into space, where they could end up landing on Dimorphos, continuing that material transfer today. Scientists will comb through Hera’s imagery for signs of rocks moving across each object’s surface, as well as between the two objects.
paras.zh: Didymos 旋转得如此之快，以至于它的重力可能不足以将所有岩石固定在一起。当小行星旋转时，它可能会将巨石送入太空，最终降落在 Dimorphos 上，继续今天的物质转移。科学家将梳理赫拉的图像，寻找岩石在每个物体表面以及两个物体之间移动的迹象。

paras.en: Scientists expect that Dimorphos is a rubble pile composed of boulders and rocky debris. It’s similar in structure to other recent spacecraft targets Ryugu and Bennu, although those are both significantly larger. The boulder-strewn landscape DART saw as it sped toward Dimorphos aligns with this theory, but how deep the rubbly structure extends is a mystery. “We’ve never seen the interior of an asteroid before,” says planetary scientist Angela Stickle of the Johns Hopkins University’s Applied Physics Laboratory.
paras.zh: 科学家预计迪莫弗斯是由巨石和岩石碎片组成的碎石堆。它的结构与最近的其他航天器目标“龙宫”和“本努”相似，尽管它们都大得多。 DART 在飞向 Dimorphos 时看到的布满巨石的景观与这一理论相符，但碎石结构延伸到多深仍然是个谜。 “我们以前从未见过小行星的内部，”约翰·霍普金斯大学应用物理实验室的行星科学家安吉拉·斯蒂克尔说。

paras.en: Juventas, Hera’s companion cubesat about the size of a breadbox, will change that. It carries a first-of-its-kind radar instrument to investigate Dimorphos’ internal structure.
paras.zh: 赫拉的同伴立方体尤文塔斯（Juventas）大约有一个面包盒那么大，它将改变这一现状。它搭载了首个雷达仪器来研究 Dimorphos 的内部结构。

paras.en: Juventas will also attempt to land on Dimorphos, allowing scientists to directly interact with the surface. That’s a particularly tantalizing endeavor given one of the biggest surprises of NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission. When that spacecraft grabbed a sample of Bennu, it accidentally sank some half a meter into the rubble as the asteroid unexpectedly gave way beneath it, even though the surface had looked perfectly sturdy.
paras.zh: Juventas 还将尝试降落在 Dimorphos 上，让科学家能够直接与地表互动。鉴于美国宇航局奥西里斯-雷克斯任务的最大惊喜之一，这是一项特别诱人的努力。当该航天器抓取贝努的样本时，由于小行星意外地在其下方塌陷，它意外地沉入了废墟中约半米，尽管表面看起来非常坚固。

paras.en: “Even though we had amazing images, the reaction was not what we expected,” says planetary scientist Patrick Michel of the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) of that experience. “There is still sort of a mismatch between what we see and what we feel.” He hopes that the Juventas landing will help scientists better connect appearance and reality on this front.
paras.zh: 法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）的行星科学家帕特里克·米歇尔（Patrick Michel）在谈到那次经历时表示：“尽管我们拍摄到了令人惊叹的图像，但人们的反应却出乎我们的意料。” “我们所看到的和我们感受到的之间仍然存在某种不匹配。”他希望尤文塔斯的登陆能够帮助科学家在这方面更好地连接表象和现实。

paras.en: Although scientists will need to pick out the ways DART made Didymos and Dimorphos different from other binary asteroids, observations with Hera will offer new avenues for investigating more general questions in asteroid science.
paras.zh: 尽管科学家需要找出 DART 使 Didymos 和 Dimorphos 与其他双小行星不同的方式，但 Hera 的观测将为研究小行星科学中更普遍的问题提供新途径。

paras.en: For example, scientists know that before DART’s impact, Dimorphos always showed the same face to Didymos, just like our moon does to Earth. The collision probably changed that, sending Dimorphos tumbling — but there’s no way to know what state it’s in now because scientists have never seen this resetting process unfold. “Eventually, the system might stabilize, but we don’t know how long it takes,” says planetary scientist Eva Lilly of the Planetary Science Institute, who is not involved in either mission.
paras.zh: 例如，科学家们知道，在 DART 撞击之前，Dimorphos 总是向 Didymos 展示相同的面孔，就像我们的月球向地球展示一样。这次碰撞可能改变了这一点，导致 Dimorphos 翻滚——但无法知道它现在处于什么状态，因为科学家从未见过这种重置过程的展开。 “最终，该系统可能会稳定下来，但我们不知道需要多长时间，”行星科学研究所的行星科学家伊娃·莉莉（Eva Lilly）说，她没有参与这两项任务。

paras.en: Similarly, scientists know that the rain of charged particles onto an asteroid’s surface darkens a thin layer of rock at the surface, but without the detailed understanding they’d like. At Dimorphos, they’ll be able to observe fresh rock uncovered by a known event, potentially offering clearer insight into the universal process.
paras.zh: 同样，科学家们知道小行星表面的带电粒子雨会使表面的一层薄薄的岩石变暗，但他们并没有得到他们想要的详细了解。在 Dimorphos，他们将能够观察已知事件中发现的新鲜岩石，从而有可能为普遍过程提供更清晰的见解。

paras.en: Cosmic crash scene or not, asteroid scientists are never going to miss out on up-close views of two different space rocks.
paras.zh: 无论是否存在宇宙碰撞场景，小行星科学家都不会错过两种不同太空岩石的近距离观察。

articles.title: The brain’s fear center moonlights as the save button for memories
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: The walnut-sized fear center of the brain also distinguishes the memorable from the mundane.
paras.zh: 大脑核桃大小的恐惧中心也将难忘的事情与平凡的事情区分开来。

paras.en: Neurons in the amygdala act like a save button for memories, scientists report October 27 in Nature Neuroscience. Though the study doesn’t nail down the exact mechanism for memory formation, it points to a broader role for the amygdala within the memory-sorting apparatus.
paras.zh: 科学家于 10 月 27 日在《自然神经科学》杂志上发表报告称，杏仁核中的神经元就像记忆的保存按钮。尽管这项研究没有确定记忆形成的确切机制，但它指出了杏仁核在记忆分类装置中发挥着更广泛的作用。

paras.en: The study probes an enduring quandary about the mind, says neuroscientist Jiayang Xiao of Cedars-Sinai Health Sciences University in Los Angeles. “We forget much of what we experience … only a fraction of the information we encounter becomes a lasting memory,” she says.
paras.zh: 洛杉矶雪松-西奈健康科学大学的神经科学家肖嘉阳表示，这项研究探讨了关于大脑的一个持久的难题。 “我们忘记了我们经历过的很多事情……只有我们遇到的信息的一小部分会成为持久的记忆，”她说。

paras.en: Although a role for the amygdala in memory has been suggested before, previous studies that used electrodes reading brain activity through the scalp, or at the scale of thousands rather than individual neurons, captured a blurrier picture. It’s akin to a microphone recording from outside of a stadium, says cognitive neuroscientist Cory Inman at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 尽管之前已经提出过杏仁核在记忆中的作用，但之前的研究使用电极通过头皮读取大脑活动，或者以数千个而不是单个神经元的规模读取大脑活动，捕捉到的图像更加模糊。盐湖城犹他大学认知神经科学家科里·英曼（未参与这项研究）表示，这类似于体育场外的麦克风录音。

paras.en: “You might be able to tell that there’s a game happening. You might be able to tell when somebody scores a touchdown. You might even be able to tell that one side of the stadium is cheering for one team and another side of the stadium is cheering for another team,” but that’s about it, Inman says. The new study is more like a lapel mic pinned on a single fan in terms of scale and what the researchers were able to capture, adding clarity.
paras.zh: “你也许能够分辨出正在发生一场比赛。你也许能够分辨出某人何时达阵。你甚至可能能够分辨出体育场的一侧正在为一支球队欢呼，而体育场的另一侧正在为另一支球队欢呼，”但仅此而已，英曼说。就规模和研究人员能够捕获的内容而言，这项新研究更像是固定在单个风扇上的翻领麦克风，从而增加了清晰度。

paras.en: The amygdala, which is typically associated with regulating emotions like fear and aggression, has neurons that are challenging to reach, residing in two clusters deep within the brain. Xiao and her colleagues leveraged electrodes previously surgically implanted in more than 90 people with drug-resistant epilepsy to identify where seizures originate. In their new role, the electrodes singled out neurons involved in saving memories.
paras.zh: 杏仁核通常与调节恐惧和攻击性等情绪有关，其神经元难以到达，位于大脑深处的两个簇中。肖和她的同事利用之前通过手术植入 90 多名耐药性癫痫患者体内的电极来确定癫痫发作的根源。在新的角色中，电极挑选出了参与保存记忆的神经元。

paras.en: Patients were shown images of everyday objects belonging to five categories such as food and animals. About 10 to 30 minutes later, they attempted to recall which images were already shown. Xiao and her colleagues found that activity in certain amygdala neurons corresponded with an image being remembered. The image had been earmarked for longer term storage, Xiao says.
paras.zh: 向患者展示属于食物和动物等五类的日常物品的图像。大约 10 到 30 分钟后，他们试图回忆起已经播放过哪些图像。肖和她的同事发现，某些杏仁核神经元的活动与所记住的图像相对应。肖说，该图像已指定用于长期存储。

paras.en: Although participants had to recall something from half an hour ago at most and the exact mechanism for saving memories is still unclear, the researchers think there are two main steps of the process. The team showed that individual neurons have a preference for one of the five categories of images. First the image is categorized by the amygdala. Then, the strength of the category neuron response the first time the image is shown dictates whether the image is later recalled.
paras.zh: 尽管参与者最多只能回忆半小时前的事情，而且保存记忆的确切机制仍不清楚，但研究人员认为这个过程有两个主要步骤。研究小组表明，单个神经元对五类图像之一有偏好。首先，图像按杏仁核分类。然后，第一次显示图像时类别神经元响应的强度决定了以后是否会回忆起该图像。

paras.en: A better understanding of this mechanism may pave the way for more effective treatments of memory disorders, Xiao says, a medical conundrum for which there are currently no broadly effective treatments.
paras.zh: 肖说，更好地理解这一机制可能为更有效地治疗记忆障碍铺平道路，这是一个目前还没有广泛有效的治疗方法的医学难题。

paras.en: The hippocampus is typically more directly linked to memory, so “it surprised me that we observe such a clear relationship between memory formation and activity in the amygdala,” Xiao says. By contrast, the correlation between hippocampus neuron activity and image recall was weaker and slightly delayed.
paras.zh: 海马体通常与记忆有更直接的联系，因此“令我惊讶的是，我们观察到记忆形成和杏仁核活动之间存在如此清晰的关系，”肖说。相比之下，海马神经元活动与图像回忆之间的相关性较弱且略有延迟。

paras.en: Future work like observing the impacts of stimulating amygdala neurons on memory will help researchers discern if this region can be targeted to improve memory, Xiao says.
paras.zh: 肖说，未来的工作，比如观察刺激杏仁核神经元对记忆的影响，将有助于研究人员辨别该区域是否可以针对改善记忆。

paras.en: For now, the secret to memory’s hidden machinations remains in the shadows.
paras.zh: 目前，记忆中隐藏的阴谋的秘密仍然处于阴影之中。

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms

paras.en: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimerâs years before symptoms
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学的科学家发现隐藏的大脑信号，可以在阿尔茨海默病出现症状前数年预测

paras.en: - Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimerâs risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect memory.
paras.zh: - 斯坦福大学的研究人员发现，隐藏的大脑活动模式可以在记忆问题出现前几年预测阿尔茨海默病的风险，这可能比传统的生物标记物更早发出警告。同样的模式还揭示了哪些大脑具有异常抵抗衰老的能力，这为未来有助于保护记忆的治疗带来了希望。

paras.en: Subtle patterns of brain activity may reveal the risk of Alzheimer's disease years before memory problems develop or harmful proteins begin accumulating in the brain, according to new research led by Stanford Medicine. The same approach can also identify people whose brains show exceptional resistance to cognitive decline, suggesting they may eventually become "super agers."
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学医学院领导的一项新研究表明，大脑活动的微妙模式可能会在记忆问题出现或有害蛋白质开始在大脑中积聚之前数年揭示出患阿尔茨海默病的风险。同样的方法还可以识别那些大脑对认知能力下降表现出异常抵抗力的人，这表明他们最终可能成为“超级老年人”。

paras.en: The study, published November 4 in Science Advances, points to a potentially powerful new way to detect early warning signs of cognitive decline. Unlike conventional biomarkers, these patterns of brain activity might eventually be possible to change through targeted interventions.
paras.zh: 这项研究于 11 月 4 日发表在《科学进展》上，指出了一种潜在的强大新方法来检测认知能力下降的早期预警信号。与传统的生物标志物不同，这些大脑活动模式最终可能通过有针对性的干预措施而改变。

paras.en: To investigate, the research team examined brain activity in adults aged 75 and older who represented opposite ends of the cognitive aging spectrum. One group had Alzheimer's disease, while the other consisted of super agers, older individuals whose memories remained comparable to those of people decades younger. Using the differences between these groups, the scientists created a scoring system to evaluate brain activity in cognitively healthy adults between 55 and 70.
paras.zh: 为了进行调查，研究小组检查了 75 岁及以上成年人的大脑活动，他们代表了认知衰老谱的两端。一组患有阿尔茨海默病，而另一组则由超级老年人组成，这些老年人的记忆力仍与年轻数十岁的人相当。利用这些群体之间的差异，科学家们创建了一个评分系统来评估 55 岁至 70 岁之间认知健康的成年人的大脑活动。

paras.en: The results revealed a striking connection between brain activity and future cognitive health. People whose brain patterns more closely resembled those of Alzheimer's patients were more likely to experience cognitive decline, accumulate amyloid-beta plaques, and receive an Alzheimer's diagnosis during follow-up periods extending up to 12 years. Those with activity patterns resembling super agers were more likely to maintain their cognitive abilities and avoid these outcomes.
paras.zh: 结果揭示了大脑活动与未来认知健康之间的显着联系。大脑模式与阿尔茨海默氏症患者的大脑模式更相似的人更有可能出现认知能力下降、β-淀粉样蛋白斑块积聚，并在长达 12 年的随访期间被诊断为阿尔茨海默氏症。那些活动模式类似于超级老年人的人更有可能保持他们的认知能力并避免这些结果。

paras.en: A New Way to Detect Alzheimer's Before Memory Loss
paras.zh: 在记忆丧失之前检测阿尔茨海默病的新方法

paras.en: The new scoring system predicted future cognitive decline more effectively than several established indicators, including demographic characteristics, genetic risk factors, and amyloid-beta and tau biomarkers. This suggests that examining how different regions of the brain communicate could reveal Alzheimer's risk earlier than existing approaches.
paras.zh: 新的评分系统比人口特征、遗传风险因素、β-淀粉样蛋白和 tau 蛋白生物标志物等多项既定指标更能有效地预测未来的认知能力下降。这表明，检查大脑不同区域如何沟通可以比现有方法更早地揭示阿尔茨海默病的风险。

paras.en: "We want to address a major challenge in the Alzheimer's field nowadays -- most studies are looking at well-known Alzheimer's disease biomarkers, such as amyloid-beta or tau. But those are observable at relatively late stages of the disease," said Yu Zhang, PhD, assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences and senior author of the study. "What we really care about is defining early markers that can detect earlier signs of cognitive decline and potentially help us deliver timely interventions to people."
paras.zh: “我们希望解决当今阿尔茨海默病领域的一个重大挑战——大多数研究都在关注众所周知的阿尔茨海默病生物标志物，例如β淀粉样蛋白或tau蛋白。但这些是在疾病相对较晚的阶段才能观察到的，”精神病学和行为科学助理教授、该研究的资深作者张宇博士说。 “我们真正关心的是定义早期标记，这些标记可以检测认知能力下降的早期迹象，并有可能帮助我们及时为人们提供干预措施。”

paras.en: Zhang envisions a future in which treatments could potentially move someone's brain activity toward the patterns associated with greater cognitive resilience. Possible approaches include cognitive training and transcranial magnetic stimulation, which uses magnetic pulses to influence brain activity.
paras.zh: 张设想，在未来，治疗可能会将某人的大脑活动转向与更强的认知弹性相关的模式。可能的方法包括认知训练和经颅磁刺激，后者使用磁脉冲影响大脑活动。

paras.en: Transcranial magnetic stimulation has already demonstrated potential for changing brain activity in people being treated for depression. However, neither of these proposed approaches has been tested in this context for preventing cognitive decline, and researchers do not yet know whether changing brain activity would alter the course of Alzheimer's disease. The new findings provide a starting point for identifying which brain regions might be useful treatment targets.
paras.zh: 经颅磁刺激已经显示出改变抑郁症患者大脑活动的潜力。然而，这些提出的方法都没有在这方面进行过预防认知能力下降的测试，研究人员还不知道改变大脑活动是否会改变阿尔茨海默病的病程。新发现为确定哪些大脑区域可能是有用的治疗目标提供了一个起点。

paras.en: "There are two main components: One is to know which part of the brain to target, the other is how we should change it," Zhang said. "That's why identifying the super-ager brain resilience pattern is a critical component -- so we know what a good pattern should be."
paras.zh: “有两个主要组成部分：一是知道要针对大脑的哪一部分，二是我们应该如何改变它，”张说。 “这就是为什么识别超级老年人的大脑恢复模式是一个关键组成部分——这样我们就知道一个好的模式应该是什么。”

paras.en: What Makes Super Agers' Brains Different?
paras.zh: 是什么让超级老年人的大脑与众不同？

paras.en: Depending on how they are defined, approximately 10% of older adults may qualify as super agers. For this research, the term referred to people at least 75 years old who performed on memory tests at a level typical of a 45-year-old while maintaining normal executive function for their age.
paras.zh: 根据定义的不同，大约 10% 的老年人可能符合超级老年人的资格。在这项研究中，该术语指的是至少 75 岁的人，他们在记忆测试中的表现相当于 45 岁的典型水平，同时保持了同龄人的正常执行功能。

paras.en: Scientists have become increasingly interested in these unusually resilient individuals. Most earlier studies, however, compared super-agers with other older adults who performed normally on cognitive assessments.
paras.zh: 科学家们对这些异常坚韧的个体越来越感兴趣。然而，大多数早期研究将超级老年人与其他认知评估表现正常的老年人进行了比较。

paras.en: Zhang recognized that this approach could overlook important biological differences. Two people might receive similar scores on memory tests despite having very different underlying brain health. One might already be developing amyloid-beta plaques or showing other biological changes associated with aging, while the other might not.
paras.zh: 张认识到这种方法可能会忽略重要的生物学差异。尽管两个人的潜在大脑健康状况截然不同，但他们在记忆测试中可能会得到相似的分数。其中一个可能已经形成淀粉样蛋白斑块或显示出与衰老相关的其他生物学变化，而另一个可能还没有。

paras.en: "Normal, cognitively unimpaired individuals are pretty heterogeneous in terms of their biological abnormalities," he said. "Simply comparing super agers with such a heterogeneous population makes it challenging to define what is critical in terms of resilient or vulnerable brain patterns."
paras.zh: “正常的、认知未受损的个体在生物学异常方面是相当异质的，”他说。 “仅仅将超级老年人与如此异质的人群进行比较，就很难定义什么是弹性或脆弱的大脑模式的关键。”

paras.en: In other words, comparing super agers with a broad mixture of seemingly healthy older adults makes it difficult to determine which brain characteristics actually protect against decline.
paras.zh: 换句话说，将超级老年人与一系列看似健康的老年人进行比较，很难确定哪些大脑特征实际上可以防止衰退。

paras.en: The Stanford team took a different approach. Rather than using typical older adults as the comparison group, they examined people with Alzheimer's disease who were approximately the same age as the super agers. This created two more clearly defined groups at opposite ends of the cognitive spectrum.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学团队采取了不同的方法。他们没有使用典型的老年人作为对照组，而是检查了与超级老年人年龄大致相同的阿尔茨海默病患者。这在认知范围的两端创建了两个更明确定义的群体。

paras.en: The researchers drew on imaging information collected through several major research initiatives, including the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies, the Harvard Aging Brain Study, and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用了通过几项主要研究计划收集的成像信息，包括成像研究开放获取系列、哈佛大脑老化研究和阿尔茨海默病神经影像计划。

paras.en: They examined resting-state functional MRI scans from 180 super agers and 110 people diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. This imaging technique records patterns of brain activity while a person lies quietly inside a scanner.
paras.zh: 他们检查了 180 名超级老年人和 110 名被诊断患有阿尔茨海默病的人的静息态功能 MRI 扫描。当一个人安静地躺在扫描仪内时，这种成像技术会记录大脑活动的模式。

paras.en: The comparison uncovered distinctive differences in activity across multiple brain regions. Some areas showed greater activity while others showed reduced activity, producing recognizable patterns that distinguished the two groups. Scientists refer to the relationships among these regions as functional connectivity, or the functional connectome.
paras.zh: 比较揭示了多个大脑区域活动的显着差异。一些区域表现出更大的活动，而另一些区域则表现出活动减少，从而产生了区分这两个群体的可识别模式。科学家将这些区域之间的关系称为功能连接或功能连接组。

paras.en: Using these patterns, the team developed a measurement called the Alzheimer's resilience-vulnerability connectome, or ARC score. This scoring method distinguished super agers from Alzheimer's patients with approximately 85% accuracy.
paras.zh: 利用这些模式，研究小组开发了一种称为阿尔茨海默氏症恢复力-脆弱性连接组或 ARC 评分的测量方法。这种评分方法区分超级老年人和阿尔茨海默病患者的准确率约为 85%。

paras.en: The researchers then investigated whether the same brain signature could help predict what would happen to people who had not yet developed any noticeable cognitive problems.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后调查了相同的大脑特征是否可以帮助预测尚未出现任何明显认知问题的人会发生什么。

paras.en: Predicting Alzheimer's Risk Years in Advance
paras.zh: 提前数年预测阿尔茨海默病风险

paras.en: The team applied the ARC scoring system to more than 1,300 cognitively healthy adults between the ages of 55 and 70. Their scores fell across a broad range, with lower values reflecting brain activity more similar to super agers and higher values indicating patterns closer to those observed in Alzheimer's patients.
paras.zh: 研究小组将 ARC 评分系统应用于 1,300 多名年龄在 55 岁到 70 岁之间认知健康的成年人。他们的得分范围很广，较低的值反映了与超级老年人更相似的大脑活动，较高的值表明更接近于阿尔茨海默病患者观察到的模式。

paras.en: At the beginning of the study, people with high and low ARC scores showed no obvious differences in cognitive performance. As researchers examined follow-up data collected over subsequent years, however, important differences became apparent.
paras.zh: 研究开始时，ARC分数高低的人在认知表现上没有表现出明显的差异。然而，当研究人员检查随后几年收集的后续数据时，重要的差异变得明显。

paras.en: "We used the ARC score to make a prediction of how likely this patient will convert into mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer's disease," said Kanhao (Alex) Zhao, PhD, a postdoctoral scholar in psychiatry and lead author of the study.
paras.zh: “我们使用 ARC 评分来预测该患者转化为轻度认知障碍或阿尔茨海默氏病的可能性，”精神病学博士后学者、该研究的主要作者 Kanhao（Alex）Zhao 博士说。

paras.en: The available follow-up periods differed across the datasets. Some participants had records extending as long as 12 years, although most were tracked for approximately five to six years. Even within these shorter periods, the initial ARC scores helped predict subsequent changes in cognitive abilities.
paras.zh: 不同数据集的可用随访期有所不同。一些参与者的记录长达 12 年，但大多数参与者的记录时间约为五到六年。即使在较短的时间内，最初的 ARC 分数也有助于预测随后的认知能力变化。

paras.en: People whose scores indicated more Alzheimer's-like brain activity experienced more rapid declines on standard tests of memory, attention, and executive function. In contrast, those with patterns most similar to super agers generally experienced the slowest cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 那些得分显示更多类似阿尔茨海默氏症的大脑活动的人在记忆、注意力和执行功能的标准测试中经历了更快的下降。相比之下，那些与超级老年人最相似的模式的人通常经历的认知衰退最慢。

paras.en: "We compared the ARC score with existing biomarkers in predicting people converting to Alzheimer's disease," Zhao said. "Our model shows comparable or better prediction ability, and it can do so at an earlier time point. And if we combine our score with the existing biomarkers, the prediction performance improves."
paras.zh: “我们将 ARC 评分与现有的生物标志物进行了比较，以预测人们是否会患上阿尔茨海默病，”赵说。 “我们的模型显示出可比或更好的预测能力，并且可以在更早的时间点做到这一点。如果我们将我们的分数与现有的生物标志物结合起来，预测性能就会提高。”

paras.en: The team also investigated how ARC scores related to another measure of neurological health called brain age. This measure estimates brain aging using functional MRI information collected from healthy individuals.
paras.zh: 研究小组还研究了 ARC 评分与另一种神经健康指标（即大脑年龄）的关系。这项措施使用从健康个体收集的功能性 MRI 信息来估计大脑老化。

paras.en: Although the two measurements showed some correlation, Zhang emphasized that ARC provides more targeted information about a person's vulnerability or resistance to cognitive decline during aging.
paras.zh: 尽管这两项测量显示出一些相关性，但张强调，ARC 提供了更有针对性的信息，了解一个人在衰老过程中对认知能力下降的脆弱性或抵抗力。

paras.en: "I'm excited we established a signature that can help us better understand the difference between people who can maintain excellent cognitive performance and people who show cognitive decline," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“我很高兴我们建立了一个特征，可以帮助我们更好地理解能够保持出色认知表现的人和表现出认知能力下降的人之间的差异。”

paras.en: The findings suggest that patterns of communication between brain regions may offer valuable information about future cognitive health that cannot be captured through standard memory testing alone.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，大脑区域之间的通信模式可能提供有关未来认知健康的有价值的信息，而这些信息无法仅通过标准记忆测试来捕获。

paras.en: They also raise the possibility that combining brain activity measurements with established Alzheimer's biomarkers could improve the identification of people who would benefit most from earlier monitoring or future preventive treatments.
paras.zh: 他们还提出了一种可能性，即将大脑活动测量与已建立的阿尔茨海默病生物标志物相结合，可以更好地识别哪些人将从早期监测或未来的预防性治疗中受益最多。

paras.en: Could Brain Training Help Prevent Alzheimer's?
paras.zh: 大脑训练有助于预防阿尔茨海默氏症吗？

paras.en: Despite the encouraging results, researchers caution that ARC scores are not intended to diagnose Alzheimer's disease. For now, the system should be viewed as a potential tool for tracking cognitive health and estimating future risk.
paras.zh: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，但研究人员警告说，ARC 评分并不是为了诊断阿尔茨海默病。目前，该系统应被视为跟踪认知健康和估计未来风险的潜在工具。

paras.en: Zhang also stresses that a person's score is not a permanent prediction of their future. Brain activity can change over time, and an individual who initially shows a resilient pattern may not maintain it indefinitely.
paras.zh: 张还强调，一个人的分数并不能永久预测他们的未来。大脑活动会随着时间的推移而改变，最初表现出弹性模式的人可能无法无限期地维持这种模式。

paras.en: For example, the proportion of people with super-ager-like ARC scores generally declines with advancing age. Brain injuries and neuropsychiatric conditions can also influence the patterns associated with cognitive resilience.
paras.zh: 例如，具有类似超级老年人 ARC 分数的人的比例通常随着年龄的增长而下降。脑损伤和神经精神疾病也会影响与认知弹性相关的模式。

paras.en: Importantly, this potential for change may work in both directions. If brain activity can shift toward patterns associated with vulnerability, Zhang hopes future treatments might also encourage it to move toward greater resilience.
paras.zh: 重要的是，这种变革的潜力可能是双向的。如果大脑活动能够转向与脆弱性相关的模式，张希望未来的治疗也可能会鼓励它转向更强的恢复力。

paras.en: His research team is preparing a trial that will measure ARC scores before and after cognitive training. The goal is to explore whether targeted training can influence the brain activity patterns associated with healthier cognitive aging.
paras.zh: 他的研究团队正在准备一项试验，测量认知训练前后的 ARC 分数。目标是探索有针对性的训练是否可以影响与更健康的认知衰老相关的大脑活动模式。

paras.en: "But the critical part is that we have to intervene at an early stage," he said. "That's why we focus on the cognitively unimpaired population to identify super-ager-like versus Alzheimer's-like individuals. If we can precisely identify such as early indicator, I'm optimistic that we can reverse or prevent this process through advanced intervention technologies."
paras.zh: “但关键是我们必须在早期阶段进行干预，”他说。 “这就是为什么我们专注于认知未受损的人群，以识别超级老年人与阿尔茨海默氏症样个体。如果我们能够精确识别诸如早期指标，我乐观地认为我们可以通过先进的干预技术扭转或阻止这一过程。”

paras.en: Although it remains unknown whether modifying these brain patterns can prevent or delay Alzheimer's, the discovery offers a potentially important new direction for research. By identifying differences in brain activity before symptoms emerge, scientists may eventually gain a valuable opportunity to intervene while cognitive function is still intact.
paras.zh: 尽管尚不清楚改变这些大脑模式是否可以预防或延缓阿尔茨海默病，但这一发现为研究提供了一个潜在的重要新方向。通过在症状出现之前识别大脑活动的差异，科学家最终可能获得在认知功能仍然完好的情况下进行干预的宝贵机会。

paras.en: Researchers from Children's National Hospital; the University of Texas at Austin; Lehigh University; Penn State College of Medicine; New York University Grossman School of Medicine; and the University of California, Los Angeles also participated in the research.
paras.zh: 国家儿童医院的研究人员；德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校；理海大学；宾夕法尼亚州立大学医学院；纽约大学格罗斯曼医学院；加州大学洛杉矶分校也参与了这项研究。

paras.en: Funding was provided by the National Institutes of Health (grants R21AG080425, R01MH129694 and R01AG081768), a joint Rosenkranz Foundation-Knight Initiative program, an Alzheimer's Association grant, and a Lehigh University CORE grant.
paras.zh: 资金由美国国立卫生研究院（拨款 R21AG080425、R01MH129694 和 R01AG081768）、罗森克兰茨基金会-奈特联合计划、阿尔茨海默病协会拨款和理海大学 CORE 拨款提供。

paras.en: Materials provided by Stanford Medicine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由斯坦福大学医学院提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Kanhao Zhao, Hua Xie, Gregory A. Fonzo, Nancy B. Carlisle, Tovia Jacobs, Ricardo S. Osorio, Arpana Church, Feng Vankee Lin, Yu Zhang. A functional connectome identifies vulnerability to cognitive decline and Alzheimerâs disease progression. Science Advances, 2026; 12 (45) DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aed9351

articles.title: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome

paras.en: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
paras.zh: 一种新的纤维补充剂可以帮助数百万人患有肠易激综合症

paras.en: - Scientists have developed a promising new fiber supplement that improves gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) without worsening bloating, pain, or other digestive symptoms. The specially designed blend also improved gut-related anxiety and produced surprisingly rapid changes in gut bacteria, potentially offering a new way to manage IBS.
paras.zh: - 科学家们开发出了一种很有前途的新型纤维补充剂，可以改善肠易激综合症 (IBS) 患者的肠道健康，而不会加重腹胀、疼痛或其他消化系统症状。这种专门设计的混合物还改善了与肠道相关的焦虑，并使肠道细菌产生惊人的快速变化，有可能提供一种治疗肠易激综合症的新方法。

paras.en: A specially designed fiber supplement may offer a promising new way to improve gut health for millions of people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Researchers at Edith Cowan University (ECU) have developed and tested a fiber combination that supports beneficial gut bacteria without making common digestive symptoms worse.
paras.zh: 一种专门设计的纤维补充剂可能为数百万肠易激综合症（IBS）患者提供一种改善肠道健康的有前景的新方法。埃迪斯科文大学 (ECU) 的研究人员开发并测试了一种纤维组合，它可以支持有益的肠道细菌，而不会使常见的消化症状恶化。

paras.en: The research team at ECU's Nutrition and Health Innovation Research Institute (NHIRI) found that the supplement, called ur gut®, improved gut health in people with IBS without increasing abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation.
paras.zh: ECU 营养与健康创新研究所 (NHIRI) 的研究小组发现，这种名为 ur gut® 的补充剂可以改善 IBS 患者的肠道健康，而不会增加腹痛、腹胀、腹泻或便秘。

paras.en: IBS affects people around the world, including nearly 11 percent of Australians. Although its exact cause remains unclear, stress, infections, and certain medications may contribute to the condition. Symptoms can also become worse because of particular foods, inadequate sleep, psychological stress, hormonal changes, and lifestyle factors.
paras.zh: IBS 影响世界各地的人们，其中包括近 11% 的澳大利亚人。尽管其确切原因尚不清楚，但压力、感染和某些药物可能会导致这种情况。由于特定的食物、睡眠不足、心理压力、荷尔蒙变化和生活方式因素，症状也可能变得更严重。

paras.en: Why Common IBS Diets Can Affect Gut Health
paras.zh: 为什么常见的肠易激综合症饮食会影响肠道健康

paras.en: People with IBS are frequently advised to follow a low-FODMAP diet, which limits certain carbohydrates that are easily fermented by gut bacteria. Although this approach can help control uncomfortable symptoms, restricting these foods may also have unintended consequences for the gut microbiome.
paras.zh: 肠易激综合症患者经常被建议遵循低 FODMAP 饮食，这会限制某些容易被肠道细菌发酵的碳水化合物。尽管这种方法可以帮助控制不适症状，但限制这些食物也可能对肠道微生物组产生意想不到的后果。

paras.en: "For years we've known that a diet low in Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monesaccharides and Polyols (FODMAPs) can relieve symptoms, but they can also reduce beneficial gut bacteria and negatively impact fiber intake over time," lead author Dr. Tina Yan said.
paras.zh: 主要作者 Tina Yan 博士说：“多年来，我们知道低含量可发酵低聚糖、二糖、单糖和多元醇 (FODMAP) 的饮食可以缓解症状，但随着时间的推移，它们也会减少有益的肠道细菌，并对纤维摄入量产生负面影响。”

paras.en: "We wanted to find a way to build better gut health while following a low-FODMAP diet."
paras.zh: “我们希望找到一种方法，在遵循低 FODMAP 饮食的同时，增强肠道健康。”

paras.en: The new findings suggest that a carefully formulated fiber supplement could help address this problem, allowing people with IBS to support a healthier gut microbiome while continuing to manage their symptoms through dietary changes.
paras.zh: 新的研究结果表明，精心配制的纤维补充剂可以帮助解决这个问题，让肠易激综合症患者能够支持更健康的肠道微生物组，同时继续通过饮食改变来控制症状。

paras.en: The researchers attribute the supplement's promising effects to its combination of two ingredients: resistant starch and psyllium husk.
paras.zh: 研究人员将这种补充剂的良好效果归因于其两种成分的组合：抗性淀粉和洋车前子壳。

paras.en: Psyllium appears to slow the breakdown of resistant starch by gut bacteria, allowing more of it to reach deeper sections of the colon before fermentation occurs. This process may increase the production of beneficial compounds that support intestinal health.
paras.zh: 洋车前子似乎可以减缓肠道细菌对抗性淀粉的分解，使更多的抗性淀粉在发酵发生之前到达结肠的更深部分。这个过程可能会增加支持肠道健康的有益化合物的产生。

paras.en: Ordinarily, fermentable fiber can be challenging for people with IBS because bacterial fermentation can produce excess gas and increase digestive discomfort. The new formulation appears to offer a way to obtain the benefits of fermentation without aggravating these symptoms.
paras.zh: 通常，可发酵纤维对于肠易激综合症患者来说可能具有挑战性，因为细菌发酵会产生过量气体并增加消化不适。新配方似乎提供了一种获得发酵益处而不加重这些症状的方法。

paras.en: "Traditionally, fermentable fibers can be difficult for people with IBS because they can increase gas production and discomfort," Dr. Yan said.
paras.zh: “传统上，可发酵纤维对于肠易激综合症患者来说可能很困难，因为它们会增加气体产生和不适，”严博士说。

paras.en: "What's exciting about this study is that participants maintained stable symptoms while showing meaningful improvements in their gut microbiota as well as in their gut-related anxiety."
paras.zh: “这项研究令人兴奋的是，参与者保持了稳定的症状，同时肠道菌群以及与肠道相关的焦虑也出现了有意义的改善。”

paras.en: Significant Changes in Gut Bacteria and Anxiety
paras.zh: 肠道细菌的显着变化与焦虑

paras.en: The researchers observed substantial shifts in the composition of participants' gut bacteria during the intervention. These changes were particularly notable because they occurred over a relatively short period.
paras.zh: 研究人员观察到干预期间参与者肠道细菌的组成发生了重大变化。这些变化特别引人注目，因为它们发生的时间相对较短。

paras.en: "Changes of this magnitude are rarely seen with such a short intervention," ur gut® co-creator Professor Amanda Devine said.
paras.zh: ur gut® 联合创始人阿曼达·迪瓦恩 (Amanda Devine) 教授表示：“在如此短的干预时间内，很少会出现如此大规模的变化。”

paras.en: "The study demonstrated that our targeted dietary fiber blend positively reshaped the gut microbiome in people with IBS following a low-FODMAP diet, supporting beneficial bacteria linked to gut and mental health. This was great to see."
paras.zh: “研究表明，我们的针对性膳食纤维混合物可以积极重塑采用低 FODMAP 饮食的 IBS 患者的肠道微生物群，支持与肠道和心理健康相关的有益细菌。这真是太棒了。”

paras.en: Alongside improvements in gut bacteria, participants also experienced reductions in gut-related anxiety. These findings suggest that the supplement's potential benefits may extend beyond changes in the digestive system, although further research will be needed to establish its broader effects.
paras.zh: 除了肠道细菌的改善之外，参与者还减少了与肠道相关的焦虑。这些发现表明，该补充剂的潜在益处可能不仅仅限于消化系统的改变，尽管还需要进一步的研究来确定其更广泛的影响。

paras.en: A New Approach to Managing Irritable Bowel Syndrome
paras.zh: 治疗肠易激综合症的新方法

paras.en: The researchers believe their findings could help shift IBS care toward improving the underlying health of the gut rather than focusing exclusively on avoiding foods that cause discomfort.
paras.zh: 研究人员相信，他们的发现可能有助于将肠易激综合征治疗转向改善肠道的潜在健康，而不是仅仅专注于避免引起不适的食物。

paras.en: "For many people with IBS, success has traditionally meant simply avoiding certain foods," ur gut® co-creator Associate Professor Claus Christophersen said.
paras.zh: “对于许多患有肠易激综合症的人来说，成功传统上意味着简单地避免某些食物，”ur gut® 联合创始人克劳斯·克里斯托弗森副教授说。

paras.en: "Our findings suggest we may also be able to actively rebuild gut health and the microbiome while not making IBS symptoms worse. That's an important step forward."
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果表明，我们或许还能够积极重建肠道健康和微生物组，同时不会使肠易激综合症症状恶化。这是向前迈出的重要一步。”

paras.en: By demonstrating that beneficial gut bacteria can be supported without increasing IBS symptoms, the study points toward new dietary strategies that could complement existing treatments.
paras.zh: 通过证明有益的肠道细菌可以在不增加肠易激综合症症状的情况下得到支持，该研究指出了可以补充现有治疗方法的新饮食策略。

paras.en: The ur gut® supplement is already available for purchase. The research team has also created a cookbook featuring recipes designed to help people incorporate the supplement into a healthy diet.
paras.zh: ur gut® 补充剂现已可供购买。研究团队还编写了一本食谱，其中包含旨在帮助人们将补充剂纳入健康饮食的食谱。

paras.en: The study, "Dietary fibre blend improves gut health in patients with irritable bowel syndrome following a low FODMAP diet: a randomised, double-blind control trial," was published online in the European Journal of Nutrition.
paras.zh: 该研究“膳食纤维混合物可改善低 FODMAP 饮食后肠易激综合症患者的肠道健康：一项随机、双盲对照试验”，在线发表在《欧洲营养学杂志》上。

paras.en: Materials provided by Edith Cowan University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由埃迪斯科文大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Ran Yan, Amanda Devine, Johnny Lo, Evania Marlow, Ian C. Dunican, Kanita Kunaratnam, Lesley Andrew, Claus T. Christophersen. Dietary fibre blend improves gut health in patients with irritable bowel syndrome following a low FODMAP diet: a randomised, double-blind control trial. European Journal of Nutrition, 2026; 65 (7) DOI: 10.1007/s00394-026-04113-5
paras.zh: - Ran Yan、Amanda Devine、Johnny Lo、Evania Marlow、Ian C. Dunican、Kanita Kunaratnam、Lesley Andrew、Claus T. Christophersen。膳食纤维混合物可改善低 FODMAP 饮食后肠易激综合征患者的肠道健康：一项随机、双盲对照试验。欧洲营养杂志，2026； 65 (7) DOI: 10.1007/s00394-026-04113-5

articles.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression

paras.en: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
paras.zh: 科学家发现简单的日常生活可以减少疼痛和抑郁

paras.en: - A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia. Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.
paras.zh: - 对您的日常生活进行简单的改变可能会给您的身体和精神感觉带来惊人的变化。密苏里大学的研究人员发现，遵循固定作息时间的老年人报告称，即使在失眠的情况下，身体疼痛也较少，抑郁症状也较少。保持规律的睡眠、饮食和其他活动时间可能有助于调节身体的生物钟，从而影响情绪、睡眠和整体健康。

paras.en: A consistent daily routine may do more for your health than you realize. Researchers at the University of Missouri have found that older adults who follow regular daily schedules tend to experience less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggle to get a good night's sleep.
paras.zh: 一致的日常生活对您的健康的作用可能比您想象的要大。密苏里大学的研究人员发现，遵循规律作息的老年人往往会经历更少的身体疼痛和更少的抑郁症状，即使他们很难睡个好觉。

paras.en: The findings suggest that everyday habits, such as waking up, eating meals, socializing, and going to bed at consistent times, may play an important role in physical and mental well-being. By helping the body maintain its natural internal clock, a predictable routine could offer health benefits that extend beyond improved sleep.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，日常习惯，例如起床、吃饭、社交和按时就寝，可能对身心健康发挥重要作用。通过帮助身体维持自然的生物钟，可预测的作息时间不仅可以改善睡眠，还可以带来健康益处。

paras.en: The discovery could be especially important for older adults, who frequently experience sleep difficulties. According to the National Council on Aging, roughly half of adults age 60 and older report symptoms of insomnia, a condition that can make it difficult to fall asleep, stay asleep, or get restful sleep.
paras.zh: 这一发现对于经常遇到睡眠困难的老年人来说尤其重要。根据国家老龄化委员会的数据，大约一半 60 岁及以上的成年人有失眠症状，这种症状会让人难以入睡、保持睡眠或获得安宁的睡眠。

paras.en: Daily Routines Linked to Less Pain and Depression
paras.zh: 日常活动有助于减少疼痛和抑郁

paras.en: To investigate the relationship between sleep, daily habits, and overall health, Eunjin Tracy, an assistant professor in the College of Education and Human Development at the University of Missouri, examined survey responses from 67 older adults. Among the participants, 37 reported experiencing insomnia.
paras.zh: 为了调查睡眠、日常习惯和整体健康之间的关系，密苏里大学教育与人类发展学院助理教授 Eunjin Tracy 检查了 67 名老年人的调查回复。在参与者中，有 37 人表示患有失眠症。

paras.en: As researchers expected, those with insomnia generally reported more physical pain and higher levels of depression than participants without the condition. However, another pattern emerged when Tracy examined their daily routines.
paras.zh: 正如研究人员预期的那样，失眠者通常比没有失眠症的参与者报告更多的身体疼痛和更高程度的抑郁。然而，当特雷西检查他们的日常生活时，出现了另一种模式。

paras.en: Participants who maintained more consistent schedules tended to report less pain and fewer depressive symptoms, regardless of their sleep quality. This suggests that keeping regular daily habits may be associated with better health even when sleep problems persist.
paras.zh: 无论睡眠质量如何，保持更一致作息时间的参与者往往会报告较少的疼痛和抑郁症状。这表明，即使睡眠问题持续存在，保持规律的日常习惯也可能与更好的健康有关。

paras.en: "Regardless of sleep quality, those who reported having a regular daily routine had lower levels of physical pain and less depression compared to those without a daily routine," Tracy said. "If we are consistent with when we wake up, eat, work or study, interact with others and go to bed, those time cues help synchronize our internal body clocks. Over the long term, that seems to be linked with improved health outcomes."
paras.zh: 特雷西说：“无论睡眠质量如何，那些自称有规律作息的人与那些没有作息规律的人相比，身体疼痛程度较低，抑郁程度也较低。” “如果我们在起床、吃饭、工作或学习、与他人互动和上床睡觉的时间保持一致，这些时间线索有助于同步我们的内部生物钟。从长远来看，这似乎与改善健康状况有关。”

paras.en: One possible explanation involves the circadian rhythm, the body's natural 24-hour timing system. This internal clock helps coordinate when we feel awake or sleepy and influences numerous biological processes, including hormone activity, metabolism, and mood.
paras.zh: 一种可能的解释涉及昼夜节律，即人体自然的 24 小时计时系统。这种内部时钟有助于协调我们何时感到清醒或困倦，并影响许多生物过程，包括激素活动、新陈代谢和情绪。

paras.en: Rather than operating independently of our surroundings, the circadian system responds to signals that help it keep time. Light and darkness are especially important, but regular activities such as eating, working, interacting with others, and sleeping can also provide timing cues.
paras.zh: 昼夜节律系统不是独立于周围环境而运作，而是对有助于其保持时间的信号做出反应。光明和黑暗尤其重要，但饮食、工作、与他人互动和睡眠等常规活动也可以提供时间线索。

paras.en: When these signals follow a predictable pattern, they help keep the body's biological rhythms aligned. Irregular schedules, on the other hand, can interfere with that coordination.
paras.zh: 当这些信号遵循可预测的模式时，它们有助于保持身体的生物节律一致。另一方面，不规则的日程安排可能会干扰这种协调。

paras.en: "When we regulate our circadian rhythm well, our bodies function well, but if it gets too distracted, our bodies don't function as well," Tracy said.
paras.zh: 特雷西说：“当我们很好地调节昼夜节律时，我们的身体机能就会很好，但如果过于分散，我们的身体机能就不会那么好。”

paras.en: Although the study did not establish that regular routines directly reduce pain or depression, the findings point to circadian regulation as one possible explanation for the connection.
paras.zh: 尽管该研究并未证实规律作息可以直接减轻疼痛或抑郁，但研究结果表明昼夜节律调节是这种联系的一种可能解释。

paras.en: Even relatively small changes in daily schedules may disrupt the body's internal clock. One common example is social jet lag, which occurs when a person's sleep schedule shifts between workdays and days off.
paras.zh: 即使日程安排中相对较小的变化也可能会扰乱人体的生物钟。一个常见的例子是社交时差，当一个人的睡眠时间表在工作日和休息日之间变化时就会发生这种情况。

paras.en: Someone who wakes up early throughout the week but stays up late and sleeps in on weekends may experience this mismatch. The resulting disruption resembles some of the effects of traveling across time zones, even though the person has never left home.
paras.zh: 一周中早起但周末熬夜并睡懒觉的人可能会经历这种不匹配。由此产生的干扰类似于跨时区旅行的一些影响，即使这个人从未离开过家。

paras.en: Tracy suggests that maintaining reasonably consistent schedules throughout the entire week, including weekends, may help limit these disruptions and support healthier circadian rhythms.
paras.zh: 特雷西建议，在整个星期（包括周末）保持合理一致的时间表可能有助于限制这些干扰并支持更健康的昼夜节律。

paras.en: "As someone who wakes up and goes to bed at the same time every day, I think a daily routine can be helpful for people of all ages across their lifespan," Tracy said. "There is growing awareness about the concept of social jet lag -- waking up and going to bed at different times on weekends compared to weekdays -- and the disruptions it causes to our circadian rhythm, so hopefully this research helps more people consider the health benefits of a daily routine. Since one-third of our lives will be spent sleeping, I think health and well-being research should be looked at holistically from a 24-hour perspective and not just focus on when we are awake."
paras.zh: 特雷西说：“作为一个每天在同一时间起床和睡觉的人，我认为日常生活对各个年龄段的人在一生中都有帮助。” “人们越来越意识到社会时差的概念——周末与工作日的不同时间起床和睡觉——以及它对我们的昼夜节律造成的干扰，因此希望这项研究能够帮助更多的人考虑日常生活对健康的益处。由于我们一生中有三分之一的时间是在睡眠中度过的，我认为健康和福祉研究应该从 24 小时的角度全面审视，而不仅仅是关注我们醒着的时间。”

paras.en: A Simple Habit With Potential Health Benefits
paras.zh: 一个具有潜在健康益处的简单习惯

paras.en: The research highlights an aspect of healthy living that can be easy to overlook. While getting enough quality sleep remains important, the consistency of activities throughout the day may also be connected to how people feel physically and emotionally.
paras.zh: 这项研究强调了健康生活中很容易被忽视的一个方面。虽然获得充足的优质睡眠仍然很重要，但全天活动的一致性也可能与人们的身体和情感感受有关。

paras.en: Because the study relied on survey data from a relatively small group of older adults, it cannot prove that adopting a regular routine will relieve pain or depression. Larger studies would be needed to establish whether changing daily schedules directly improves these outcomes.
paras.zh: 由于该研究依赖于相对较小的老年人群体的调查数据，因此它不能证明采取规律的生活习惯可以缓解疼痛或抑郁。需要进行更大规模的研究来确定改变日常安排是否可以直接改善这些结果。

paras.en: Still, the findings suggest that a predictable daily routine may be a useful component of a broader approach to health, particularly for people experiencing insomnia.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，研究结果表明，可预测的日常生活可能是更广泛的健康方法的有用组成部分，特别是对于失眠的人来说。

paras.en: For older adults and potentially people of other ages, simple habits such as maintaining regular waking times, eating meals on a consistent schedule, and limiting major changes in weekend sleep patterns may help support the body's natural rhythms.
paras.zh: 对于老年人和其他年龄段的人来说，保持规律的起床时间、按时吃饭以及限制周末睡眠模式的重大变化等简单的习惯可能有助于支持身体的自然节律。

paras.en: The study, "Behavioral-social rhythms and insomnia symptoms: associations with pain, body mass index, and depressive symptoms among older adults," was published in the Journal of Behavioral Medicine.
paras.zh: 该研究题为“行为社会节律和失眠症状：老年人中与疼痛、体重指数和抑郁症状的关联”，发表在《行为医学杂志》上。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Missouri-Columbia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由密苏里大学哥伦比亚分校提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Eunjin Lee Tracy, Christine J. So, Brian Chin, Yuxi Xie, H. Matthew Lehrer, Jill A. Kanaley, Brant P. Hasler, Daniel J. Buysse. Behavioral-social rhythms and insomnia symptoms: associations with pain, body mass index, and depressive symptoms among older adults. Journal of Behavioral Medicine, 2026; 49 (3): 551 DOI: 10.1007/s10865-026-00646-6
paras.zh: - Eunjin Lee Tracy、Christine J. So、Brian Chin、Yuxi Xie、H. Matthew Lehrer、Jill A. Kanaley、Brant P. Hasler、Daniel J. Buysse。行为社会节律和失眠症状：与老年人疼痛、体重指数和抑郁症状的关联。行为医学杂志，2026； 49 (3): 551 DOI: 10.1007/s10865-026-00646-6

articles.title: Why did Starship Flight 15 booster abort 'chopsticks' landing catch? SpaceX still investigating (video)
articles.author: Tariq Malik

paras.en: SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster.
paras.zh: SpaceX 正在调查其最新的 Starship 巨型火箭试飞为何错过了周五（11 月 13 日）两次计划着陆中的第一次，并引发自动中止并摧毁了助推器。

paras.en: The giant Starship rocket, a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight. The goal: To land both the Super Heavy first stage and the Ship upper stage, for the first full Starship recovery — and the first complete recovery of an orbital launch system in history.
paras.zh: 周五，在该公司雄心勃勃的 Flight 15 试飞中，巨型两级运载火箭 Starship 火箭是地球上最大的运载火箭，从位于德克萨斯州南部的 SpaceX Starbase 升入轨道。目标：使超重型第一级和飞船上级着陆，实现首次完整的星舰回收，也是历史上首次完整回收轨道发射系统。

paras.en: The Super Heavy stage, called Booster 22, came back to Earth mere minutes after liftoff as planned. Instead of returning to its launch tower to be caught mid-air by the tower's metal "chopstick" arms, however, the rocket veered offshore and detonated its flight termination system. SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot initially said that a guidance issue appeared to be the cause.
paras.zh: 被称为“Booster 22”的超重型火箭按计划在升空几分钟后就返回了地球。然而，火箭并没有返回发射塔，在半空中被发射塔的金属“筷子”臂抓住，而是转向离岸并引爆了其飞行终止系统。 SpaceX 发言人 Dan Huot 最初表示，原因似乎是制导问题。

paras.en: Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon.
paras.zh: 星舰压铸火箭模型在亚马逊上原价 47.99 美元，现价 39.99 美元。

paras.en: Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g.
paras.zh: 即使您无法亲眼目睹 SpaceX 的星际飞船，您也可以获得自己的模型。高度为 13.77 英寸（35 厘米），这是 SpaceX 星际飞船桌面模型的 1:375 比例。这里的材料是合金钢，重量仅为225克。

paras.en: "We were initially 'go' for a catch," Huot said during live commentary on Friday, about seven hours into the mission. "But in the later stages of the coast, the booster aborted itself for a GNC issue that it detected, and that put it into its contingency landing offshore." Super Heavy exploded a few feet above the waves of the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after liftoff.
paras.zh: “我们最初是‘去’抓鱼的，”霍特在周五的现场评论中说，此时任务已经进行了大约七个小时。 “但在海岸的后期阶段，助推器由于检测到 GNC 问题而自行中止，这使其进入了海上应急着陆阶段。”升空后约 6.5 分钟，“超级重型”在墨西哥湾海浪上方几英尺处爆炸。

paras.en: GNC is short for Guidance and Navigation Control, a criticial system used by rockets to control their flight and ensure they remain on their planned course. Such a system is vital for any landing attempt by a Starship Super Heavy or Ship upper stage to ensure the vehicle returns to its landing site safely and doesn't veer off course to damage SpaceX's Starbase or surrounding populated areas.
paras.zh: GNC 是制导和导航控制的缩写，是火箭用来控制飞行并确保其保持在计划航线上的关键系统。这样的系统对于 Starship Super Heavy 或 Ship 上级的任何着陆尝试都至关重要，以确保车辆安全返回着陆点，并且不会偏离航线而损坏 SpaceX 的 Starbase 或周围的人口稠密地区。

paras.en: In an update during SpaceX's Flight 15 coverage on Saturday, however, Huot said that Super Heavy's GNC system actually performed well.
paras.zh: 然而，在周六 SpaceX 的 Flight 15 报道期间的更新中，Huot 表示 Super Heavy 的 GNC 系统实际上表现良好。

paras.en: "I did a disservice to our booster GNC guys last night," Huot said. "It was not a GNC issue that caused us not to come back. GNC triggered that abort; it was doing what it was supposed to do. Basically, [it] detected that the booster was not in the place that it was supposed to be to proceed with a catch, did an automated abort and then headed out to that offshore splashdown location."
paras.zh: “昨晚我伤害了我们的 GNC 助推者，”霍特说。 “导致我们没有回来的不是 GNC 问题。GNC 触发了中止；它正在做它应该做的事情。基本上，[它]检测到助推器不在应该进行捕获的位置，进行了自动中止，然后前往离岸溅落地点。”

paras.en: SpaceX is "still digging into the root cause on how we got there, and so, more to come on that," he added on Saturday.
paras.zh: 他周六补充道，SpaceX“仍在深入研究我们如何达到这一目标的根本原因，因此，还会有更多的工作要做”。

paras.en: You can follow our Starship Flight 15 live updates for the latest on the mission.
paras.zh: 您可以关注我们的 Starship Flight 15 实时更新，了解该任务的最新信息。

paras.en: Super Heavy is powered by a cluster of 33 Raptor rocket engines that fire simultaneously during liftoff to send the 41-story Starship megarocket into orbit. During Friday's launch, all 33 engines fired as planned for the ascent, Huot said.
paras.zh: Super Heavy 由一组 33 个猛禽火箭发动机提供动力，这些发动机在升空时同时点火，将 41 层的 Starship 巨型火箭送入轨道。霍特说，在周五的发射过程中，所有 33 台发动机都按计划点火启动。

paras.en: One engine did drop out after stage separation, when Super Heavy dropped away from Ship and flipped over for a "boostback" burn to begin its trip back to Earth, Huot said on Friday.
paras.zh: 霍特周五表示，当超重型从飞船上坠落并翻转进行“助推”燃烧以开始返回地球时，一台发动机确实在级分离后脱落。

paras.en: "We had 32 out of the 33 booster engines lit for boostback, which started sending it back here to the launch site," he added.
paras.zh: “我们在 33 个助推发动机中点燃了 32 个进行助推，开始将其送回发射场，”他补充道。

paras.en: That firing was followed by the booster's landing burn. In SpaceX's launch video, Super Heavy can be seen activating 13 of its Raptor engines as planned, followed by the abort and the booster steering itself to a contingency landing zone in Gulf waters.
paras.zh: 那次发射之后，助推器着陆燃烧。在 SpaceX 的发射视频中，可以看到 Super Heavy 按计划启动了 13 个猛禽发动机，随后中止，助推器自行转向海湾水域的应急着陆区。

paras.en: "It did that hover, cut the engines off, the FTS — the flight termination system — triggered, and it splashed down in the water," Huot said on Friday. (The FTS is designed to destroy a booster in the event of an emergency.)
paras.zh: 霍特周五表示：“它悬停了，关闭了发动机，触发了 FTS（飞行终止系统），然后飞机溅入水中。” （FTS 的设计目的是在紧急情况下摧毁助推器。）

paras.en: As its name suggests, Starship Flight 15 is SpaceX's 15th test flight of the giant rocket, but it will be the first to attempt to catch a Ship upper stage with the chopsticks. SpaceX has successfully caught Super Heavy boosters on three test flights to date.
paras.zh: 顾名思义，Starship Flight 15 是 SpaceX 巨型火箭的第 15 次试飞，但这将是第一次尝试用筷子抓住飞船上级。迄今为止，SpaceX 已经在三次试飞中成功捕获了超重型助推器。

paras.en: Flight 15's Ship vehicle is in good health and will orbit Earth a total of 14 times before landing back at its launch pad in Starbase at around 4:20 p.m. EST (1920 GMT) today, if all goes well.
paras.zh: 15 号航班的飞船运行状况良好，将绕地球飞行 14 圈，然后于下午 4 点 20 分左右返回 Starbase 的发射台。如果一切顺利的话，今天美国东部时间（1920 GMT）。

paras.en: "Our heat shield team reviewed all the data we got from our ground-tracking cameras, and from those satellite cameras and confirmed the heat shield is in a good posture for a reentry and return to the launch site," Huot said in Friday's mission update. (Flight 15 hauled 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites to orbit, and a few of those spacecraft carried cameras for heat-shield inspection.)
paras.zh: 霍特在周五的任务更新中说：“我们的隔热罩团队审查了从地面跟踪摄像机和卫星摄像机获得的所有数据，并确认隔热罩处于重新进入并返回发射场的良好状态。” （15 号航班将 26 颗 SpaceX 的下一代 Starlink V3 卫星送入轨道，其中一些航天器携带了用于隔热罩检查的摄像机。）

paras.en: SpaceX designed Starship to be fully reusable, with the company banking on that reusability to make it an affordable heavy-lift booster capable of a wide range of missions to low Earth orbit, the moon and eventually Mars.
paras.zh: SpaceX 设计的 Starship 是完全可重复使用的，该公司依靠这种可重复使用性使其成为负担得起的重型助推器，能够执行近地轨道、月球和最终火星的各种任务。

paras.en: NASA has picked Starship as one of two commercial landers to carry Artemis astronauts to the moon in 2028, and SpaceX sees the rocket as vital to building out a 100,000 constellation of Starlink V3 internet satellites, as well as a new AI data center network in orbit called Starmind.
paras.zh: NASA 已选择 Starship 作为 2028 年将 Artemis 宇航员送上月球的两艘商业着陆器之一，而 SpaceX 认为该火箭对于构建由 10 万颗 Starlink V3 互联网卫星组成的星座以及名为 Starmind 的新轨道人工智能数据中心网络至关重要。

paras.en: But first, SpaceX has to successfully land a Starship upper stage from orbit. That's the next step for Flight 15.
paras.zh: 但首先，SpaceX 必须成功地将星际飞船上级从轨道着陆。这是 15 号航班的下一步。

paras.en: Huot said that flight controllers will make one last check at the 20-hour mark in the mission to decide whether to proceed with the landing at Starbase or make an "early return" splashdown off the coast of Hawaii.
paras.zh: 霍特表示，飞行控制人员将在任务进行到 20 小时时进行最后一次检查，以决定是继续在 Starbase 着陆还是在夏威夷海岸“提前返回”。

paras.en: That final check is expected by about 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT). Space.com's Starship Flight 15 landing livestream will begin at that time, and will be carried on our live updates page, Space.com homepage and our VideoFromSpace YouTube page.
paras.zh: 最终检查预计在下午 2 点左右进行。美国东部时间（1900 GMT）。 Space.com 的 Starship Flight 15 着陆直播将在那时开始，并将在我们的实时更新页面、Space.com 主页和我们的 VideoFromSpace YouTube 页面上进行。

paras.en: Editor's note: This story was updated at 11:50 a.m. ET on Nov. 14 with the latest information from SpaceX's Dan Huot, who clarified that the booster tower-catch abort was not caused by a GNC issue.
paras.zh: 编者注：本文于美国东部时间 11 月 14 日上午 11:50 更新，包含 SpaceX 的 Dan Huot 的最新信息，他澄清助推器塔卡住中止并非由 GNC 问题引起。

paras.en: Tariq is the award-winning Editor-in-Chief of Space.com and joined the team in 2001. He covers human spaceflight, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Editor-in-Chief in 2019. Before joining Space.com, Tariq was a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra, Fullerton and Huntington Beach. He's a recipient of the 2022 Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting and the 2025 Space Pioneer Award from the National Space Society. He is an Eagle Scout and Space Camp alum with journalism degrees from the USC and NYU. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.
paras.zh: Tariq 是 Space.com 屡获殊荣的主编，于 2001 年加入该团队。他负责载人航天以及天空观测和娱乐。他于 2019 年成为 Space.com 的主编。在加入 Space.com 之前，塔里克是《洛杉矶时报》的特约记者，报道拉哈布拉、富勒顿和亨廷顿海滩的教育和城市动态。他因其在太空报道方面的卓越表现而荣获 2022 年哈利·科尔库姆奖和国家航天协会颁发的 2025 年太空先锋奖。他是鹰童子军和太空营的校友，拥有南加州大学和纽约大学的新闻学学位。您可以在 Space.com 上找到塔里克，他也是 TWiT 网络上本周太空播客的联合主持人。要查看他的最新项目，您可以在 Twitter 上关注 Tariq @tariqjmalik。

paras.zh: 评论前您必须确认您的公开显示名称

articles.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
articles.author: Fran Ruiz

paras.en: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games, and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel.
paras.zh: 第一代《异形：火力小队精英》是我最喜欢的异形电子游戏之一，有很多理由对续集感到兴奋。

paras.en: At Summer Game Fest 2026, we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong?
paras.zh: 在 2026 年夏季游戏节上，我们了解到了公式的许多巧妙变化和改进，我渴望再次寻找错误。新的战役、完全重新设计的职业以及四人合作模式。可能会出什么问题？

paras.en: Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.
paras.zh: 几个月后，《异形：火力小队 2》的首次亮相遇到了困难，主要是由于明显的技术问题。尽管如此，对于近年来一直致力于让异形再次变得可怕的系列来说，这仍然是一个值得欢迎的动作震动。

paras.en: Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2's pure survival horror to look forward to.
paras.zh: 《异形：罗穆卢斯》（2024）和《异形：地球》（2025）将酸血异形重新塑造为真正的恐怖偶像，而《异形：黑暗后裔》等游戏则押注于紧张的实时战术和小队管理； 《Rogue Incursion》让 VR 和非 VR 玩家都感到害怕；我们甚至还有《隔离 2》的纯粹生存恐怖值得期待。

paras.en: Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason.
paras.zh: 抛开粗糙的一面不谈，《异形：火力小组精英 2》是对无意识射击的必要回归，并将异形视为无情的部落，放弃了跟踪和血腥的谋杀，转而采用科幻枪战和男子气概的俏皮话。这远不是一个新颖的想法——即使最初的游戏也只有五年的历史——但它成为经典是有原因的。

paras.en: Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat.
paras.zh: 不管你相信与否，《Fireteam Elite 2》中的另一个殖民地已成为异形的猎物。熟悉的设置将一支新的殖民海军陆战队带到了 LV-558 上的采矿设施，在那里与第一波前往应对威胁的海军陆战队员失去了联系。

paras.en: This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running.
paras.zh: 这不是第一次接触，而是第一次接触。海军陆战队现在已经习惯了寻找虫子，这意味着在进入异种爆破混乱之前需要进行的说明会减少。写作当然不会让学院感到震惊（任务之间肯定有太多的写作），但这里的敏捷性值得赞赏。我们之前已经和这些外星人战斗过很多很多次了。 Fireteam Elite 2 足够聪明，可以避开虚假的紧张气氛并立即开始运行。

paras.en: All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode.
paras.zh: 所有的设计变更和升级都强化了制作终极外星人动作游戏的意图。职业有更明确的角色，可以使用更好、更具破坏性的科幻武器，当外星人和敌对合成人不断涌入时，升级到四人火力小队是受欢迎的。厌倦了在更高的难度和修改器下重玩战役任务？在这款射击游戏的经典部落模式中，做好最坏的打算。

paras.en: At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away.
paras.zh: 《异形：火力小队精英 2》充分诠释了为什么詹姆斯·卡梅隆的杰作至今仍经久不衰。在最大的异形攻击期间——当子弹飞舞、酸液喷洒时——游戏的缺点和卡顿元素就会消失。

paras.en: There are still some scares hiding in here, though, ready to make complacent players jump out of their seats. Special Xenomorphs have tricks to pounce on distracted players, throwing chaos into the middle of their carefully coordinated rain of fire. Others have the ability to spit from afar, breaking tight defenses that count on the Xenos' predictable tactics from other games and the movies.
paras.zh: 不过，这里仍然隐藏着一些恐惧，准备让自满的玩家从座位上跳起来。特殊的异形有一些技巧可以扑向分心的玩家，在他们精心协调的火雨中制造混乱。其他人则有能力从远处吐口水，打破依赖异形在其他游戏和电影中可预测的战术的严密防御。

paras.en: It's been 40 years since Aliens first graced the big screen, but Fireteam Elite 2 manages to refresh that mix of horror and action well enough, despite sharing much of its bones with the original game. But the disturbing lack of polish threatens to undo Cold Iron Studios' best ideas.
paras.zh: 自《异形》首次登上大银幕以来，已有 40 年的历史，但《火力小队 2》成功地刷新了恐怖与动作的融合，尽管它与原版游戏有很多共同之处。但令人不安的是，冷铁工作室的最佳创意可能会因为缺乏完善而被毁掉。

paras.en: Those ideas include more varied enemies, which can disrupt almost any tried-and-tested team composition, and even a late-game class that rewards an extensive knowledge of the game by letting veterans pick weapons from all over the roster to create a custom loadout.
paras.zh: 这些想法包括更多样化的敌人，这几乎可以破坏任何经过考验的团队组成，甚至包括游戏后期课程，通过让退伍军人从名单上的所有武器中挑选武器来创建自定义装备，奖励对游戏的广泛了解。

paras.en: These playful creative swings somewhat offset the frustration caused by glitched objectives, enemy AI that often goes off the rails, and performance issues that have often given me flashbacks to its predecessor's worst moments on PS4. Sometimes, you can just tell when six extra months would've done a game a lot of good, and it's obvious that Fireteam Elite 2 will be in a much better place by spring.
paras.zh: 这些有趣的创意波动在一定程度上抵消了由于目标故障、敌人人工智能经常脱轨以及性能问题而造成的挫败感，这些性能问题经常让我回想起前作在 PS4 上最糟糕的时刻。有时，你可以看出，额外六个月的时间会让游戏变得更加出色，而且很明显，《Fireteam Elite 2》到了春天将会变得更好。

paras.en: That said, its loose and confident approach to design is rare to see when dealing with games that adapt well-established IPs like Alien.
paras.zh: 也就是说，在处理采用《异形》等成熟 IP 的游戏时，其宽松而自信的设计方法是很少见的。

paras.en: Recent Star Wars games have achieved just that, and even if Fireteam Elite 2 misses some of its shots and has faced more initial trouble than the USCM's first incursion on LV-426, it's safe to say its heart and mind are in the right place. No one can take that away from the devs. Show me another modern Alien video game that allows you to zap Xenomorphs to death with a big cannon or to hold them off with combat drones.
paras.zh: 最近的《星球大战》游戏就做到了这一点，即使《Fireteam Elite 2》错过了一些镜头，并且比 USCM 第一次入侵 LV-426 时遇到了更多的麻烦，但可以肯定地说它的心和思想是正确的。没有人可以从开发者手中夺走这一点。给我展示另一款现代的外星人视频游戏，它可以让你用大炮将异形杀死，或者用战斗无人机阻止它们。

paras.en: We've seen developers win uphill battles before, and we know for a fact the huge Alien fandom is as enduring as the deadly extraterrestrials, so Daybreak and Cold Iron have a chance to turn things around and solidify Fireteam Elite 2 as the iterative but satisfying sequel it actually is.
paras.zh: 我们以前见过开发商赢得艰苦的战斗，而且我们知道，庞大的《异形》粉丝群体和致命的外星人一样经久不衰，因此《黎明》和《冷铁》有机会扭转局面，巩固《火力小队 2》作为迭代但令人满意的续作的地位。

paras.en: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is available now for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. A Nintendo Switch 2 version is coming in 2027.
paras.zh: 《异形：火力小队精英 2》现已推出 PS5、Xbox Series X|S 和 PC 版本。 Nintendo Switch 2 版本将于 2027 年推出。

paras.en: Fran Ruiz is our resident Star Wars guy. His hunger for movies and TV series is only matched by his love for video games. He got a BA of English Studies, focusing on English Literature, from the University of Malaga, in Spain, as well as a Master's Degree in English Studies, Multilingual and Intercultural Communication. On top of writing features and other longform articles for Space.com since 2021, he is a frequent collaborator of VG247 and other gaming sites. He also serves as associate editor over at Star Wars News Net and its sister site, Movie News Net.
paras.zh: 弗兰·鲁伊斯是我们的星球大战常驻人员。他对电影和电视剧的渴望与他对电子游戏的热爱相匹配。他在西班牙马拉加大学获得英语研究学士学位，主修英国文学，以及英语研究、多语言和跨文化交流硕士学位。自 2021 年以来，他除了为 Space.com 撰写专题文章和其他长篇文章外，还经常与 VG247 和其他游戏网站合作。他还担任星球大战新闻网及其姊妹网站电影新闻网的副编辑。
